stories.title: PM meets NDA MPs over breakfast, raises concern over Parliament disruptions
Yogi asks if Rahul, Akhilesh are educated:‘Their statements make me laugh’; warns, ‘Those who rob youths of jobs will go to hell’
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath on Tuesday questioned the education of Congress leader Rahul Gandhi and Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav during an event in Sant Kabir Nagar. He said, ‘Rahul ji and Akhilesh Yadav ji, I do not know whether you are educated or not. Sometimes, the things you say are so ridiculous that they put you in the dock.’ Yogi accused the Congress and Samajwadi Party of spreading propaganda and questioned their record in government. He said people in Purvanchal had died from disease, including children from poor families, while the previous governments remained silent. The Chief Minister said that as an MP, he had fought against encephalitis “from the streets to Parliament” and claimed that the region is now free of the disease. He also assured young people that they would get jobs without corruption. During the time of the SP and Congress, the jobs of young people were robbed. But now, if anyone tries to interfere with the youth’s jobs, we will send them to hell. Here are seven major points from Yogi Adityanath’s speech- 1. ‘The belief that dying in Maghar leads to hell was a misconception’ Yogi said Sant Kabir Das had spoken out against hypocrisy and attempts to create deep divisions in society in the name of caste. He said Kabir came to Maghar specifically to challenge such hypocrisy. A misconception had been spread that anyone who died in Maghar would go to hell. According to Yogi, heaven and hell depend on a person’s deeds. If someone does good and virtuous work, he said, they can attain heaven anywhere. The double-engine government has constructed the Kabir Academy in Maghar and is advancing research related to Sant Kabir, he said. 2. ‘SP-Congress had no interest in building medical colleges’ Yogi questioned Rahul Gandhi and Akhilesh Yadav over the development of education and healthcare infrastructure. He said that before 2014, during the Congress era, there were only 16 IITs in the country, compared with 23 today. The number of IIMs has increased from 13 to 22. He said there were previously no Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana centres, whereas 600 are now operating. According to Yogi, the number of AIIMS has risen from seven before 2014 to 23 today. Medical colleges have increased from 431 to 818, while MBBS seats have risen from 51,348 to 1,28,926. He said postgraduate medical seats have increased from 31,185 to 85,822. Yogi also claimed that total employment generated after 1947 has risen from 47 crore to 64.33 crore and that the number of start-ups has increased from fewer than 500 to more than 2.23 lakh. He questioned how children could have secured medical college admissions when previous governments had shown little interest in building medical colleges. 3. ‘Muslims do not even want to touch Kabir’ Yogi alleged that the previous governments did not believe in the teachings of Sant Kabir. He said Hindus worship Sant Kabir, while Muslims ‘do not even want to touch him’. A development authority will soon be established in Sant Kabir Nagar, he said, adding that the process is already underway. 4. ‘Both disease and mafia are now being eliminated’ Yogi recalled that during July and August, mothers in Purvanchal used to fear for their children because of the threat of encephalitis. He said the Congress and Samajwadi Party governments, despite governing Uttar Pradesh four times, failed to address the disease effectively. His government, he claimed, has now eradicated it. Yogi accused the SP and Congress of turning Uttar Pradesh into a ‘Bimaru’ (sick) state, with young people, farmers and other sections of society suffering as a result. He said the state is now eliminating both disease and mafia. 5. ‘Money is now being spent on corridors’ Yogi said funds were available in the past as well, but alleged that they were spent on the boundary walls of graveyards. Today, he said, the same money is being used to construct the Tameshwarnath Corridor. An auditorium has also been built in Sant Kabir’s name, while Tameshwarnath Dham is being developed as a corridor. Yogi said the Baijnath Dham temple collapsed in the rain a few days ago and that proposals have now been invited for its development. 6. Khalilabad-Bahraich railway line brings development Yogi said 95,000 houses have been provided in urban and rural areas of Sant Kabir Nagar under the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana. He also said 3.5 lakh toilets have been provided in the district. The Khalilabad-Bahraich railway line, he said, is opening a new chapter in the district’s development. 7. ‘SP-Congress did not care about the poor’ Yogi said poor people did not receive ration under previous governments, whereas everyone is now getting ration. He said Uttar Pradesh now has a long chain of medical colleges and that the Sant Kabir Nagar Medical College has been constructed. Calling Sant Kabir Nagar “like our courtyard”, Yogi said he had regularly visited the district in the past and continues to do so. He assured people that the district would not be allowed to fall behind in development.

stories.title: CM says Purvanchal transforms from ‘mafia-mosquito’ to medical hub:‘One District One Product,’ not ‘One District One Mafia,’ defines its identity
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath on Tuesday targeted the Opposition at a news channel’s ‘Changing Eastern Uttar Pradesh’ conclave at the Baba Gambhirnath Auditorium in Gorakhpur. Yogi said Eastern Uttar Pradesh was once associated with “mafias and mosquitoes”, but neither can be found today. He said ‘One District One Product’ has replaced ‘One District One Mafia’, highlighting changes in law and order, healthcare, connectivity, investment and employment. ‘Youth should not be linked with unemployment or backwardness’ Yogi said it was wrong to associate Purvanchal’s youth with backwardness, unemployment or drug addiction. He said young people now have opportunities in education, employment, self-employment, industry and entrepreneurship. He argued that if young talent could not be utilised earlier, the problem was with the system rather than the youth. Once opportunities and platforms were provided, young people demonstrated their capabilities and contributed to the region’s economic growth. Yogi also said Purvanchal’s youth are increasingly moving towards businesses and start-ups rather than relying solely on jobs, which is generating employment and boosting economic activity. Kashi and Ayodhya driving religious tourism Targeting previous governments, Yogi said those who ruled for long in the name of Mahatma Gandhi had not done enough to implement Gandhi’s vision. He recalled Gandhi’s 1916 visit to Kashi Vishwanath Temple, where he reportedly expressed displeasure over the narrow lanes and poor cleanliness. Yogi said the temple complex has since been transformed into the grand Kashi Vishwanath Dham under Prime Minister Narendra Modi. He said the development of Kashi Vishwanath Dham and the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Temple in Ayodhya has boosted religious tourism. Hotels, restaurants, taxis, flower sellers, markets, boat operators and other local businesses are benefiting from increased tourist spending. From encephalitis to a healthcare hub Yogi said Purvanchal was previously known for mosquito-borne diseases and encephalitis, while the mafia created law-and-order problems. He said he had raised the issue of encephalitis from the streets to Parliament as an MP and that his government later introduced measures to control the disease. He claimed the region is now effectively tackling encephalitis, dengue, kala-azar, chikungunya and malaria. Gorakhpur, he said, has transformed from a city associated with disease into a healthcare hub. Super-speciality facilities have expanded at BRD Medical College, while AIIMS has also been established. Medical colleges have also been opened in several districts, including Kushinagar, Deoria, Maharajganj, Siddharthnagar, Basti, Balrampur, Bahraich, Gonda, Sultanpur, Pratapgarh, Ghazipur, Mau, Azamgarh, Chandauli, Sonbhadra, Mirzapur and Ambedkarnagar. Investment and employment rise Yogi said improved law and order and better road, rail and air connectivity have encouraged investment from entrepreneurs in other states. He claimed investments in Gorakhpur over the past nine years have created employment for nearly 50,000 young people. He also cited the reopening of the Gorakhpur fertiliser factory, Pipraich and Munderwa sugar mills, a spinning mill and the Khajani blanket factory. He said improved local opportunities have also reduced the need for young people from Purvanchal to migrate to other states for work. Faster connectivity boosts Purvanchal The Chief Minister said the journey from Gorakhpur to Lucknow now takes around three hours, compared with eight hours earlier. Gorakhpur to Varanasi can now be covered in about two-and-a-half hours. He added that Gorakhpur’s air connectivity has improved significantly. While flights were infrequent around a decade ago, 14 flights now operate from the city, with strong demand. Target of a $1 trillion UP economy Yogi claimed that Uttar Pradesh’s economy and per capita income have increased approximately threefold over the past nine years. He said the government aims to move Uttar Pradesh towards a $1 trillion economy within the next three years, which will require balanced development across Purvanchal, Western UP, the Central region and Bundelkhand. He said a developed India requires a developed Uttar Pradesh and described the region’s youth as Purvanchal’s biggest strength. With the right opportunities in education, employment, self-employment and entrepreneurship, he said, young people will drive the region’s next phase of development and prosperity.

stories.title: 19-year-old girl murdered in Noida PG:B.Tech graduate hid body in room; stench exposed crime after 2 days
stories.summary: A B.Tech pass youth murdered a girl from Assam, who was living in a Paying Guest (PG) in Noida. After this, he hid her body in his room. Then he locked the room from outside and fled from there. Two days later, when a foul smell came from the room, the landlord informed the police. The police, who arrived at the scene, broke open the room's lock and found the girl's body inside. Her body had been attacked multiple times with a sharp weapon. According to the police, the 19-year-old girl was living with her friend. Meanwhile, the accused youth is a resident of Bihar. He has worked in an IT company but is currently unemployed. He was also living on rent in a room near the girl's. On August 9, the girl had an argument with the youth. The incident took place on August 10 in Barola village, Sector-49 police station area, but the police revealed it today (Tuesday). The girl had come to Noida without informing her family Mahak Ahmed (19), originally from Dibrugarh, Assam, had studied up to 12th grade. About three weeks ago, she had come to Noida without informing her parents. Here, she was living in a PG located in Barola village with her friend Sanjana. Sanjana is also from Assam. She is 18 years old. She has not yet completed her 12th grade studies. Both girls lived on the first floor of a three-story building and worked in a call center. On the same floor was also the room of Raman, who is from Katihar, Bihar. The accused has a B.Tech degree, used to work in an IT company On August 8, Sanjana went out for two days for some work. At night, Mahak was walking in the lobby outside the room. During this time, Raman was sitting outside his room, drinking alcohol. An argument broke out between the two over something. When Sanjana returned on August 10, Mahak was not found in the room. She tried to contact Mahak, but her mobile was switched off. Despite extensive searching, she could not be traced. A few hours later, the residents of the house started smelling a foul odor from Raman's room. The room was locked from the outside, and Raman was not there. As the smell intensified, the tenants became suspicious. They informed the landlord, Sarthak Bansal, about this. Police opened the lock and found Mehak's dead body The landlord informed Dial-112 around 12 PM on August 10. The police team reached the spot, had the room's lock opened, and entered. Inside the room, Mehak's body was found lying in a bloody state. There were injury marks at several places on her body. It seemed as if the girl had been attacked multiple times with a sharp weapon. Forensic team collected evidence, mobile also sent for investigation Police sent the body for post-mortem. The forensic team that arrived at the scene inspected the room and its surroundings. Police have also sent Mahak's mobile phone for investigation. Call details, chats, and other activities are being investigated to ascertain who Mahak was in contact with before the incident. Along with this, the police are also questioning other residents of the house. Along with the search for the accused Raman, aspects related to his activities and the dispute with Mahak are also being investigated.

stories.title: Ram Mandir CEO interviews underway:Former encounter specialist IPS officer, ex-Ayodhya DM in race; 5,300 applied, 18 shortlisted, 3 to be finalised
stories.summary: Interviews are underway to appoint the Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of the Ayodhya Ram Mandir. Eighteen candidates have been called for the four-day interview process. On Tuesday, the first day of interviews, former IPS officer Rajesh Pandey, known as an encounter specialist, and former Ayodhya District Magistrate Yogeshwar Ram Mishra appeared for the interview. According to sources, each candidate’s interview is lastingfor 15-20 mins. Questions such as ‘Where have you worked?’, ‘How much faith do you have in Lord Ram?’ and ‘Who are the members of your family?’ are being asked. More than 5,300 people applied for the CEO post, but only 18 were shortlisted. Apart from former IPS officer Rajesh Pandey and former Ayodhya DM Yogeshwar Ram Mishra, the names of the other 15 candidates have not been disclosed. Retired Justice Pramod Kohli, former scientist Dr Suresh Hawade and retired Lieutenant General Vishnukant Chaturvedi are conducting the interviews. Three candidates will be shortlisted from the 18. The Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust will then interview these three candidates and select the final CEO. First, know about the former officers who appeared for interviews today 5,300 applications scrutinised using 34 questions Amid the controversy over the alleged theft of Ram Mandir donations, the trust invited applications for the CEO post from July 13 to 18. Applicants were required to answer 34 questions through an online Google Form. Based on their responses, the team scrutinised more than 5,300 applications and found 18 candidates eligible for the post. They were subsequently called for interviews. Key conditions set for applicants Age limit: Applicants had to be between 50 and 70 years old. Tenure: The CEO will initially be appointed for three years. The tenure may be extended based on performance. Experience: Applicants must have at least 20 years of experience in areas such as general administration, finance and accounts, human resources, public relations, information technology, security and law. Applicants asked whether they were ‘staunch’ or ‘devout’ Hindus The Google Form sought personal details including the applicant’s name, date of birth, age, address, city, state, PIN code, mobile number and email address. Applicants were also asked about their ability to understand Hindi and English, highest educational qualification, current employment or retirement status, and previous organisation. Applicants were asked how many employees they had led, with options ranging from 1,000 to more than 5,000 employees. They were also asked whether they had previously been associated with any social or religious organisation, monastery or temple. Those who answered yes were asked to provide details of how many years they had been associated with such an organisation. Applicants also had to state whether they considered themselves a staunch Hindu or a devout Hindu. They were further asked to provide their vision, action plan and suggestions for the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra.

stories.title: 'RSS plotting to end reservation', says Mayawati:Congress-SP hijacked student protests, BJP doing the same in Ranchi
stories.summary: BSP supremo Mayawati on Tuesday targeted the BJP, Congress and Samajwadi Party over reservation and student-youth movements. She alleged that reservation for Dalits, tribals and other backward classes in government jobs is becoming almost ineffective, while RSS workers are trying to weaken it further. Mayawati said the public sector is being weakened while the private sector is being continuously promoted. As a result, poor and unemployed sections are falling further behind, while big capitalists and wealthy individuals are becoming stronger. She said the BSP is not against the private sector, but there should also be a reservation system in private-sector jobs similar to the one in government employment. Mayawati claimed that when the BSP was in power, it had introduced a system of providing reservation even in industries established with government support. ‘Conspiracy to make Dalits, tribals and OBCs helpless again’ The BSP chief alleged that an internal understanding between the ruling party and the Opposition was behind a conspiracy to make Dalits, tribals and backward classes ‘slaves and helpless’ again. Appealing to these communities to remain vigilant and cautious, she urged them to join the BSP to protect their interests and bring the party to power. Mayawati said that under BSP governments, no section of society faced discrimination or partiality. She claimed that all sections were given due attention at the political, economic and social levels. ‘Congress-SP hijacked CJP’s movement’ Mayawati also referred to the CJP movement held at Jantar Mantar in Delhi over paper leaks and unemployment. She said the movement, which concerns the problems of students, youth and Gen-Z, raises serious issues and that the BSP has always stood with students and young people. She alleged that the Congress and its allied parties had hijacked the CJP movement and that Parliament is now also unable to function under its guise. Mayawati said students and young people should certainly protest to get their problems resolved, but should not become pawns in the hands of political parties. ‘BJP and allies infiltrated Ranchi student protest’ Mayawati said that, like the protest at Jantar Mantar in Delhi, students and young people in Ranchi, the capital of Jharkhand, are also protesting over their problems. She said the Congress and its supporting parties are not openly speaking about the Ranchi protest, while the BJP and its allies are now coming forward to raise the students’ concerns. She said it appears that the BJP and its supporting parties have also hijacked the movement. According to Mayawati, more politics than solutions to students’ and young people’s problems can be seen behind both the Delhi and Ranchi movements. She said political parties lack seriousness about resolving these problems, while narrow politics driven by electoral self-interest dominates. Mayawati urges Gen-Z to stay away from political conspiracies The BSP chief appealed to students, young people and Gen-Z across the country to stay away from what she described as conspiracies by the ruling party and the Opposition. She said young people should use political parties carefully to address their problems, but should not allow either the ruling party or the Opposition to exploit their issues to serve narrow political interests. ‘BSP governments provided jobs to millions of young people’ Referring to her four terms as Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister, Mayawati said the BSP had never disappointed students and young people. She said her governments resolved students’ problems promptly and paid special attention to the ‘livelihood’ of young people. New employment opportunities were created in both the government and private sectors. Mayawati said her government lifted the long-standing ban on government recruitment, creating employment opportunities for millions of people. New government posts were also created in the police and other departments. She said that today, after completing their studies and training, students and young people are seeking employment, but governments at both the Centre and in the states are unable to meet this demand. This, she said, has led to tremendous anger among the youth. Appeals for support in UP, Uttarakhand and Punjab Mayawati said Assembly elections are due in Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand and Punjab. She appealed to people from all sections of society to strengthen and support the BSP. She said strengthening the BSP is necessary so that students, young people, Dalits, tribals, backward classes, Muslims and other religious minorities, farmers, labourers, traders, employees and other hardworking sections can lead prosperous lives. Mayawati said the BSP had governed Uttar Pradesh four times on the principle of ‘Sarvajan Hitay, Sarvajan Sukhay’, for the welfare of all, for the happiness of all, and worked for all sections of society without discrimination.

stories.title: Varanasi airport runway defect, 3 flights diverted:Delhi flight sent to Ayodhya; Ahmedabad and Navi Mumbai flights diverted to Lucknow
stories.summary: A sudden defect developed on the runway at Lal Bahadur Shastri International Airport in Varanasi on Tuesday afternoon. Airport authorities immediately began repair work, and air traffic was suspended from 1 pm to 3 pm as a safety precaution. During this period, three flights bound for Varanasi were diverted to other airports, while three others were held at their respective departure airports. After being informed about the runway defect, senior airport officials held a meeting and decided to suspend flight operations. IndiGo flight 6E 5025, which had arrived from Delhi, was diverted to Ayodhya. The aircraft had reportedly reached Varanasi airspace and was sent to Ayodhya after circling for some time. Ahmedabad and Navi Mumbai flights diverted to Lucknow IndiGo flight 6E 6805, travelling from Ahmedabad to Varanasi, was diverted to Lucknow. Similarly, IndiGo flight 6E 2442, arriving from Navi Mumbai, was also diverted to Lucknow. Meanwhile, three flights scheduled to arrive in Varanasi from Ayodhya, Delhi and Lucknow were held at their respective departure airports. The diversions caused considerable inconvenience to passengers. People who had arrived at Varanasi Airport to receive passengers were also seen waiting anxiously. Many passengers kept checking their flight status at airline counters, while others sought updates from airport officials and relatives over the phone. Airport Director says repairs will take two hours Airport Director Puneet Gupta said a defect had been detected on the runway and repair work was started immediately. He said aircraft movements had been suspended from 1 pm to 3 pm because of the repair work, which was expected to take around two hours. Flight operations would resume once the repairs were completed.

stories.title: Teacher beaten to death in front of 6-year-old daughter:Pickup rams scooter in Lalitpur; attackers beat him with sticks and smash his head with stone
stories.summary: A teacher of an inter-college in Lalitpur, UP, was beaten to death. The teacher was returning from school with his 6-year-old daughter. The accused hit their scooter with a pickup truck. The teacher and his daughter fell on the road. As the teacher moved forward to pick up his daughter, the accused repeatedly attacked him with a stick and then smashed a stone on his head. Assuming the teacher was dead, the accused fled. Nearby people took both to the hospital. The teacher died during treatment. The incident took place on Monday at 3 PM in the Kachnauda police station area. The wife accused her brother-in-law's family members of murder. She said, "My brother-in-law committed suicide by jumping into a well at his in-laws' house, and since then, his family members held a grudge against my husband." Abhay Lodhi (30) was a teacher at a private inter-college. Abhay was married to a girl named Rajni (27) seven years ago. They have a 6-year-old daughter, Bhagyashree. Wife said - The accused also beat their daughter Abhay Lodhi was a resident of Jharkon village. His wife Rajni said that on Monday, Abhay was returning home on a scooter with his daughter Bhagyashree at 3 PM after teaching at school. Meanwhile, near Garhaghat petrol pump, a pickup truck hit his scooter from behind. Due to the collision, Abhay's scooter went out of control and fell. Both father and daughter fell on the road. After this, the accused brutally beat the husband. When daughter Bhagyashree started screaming, the accused also hit her. When nearby people saw this, they reached the spot. By then, the accused fled from there. People informed the police about the incident. Police, who arrived at the scene, sent Abhay and his daughter to the district hospital. Seeing Abhay's serious condition, doctors referred him to Jhansi. Abhay died during treatment at 1 AM on Monday-Tuesday night. The daughter is still undergoing treatment at Lalitpur Medical College. Brother-in-law's family held a grudge against the husband The wife said - My husband's sister, Manisha, was married to Ramkumar, a resident of Serai, in 2022. Manisha and her husband both lived with us in Lalitpur. On April 10, 2023, Ramkumar left home after assaulting his wife under the influence of alcohol. He committed suicide by jumping into a well. After this, Ramkumar's brother filed an FIR accusing my husband and me of murder and throwing the body into the well. The police investigation also revealed that it was a suicide. Since then, Ramkumar's family held a grudge against Abhay. Relatives beat him to death CO Sadar Ajay Kumar said that Injured Abhay Singh died during treatment in Jhansi. The investigation of the incident revealed that both parties are relatives. Abhay Singh was assaulted by his brother-in-law's family members. An FIR has been registered against 6 named individuals. The accused are being searched for.

stories.title: Akhilesh, Priyanka place donation box outside Parliament:Chant ‘Who looted the funds?’; BJP hits back, ‘They only know how to shout’
stories.summary: Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav staged a protest with party MPs in the Parliament complex on Tuesday over the alleged theft of donations made to the Ram Mandir. Congress MP Priyanka Gandhi was also seen alongside Akhilesh during the protest. Opposition MPs waved posters reading, ‘Doodh ka doodh, paani ka paani’, calling for the truth to be brought to light. Amid the rain, SP MPs staged the protest with a donation box placed in the Parliament complex. The box was decorated with flowers and garlands and had a lock on it. A note reading 'Missing' was pasted on the box. A poster below it read- ‘The government must tell us where the mandir donations have gone.’ During the protest, SP MP Dimple Yadav put money into the donation box. As she turned to leave, Firozabad MP Akshay Yadav said- We will have to keep it safe, otherwise the BJP people might snatch this money. Congress MPs then joined the protest. Carrying posters that read “Who looted the donations?”, they raised slogans against the government. NDA MPs march against Opposition Meanwhile, NDA MPs also held a protest march against the Opposition. BJP MPs arrived carrying posters and accused Congress MP Rahul Gandhi of avoiding a discussion on the ‘Gen-Z’ protests in Delhi. They also questioned Rahul Gandhi’s silence over the lathi-charge on students in Jharkhand on Monday. Arun Govil hits back at Opposition BJP MP Arun Govil hit back at the Opposition, saying: Now that we have come to give answers, they do not want a discussion. The Opposition is behaving irresponsibly to a degree I have never seen before. This Opposition is extremely irresponsible; they do not want to discuss any issue. stories.title: 'She fought her father for him, but he killed her':Mother says, 'Daughter loved her husband'; govt teacher hacked wife to death with a machete
stories.summary: ‘Nine years ago, my daughter fought with her father to marry the man she loved. We agreed for her happiness, never imagining he would become her killer. My daughter loved Dilip deeply. After marriage, she never stayed with me even for a single day. The three brothers who killed my daughter should be sentenced to death.’ These are the words of Phoolmati, the mother of Shalini, who was allegedly murdered by her husband, government teacher Dilip Kumar Yadav, who attacked her with a billhook. The post-mortem report lists drowning as Shalini’s cause of death, while seven deep wounds were found on her body. When the Dainik Bhaskar team reached Shalini’s maternal home in Fatehpur, her mother spoke of her grief and anger. Family moved from village to live near daughter Jakni village is 9 km from Fatehpur district headquarters and is Shalini’s maternal home. The family now lives in a rented house in Jairam Nagar locality of the city. Her father Dharam Singh Yadav, mother Phoolmati, younger brother Abhishek Yadav and younger sister Mansi live there. After Shalini’s death, several relatives and acquaintances were also present at the house. We spoke to Shalini’s mother, Phoolmati. Met in college, relationship lasted four years Phoolmati says Dilip studied in the city, where Shalini also attended college. The two began talking and remained in contact over the phone for four years. After Shalini completed her studies, the family found a suitable match for her and finalised her engagement. Daughter persuaded family to accept Dilip When Shalini was told about the proposed marriage, she refused. She then told her father about Dilip and insisted on marrying him. She also introduced his family to her parents. After meeting Dilip’s family, they found them suitable and agreed to the marriage for their daughter’s happiness. Started teaching after son's birth On December 3, 2017, Shalini and Dilip were married in a grand ceremony at a guesthouse. After the wedding, they lived in a rented house in Nasirpeer locality. Two years later, their son Darshit was born. Dilip was an assistant teacher at Chak Ali in Bahua block. Later, Shalini also began teaching at a private school. Grandson mostly stayed with maternal grandparents Phoolmati says the family also moved from the village and rented a house 2 km from Shalini and Dilip’s home. As both Shalini and Dilip went to work, their son Darshit mostly stayed with his maternal grandparents. “For some time, Shalini seemed quite disturbed. She loved Dilip very much. Whenever she came to our house, she would eat and immediately return to her own home. She never stayed with us for even a single day after her marriage,” Phoolmati says. “The man she chose and fought with her father to marry eventually killed her.” Dilip said Shalini had drowned in bathtub At 7 am on August 7 (Friday), Dilip called Shalini’s family and said she had fallen into a bathtub and been injured. He said they were taking her to the district hospital. However, when the family reached the house, Shalini’s body was lying on the floor and the bathtub was empty. Dilip was sitting in a nearby room. House cleaned and Shalini's clothes changed Phoolmati says blood was coming from the back of Shalini’s head when they touched it. When police arrived, Dilip claimed that Shalini had fallen down the stairs. However, there were no visible blood splatters in the house. The entire house had been washed with water, and Shalini’s clothes had also been changed. While searching the house, the family found clothes stained with Shalini’s blood. Phoolmati questions why Dilip would destroy evidence if he was not responsible for the murder. She also asks why he did not take Shalini to hospital or inform the police for three hours. She believes Dilip could not have carried out everything alone and alleges that his two brothers also helped him. “Just as these people killed my daughter, all three should be hanged,” she says. Brother says police were called over a ‘snake’ Shalini’s younger brother Abhishek says, “On Friday, I received a call from my sister. She told me to go home because a snake had appeared there. When I reached the house, my brother-in-law was leaving on his bike. He did not speak to us.” Abhishek searched the entire house but found no snake. “Later that night, my sister told me that Jija had called Dial-112 and reported seeing a snake. The police also found nothing. It seems he had already been preparing to mislead everyone,” he says. Dilip was first a postmaster, later became teacher Dileep Yadav initially worked as a postmaster in Andipur village of Asothar. He later got a government job on compassionate grounds following his father’s death. In 2019, he became a government teacher. His younger brother Sandeep Yadav is posted at the Asothar BRC, while his third brother, Bhupendra Yadav, is a teacher in Sirathu, Kaushambi district. Claimed he went for walk, CCTV showed different route SP Abhimanyu Manglik says Dilip did not take the route he claimed to have used during his morning walk. Dilip told police that he left home for a walk at 5:30 am and returned at 6:30 am. He claimed that after returning, he found his wife half-submerged in a bathtub filled with water. Police checked CCTV footage from the surrounding area but did not find Dilip on the route he mentioned. Instead, he was seen travelling on a different route on his bike. Seven deep wounds found on Shalini's body The post-mortem report found seven wounds on Shalini’s body. Three deep wounds were on the back of her head, while four were on other parts of her body. The wounds measured between half an inch and one-and-a-quarter inches. The report lists drowning as the cause of death. Police suspect Shalini was first attacked with a sharp weapon and was later drowned in a bathtub filled with water, possibly because the attacker feared she was still alive. Police have registered a case against Dilip and his two brothers. Dilip was arrested on the day of the incident but has not yet confessed to the murder. stories.title: Father dies in Kashi, mother-son die by suicide:Maharashtra family consumes poison after Baba Vishwanath darshan
stories.summary: A businessman from Maharashtra died after falling seriously ill during a family trip to Varanasi. Hours after his funeral, his wife and son allegedly consumed poison in their hotel room and died. The family had travelled to Kashi to visit religious sites. Police said the businessman had been suffering from a serious illness for a long time and had not found relief despite treatment and medication. The family reached Varanasi on August 7 and visited the Kashi Vishwanath Temple. Two days later, on Sunday night, the businessman’s health suddenly deteriorated. His family took him to hospital, where doctors declared him dead. His wife and son performed his last rites at Harishchandra Ghat on Monday. They returned to their hotel later that evening. Police found their bodies in the room after hotel staff alerted them. Family had come to Kashi for pilgrimage Vishal Mukherjee, 56, from Raigad in Maharashtra, had travelled to Varanasi with his wife Jaya Mukherjee, 51, and son Ishan Mukherjee, 26. The three were involved in their family business. According to police, Vishal had been suffering from a serious illness for a long time. He had received treatment in several cities, including Nagpur, Mumbai and Delhi, but his condition did not improve significantly. He then expressed a wish to visit religious places with his family. The family had visited several pilgrimage sites over the past three months. Visited Kashi Vishwanath and watched Ganga Aarti Vishal wanted to visit the Kashi Vishwanath Temple during Sawan, so his son Ishan booked their tickets. The three left Mumbai's Lokmanya Tilak Terminus on August 5 and reached Kashi on the morning of August 7. They checked into a homestay in the Laksa police station area and planned to stay for four days. They visited the Kashi Vishwanath Temple on the first day. The following day, they watched the Ganga Aarti and visited several ghats. Father's health deteriorated on August 9 Vishal suddenly fell ill in the hotel room on Sunday evening, August 9. With the help of hotel staff, his family took him to the BHU Trauma Centre. Doctors declared him dead during treatment. Ishan informed their relatives about the death. With their consent, Vishal's last rites were performed at Harishchandra Ghat on Monday. After the funeral, Jaya and Ishan returned to the hotel. Police find traces of poison in room The mother and son did not leave their room until Monday evening. Hotel staff tried to contact them through the intercom and by knocking on the door, but received no response. The hotel staff then informed the Laksa police. Police opened the room and found Jaya and Ishan dead inside. During the initial investigation, traces of aluminium phosphide, commonly known as Sulphos, were found in the room. A forensic team was called to the scene and collected evidence. Police investigating all angles ADCP Vaibhav Bangar said police reached the hotel after receiving information from the staff. The initial investigation suggested that Jaya and Ishan may have consumed poison following the shock of Vishal's death. However, police are investigating all possible angles. The bodies have been sent for post-mortem examination. Further action will be taken based on the post-mortem report and forensic findings. The incident took place under the jurisdiction of the Laksa police station in Varanasi.

stories.title: ‘We’re not non-performers,’ says Lucknow-Kanpur Expressway builder PNC:Shares plunge 19%; did NHAI give wrong info?
stories.summary: Shares of PNC Infratech, the company that built the Lucknow-Kanpur Expressway, have fallen sharply after the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) said it had started proceedings to declare the company a ‘non-performer’. On August 5, NHAI said action was being initiated against PNC Infratech. The company’s share price stood at ₹260.24 at the time. Its shares have since fallen by around 19% in four days. PNC Infratech has now written a three-page letter to the BSE and NSE, saying it has neither been blacklisted nor declared a non-performer. The company said only a show-cause notice had been issued and that its subsidiary, Awadh Expressway Private Limited, was responding to it. This has raised questions over whether NHAI’s announcement referred to an ongoing process rather than a final decision, or whether PNC Infratech is presenting the matter differently to reassure investors. How accurate are PNC Infratech’s claims? Company says 300 metres of road was damaged In its August 6 letter to the BSE and NSE, PNC Infratech said parts of the expressway had been damaged because of continuous heavy rain. The company claimed that around 300 metres of the road had been affected, accounting for less than 0.5% of the expressway’s total length. However, the report says around 600-700 metres of the 63-km expressway has developed stretches of subsidence at different locations. These sections are being dug up and rebuilt. On the 45-km stretch between Unnao and Lucknow, the report claims that damaged or sunken sections can be found roughly every 2 km. In total, problems have reportedly been identified at 84 locations. Company blames rain; technical inspection points to construction quality PNC Infratech attributed the damage to heavy rainfall. However, according to the report, NHAI’s technical inspection found that poor construction quality and problems with the laying and settling of the asphalt layer contributed to the deterioration. Company does not mention possible non-performer status PNC Infratech has said that NHAI has neither blacklisted it nor declared it a non-performer. It maintains that it has only received a show-cause notice. However, on August 5, NHAI Regional Officer Gautam Vishal said official proceedings had begun to declare the company a non-performer. NHAI has also removed four officials from the project over alleged lapses in road construction. They include construction agency project manager Vivek Kumar Gupta, independent engineer team leader Surendra Kumar, resident engineer Yatendra Kumar and current project director Nakul Prakash Verma. Repairs have also reportedly failed PNC Infratech said severely damaged sections had been repaired immediately and work was progressing rapidly at other locations. Under the contract, the company is responsible for maintaining the expressway for 15 years after its construction. However, the report claims that some of the patchwork carried out to repair earlier defects has itself started coming apart. Over the past 24 hours, 14 new locations on the Lucknow-Kanpur Expressway have reportedly developed road subsidence. Experts cited in the report said construction quality had been inadequate and that repair work was also being carried out in haste, potentially worsening the problem. A recent video reportedly showed workers using a fan to dry the road during repair work. Company could bid again after two years An NHAI official said there are different rules governing restrictions on companies. If poor construction quality is established, a company can be blacklisted for one to two years, depending on the circumstances. After the restriction ends, the company can participate in tender processes again. It can also secure a contract if it meets the applicable eligibility requirements. Latest condition of expressway Over the past two days, 14 new locations on the Lucknow-Kanpur Expressway have reportedly developed problems including road subsidence, damaged drains and waterlogging. Near Rawal village, a hole measuring around 6 feet long and 4 feet deep has appeared alongside the divider. Three new patches have been laid on the Unnao-Lucknow carriageway. Patchwork is also under way along around 100 metres of the road at kilometre 39.7. The road has also deteriorated near Israel Kheda on the Lucknow-Unnao carriageway. IIT Kharagpur team completes inspection Engineers from IIT Kharagpur have completed their inspection of the expressway. Professor KS Reddy is expected to submit the team’s report to NHAI headquarters within 12 days. The inspection included videography of the affected sections. Investigators also recorded questioning of PNC Infratech and NHAI officials. The team is also examining whether PNC Infratech made any changes to the original design of the expressway. The findings of the IIT Kharagpur report are expected to provide further clarity on whether the damage was primarily caused by heavy rainfall or whether construction and design-related issues contributed to the deterioration.

stories.title: MLA’s ‘conman’ son-in-law duped 44 women:Targeted divorced, widowed women; posed as his son’s brother before marriage
stories.summary: A father-son duo from Sitapur allegedly conned 44 women of around ₹100 crore after marrying them or promising to marry them, according to police complaints and statements by victims. Anuj Trivedi and his son Prakhar allegedly targeted mostly women over 40, including widows, divorcees and women with disabilities. To gain their trust, Anuj allegedly introduced Prakhar as his younger brother. The case came to light after BJP MLA from Sevta in Sitapur, Gyan Tiwari, filed an FIR against his son-in-law Prakhar and his father Anuj. The MLA alleged that his MBBS-qualified daughter was also a victim of the alleged fraud. How the alleged ‘groom gang’ came to light Anuj and Prakhar, residents of Chandrawal village in Sitapur, allegedly carried out the fraud between 2016 and 2022 across Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra, Delhi, Kolkata and Karnataka. The case first came to light on March 4, 2022, when 75-year-old Sarita (name changed) filed a complaint at Nayanagar police station in Thane. She said she had placed a newspaper matrimonial for her 45-year-old daughter Shubhangi, who was Manglik. Anuj allegedly contacted her using the name ‘Ajay Agarwal’ and claimed to be a builder from Kolkata. Shubhangi married him on March 1, 2019. According to Sarita, Anuj took Shubhangi to Delhi on February 22, 2022, where he allegedly removed her 39 tolas of gold and diamond jewellery. He then put her on a train to Mumbai and switched off his phone. Complaints from Ranjita (name changed) in Amravati and Leela Pratap Nair in Mumbai later emerged. After four FIRs were registered in Maharashtra, the investigation was handed over to the Mumbai Crime Branch. Seven women describe how they were allegedly trapped Anuj allegedly arranged four marriages for Prakhar in Mumbai and cheated the women of crores of rupees. On February 14, 2024, Prakhar married Pragya Tiwari, daughter of BJP MLA Gyan Tiwari from Sevta. Pragya is an MBBS doctor and the couple also have a son. After the family allegedly discovered the truth about Anuj and Prakhar, Gyan Tiwari and his daughter cut ties with them. On August 8, the MLA filed an FIR against both men. 1. Pragya: ‘Prakhar approached me at the gym’ Prakhar allegedly targeted Pragya at the gym she attended. He started visiting the same gym and, according to her family, used an expensive car to create an impression of wealth. He gradually became acquainted with Pragya and later proposed marriage. Pragya told her father about the proposal. Gyan Tiwari said he made enquiries about the family and was told that they were well-established and ran a real-estate business in Mumbai. Anuj had allegedly built a similar reputation in his village. He had opened a school in Prakhar’s name and built a roughly 6,000-square-foot house in Krishna Vihar, near Chhath Mile on the Sitapur Road. 2. Shubhangi: 455 grams of jewellery allegedly taken Shubhangi's mother Sarita had placed a matrimonial in 2018 because her daughter was Manglik and was finding it difficult to get married. Anuj allegedly responded using the name Ajay Agarwal and claimed to be a Kolkata-based builder. He later married Shubhangi and stayed in her three-bedroom flat during the Covid period. He allegedly assaulted her and pressured her family into selling the flat. According to the complaint, he took ₹82 lakh, including the proceeds from the sale. On February 22, he allegedly took Shubhangi to Delhi on the pretext of attending the wedding of his ‘younger brother’ Prakhar. There, he allegedly removed 455 grams of gold jewellery she was wearing. Shubhangi reportedly had a serious leg injury at the time. Her family alleged that she was kept without food before being put on a train to Mumbai. Her family is now facing financial difficulties. Her 82-year-old father still has to work in a private job, according to the family. 3. Pratima: Teacher allegedly loses ₹11 lakh and jewellery Pratima (name changed), a teacher from Jhunsi in Prayagraj, also came into contact with Anuj. She alleged that he took ₹11 lakh and 50 grams of jewellery from her. Pratima said she first met him in 2017. 4. Geeta: Fake marriage certificate allegedly used Geeta, a divorcee, created a profile on a matrimonial website at her mother's suggestion. Anuj allegedly contacted her in 2017 using the name Ajay Agarwal. He introduced his son Prakhar as his younger brother, ‘Aviral’. He later gave Geeta a marriage certificate dated August 27, 2018. She subsequently discovered that the certificate was allegedly fake. After the marriage, Anuj allegedly took ₹25.90 lakh and 400 grams of gold jewellery from Geeta, claiming he needed the money to complete a building project in Kolkata. He also allegedly pressured her to sell a house worth ₹35 lakh for just ₹9 lakh. Geeta became suspicious after she saw another woman, Vinita, in a mirror during a video call with Anuj. She later went to Bandra court to verify the marriage documents and allegedly discovered that the certificate was fake. She subsequently filed an FIR at Amravati police station. 5. Rachna: Anuj allegedly claimed his wife had died Rachna's husband died of cancer in 2012. She placed a matrimonial in 2016 and came into contact with Anuj. He allegedly claimed to be a widower and said his wife, Maya Singh, had died of cancer. Rachna alleged that he took ₹8 lakh, a mobile phone, a diamond ring and a gold chain from her. She later became suspicious and travelled to Mumbai in September 2018. An investigation allegedly revealed that Maya Singh was alive and that Anuj had sold her flat and taken her to Lucknow. When Rachna threatened to approach the police, Anuj allegedly threatened to circulate her photographs. Maharashtra Police recently recorded her statement. 6. Leela Nair: ₹54 lakh flat sale and 950 grams of gold Leela Nair lived alone in Mumbai while her children were settled abroad. Anuj allegedly came into contact with her in 2015-16 and gradually gained her trust. He eventually became her caretaker. Claiming to be a prominent Mumbai builder, he allegedly arranged the sale of her flat for ₹54 lakh and kept the entire amount. He also allegedly took 950 grams of her gold jewellery before disappearing. Leela later filed a case against him at Borivali police station. 7. Mahua: Engagement allegedly followed by fraud In 2016, Anuj allegedly approached a woman named Mahua in Kolkata with a marriage proposal. The two became engaged. He allegedly took money and jewellery from her before fleeing. Mahua and around 15 other women who were allegedly targeted have since married elsewhere and do not want to come forward because of concerns about social stigma. However, the Mumbai Crime Branch has so far recorded statements from 25 alleged victims. Investigation reveals alleged first wife was alive While checking Anuj's claims, Geeta reportedly went to his Bandra flat. The security guard allegedly recognised Anuj and told her that he had married a woman named Maya Singh in 2016. Maya, who reportedly weighed around 150 kg and used a wheelchair, allegedly had her Bandra flat sold by Anuj after their marriage. The property was reportedly sold for ₹2.82 crore. Anuj then allegedly took Maya to Lucknow and kept her in a house in Gomti Nagar. Father arrested, son still missing The Mumbai Crime Branch arrested Anuj in Noida on May 24, 2026. During questioning, he allegedly admitted to marrying around 40 women across several states. Police said his son Prakhar had also married four women in Mumbai and Kolkata. Prakhar is still being searched for. Anuj is currently lodged in Amravati Central Jail. Three FIRs have been registered against him in Maharashtra and one in Kolkata. On August 8, Sitapur BJP MLA Gyan Tiwari also filed an FIR against Anuj and Prakhar, alleging that his daughter was among their victims.

stories.title: Is making, selling analogue paneer not a crime in UP?:Gujarat, Maharashtra ban it; why is it still sold here, what are the rules?
stories.summary: Chhattisgarh, Maharashtra and Gujarat have recently banned the production and sale of analogue, or ‘fake’, paneer. However, making and selling it is not a criminal offence in Uttar Pradesh and several other states, provided consumers are clearly told that it is not made from milk. It is also different from adulterated paneer, which is made using harmful substances and sold as genuine milk-based paneer. So, why is making and selling analogue paneer not a crime in Uttar Pradesh? How is it different from adulterated paneer? What are the rules governing its sale? Here is everything you need to know. Q1. What is the difference between analogue and adulterated paneer? Answer: Analogue paneer is designed to resemble traditional milk-based paneer. It is generally made using ingredients such as milk powder, vegetable oil, potato or corn starch, soya protein and food additives. When made according to prescribed standards, it does not involve the use of harmful chemicals and is not banned in Uttar Pradesh. Adulterated paneer, on the other hand, may be made using substances such as detergent, urea and caustic chemicals. It is also sold by passing it off as genuine milk-based paneer. Such practices are illegal and are treated as a non-bailable offence in Uttar Pradesh. When analogue paneer is sold, the consumer must be clearly informed that it is not made from milk. It is also generally cheaper than conventional paneer. In simple terms, there are two categories: Q2. Is analogue paneer completely safe to eat? Answer: Not necessarily. Occasional consumption may not cause immediate problems, but concerns have been raised about the effects of consuming products high in unhealthy fats and additives regularly. 1. Risk of heart disease Analogue paneer may contain significant amounts of vegetable fats, including palm oil, to give it a texture similar to traditional paneer. A diet high in unhealthy fats can raise levels of bad cholesterol and triglycerides, increasing the risk of heart disease and other cardiovascular problems. 2. Liver and digestive problems Some analogue paneer products contain vegetable fats and large amounts of starch or other thickening agents. Regular consumption of foods high in unhealthy fats can contribute to weight gain and metabolic problems, while excessive starch intake may cause digestive discomfort such as bloating, gas and constipation in some people. 3. Concerns over long-term consumption Some products may also contain preservatives and other food additives to increase their shelf life. However, the health impact depends on the ingredients used, their quantities and how frequently the product is consumed. It is therefore misleading to assume that all analogue paneer products carry the same health risks. 4. Weight gain and lower nutritional value People who eat paneer as part of a weight-loss or fitness diet may not get the same nutritional benefits from an analogue product. Traditional paneer is a source of protein and calcium. Depending on how it is made, an analogue product may contain substantially less protein and calcium while containing more vegetable fat and carbohydrates. Q3. If it can be unhealthy, why is making and selling it not a crime? Answer: In Uttar Pradesh, the sale of analogue paneer that meets food-safety standards is not, by itself, prohibited. There are several legal and technical reasons for this. 1. Its ingredients are not illegal substances Food products can be banned when they contain substances that are unsafe for human consumption. However, ingredients commonly used in analogue paneer, such as vegetable oils, corn starch and skimmed milk powder, are permitted food ingredients when used within prescribed limits. Similar ingredients are also used in products such as biscuits, savoury snacks, chips and chocolates. Therefore, the use of these approved ingredients does not automatically make a food product illegal. 2. It is treated as a separate food category The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) does not necessarily treat every analogue product as adulterated food. Dairy analogues and non-dairy substitutes can fall under separate food categories. For example, margarine made from vegetable fat is sold as an alternative to butter. Similarly, analogue paneer can be sold as an alternative to traditional paneer, provided it meets the applicable food-safety and labelling requirements. The key requirement is that consumers must not be misled. An analogue product cannot simply be sold or labelled as traditional milk-based paneer. It must be identified appropriately as an analogue or non-dairy product. 3. It can serve as an alternative for some consumers Non-dairy alternatives can be used by people who avoid or cannot tolerate conventional dairy products. They may also be chosen by consumers following plant-based diets. This is one reason regulators focus on proper labelling and consumer information rather than automatically banning every non-dairy substitute. 4. The focus is on clear labelling The basic principle is that consumers should know what they are buying and be able to make an informed choice. Manufacturers and sellers cannot misrepresent an analogue product as genuine milk-based paneer. Where applicable, packaging must clearly identify the product as an analogue or non-dairy alternative. Restaurants and hotels using such products are also expected to inform customers rather than presenting them as conventional paneer or cheese. Q4. Then why have Maharashtra and Gujarat banned it? Answer: The FSSAI is the central authority responsible for setting food-safety standards across the country. State governments, however, are responsible for enforcement and inspections on the ground. Authorities in states such as Chhattisgarh, Maharashtra, Gujarat and Uttarakhand found that, despite existing labelling requirements, some hotels, roadside eateries and sweet shops were allegedly serving analogue paneer without informing customers and passing it off as genuine paneer. The states therefore used their regulatory powers to impose restrictions or bans on analogue paneer, citing concerns over consumer deception and public health. Is UP also planning a ban? Uttar Pradesh is also considering a ban on analogue paneer. According to Harishankar Singh, Additional Director of the state's Food Safety and Drug Administration (FSDA), a proposal to ban analogue paneer has been sent to the FSSAI. If the proposal receives the required approval, Uttar Pradesh could also introduce a ban on analogue paneer.

stories.title: Son, daughter-in-law grab ₹3 crore land using dead father’s thumbprint:Evicted in Lucknow; father wanted property given to 3 daughters
stories.summary: In Lucknow, after the death of his father, the only son usurped land worth ₹3 crores by taking his thumbprint. He also involved his cousin in this act. Before the father's cremation, the son took his thumbprint on a plain paper. Villagers had made a video of the accused son, which came to light today, Thursday. Police investigation revealed that the father, troubled by the behaviour of his son and daughter-in-law, had disinherited them from his property. He had stated that the remaining property would be given to his three daughters. The incident is from Khadauha village in Rahimabad. He started living at his daughters' homes, giving each of the three one bigha of land Chhatrapal (75), a resident of Khadauha, and his wife Shivdevi had a long-standing dispute with their son Mahendra and daughter-in-law Lakshmi. It is alleged that both elderly people were subjected to ill-treatment. In the year 2023, they were also evicted from their ancestral home. According to relatives, Chhatrapal went to the house of his elder daughter Suman, who also lives in Lucknow. He also used to visit the homes of his other two married daughters. Pleased with the care provided by his daughters, Chhatrapal had expressed his intention to give one bigha of land each to his three daughters out of his approximately six and a half bighas of land. Meanwhile, angered by his son Mahendra and daughter-in-law, he had also announced their disinheritance from his property through a public notice. Son took father after dispute, death three days later According to daughter Suman, father Chhatrapal's health deteriorated on July 7. Mahendra was also informed about this. It is alleged that Mahendra reached Lucknow with his wife and other family members and took his father with him, claiming he would get him treated. Suman alleges that her father Chhatrapal died on July 9, three days after her brother took him away. During the father's last rites, Mahendra and his family members also abused the sisters. Accusation of taking thumbprint of dead body on plain paper Family members allege that after their father's death, Mahendra took the thumbprint of his dead body on a plain paper to prepare land-related documents. During this, his cousin also helped him. Villagers secretly made a video of the entire incident. This video has now surfaced.

stories.title: Class 11 friends hang themselves at lover’s house:One dies, other survives after noose breaks; families found them in Saharanpur
stories.summary: Two friends studying in the 11th grade in Saharanpur hanged themselves on Thursday afternoon. One student died, while the other survived as the noose came loose. She was found writhing on the floor. Marks of hanging were found on her neck. She has been admitted to a hospital. Both students had left home for school in the morning, but they went to meet a boy. Their families got wind of this. They reached the boy's house. Due to this, both girls got scared and hanged themselves. According to preliminary investigation, the student who died had an affair with the boy. He fled the scene after the incident. Police are searching for him. The incident occurred in a village in the Chilkana police station area, about 30 km from the district headquarters. The incident took place around 12 noon. Details of the case According to the police, there is a girls' college in the Chilkana police station area. Two students, aged 15 and 16, study in 11th grade here. They left their respective homes in the morning to go to college but both did not reach school. The school management informed the students' families around 11 am that both girls had not come to school. The families replied that both had left home in the morning to go to school. Fearing an untoward incident, the family immediately reached the school. They inquired from the friends of the students. Then, a friend of one of the students told the family that their daughter had a love affair with a boy. She had gone to his house with her friend. Family reached the boy's house, crowd gathered outside The family came to know that the boy's house was a short distance from the school. In a short while, everyone reached there. The family started knocking on the door of the house. When the door did not open, people from the vicinity also arrived at the scene. At that time, both students were inside the house. Seeing the crowd of family members and people outside, both of them got scared. Hanged Themselves with Dupattas, The Other's Noose Came Undone Fearing exposure and disgrace, both students made a noose with their school dupattas (scarves) and attempted to hang themselves. When the house door did not open for a long time, the family members tried to enter through another way. One of the family members reached the house via the neighbor's roof and opened the door. Inside, they saw one student hanging from the noose. She had died on the spot. Meanwhile, the other student's noose had come undone, and she had fallen down. Upon receiving information, the police also reached the spot and took both students to the hospital. Doctors declared one student dead. The other is undergoing medical examination, and the police are monitoring her condition. Accused boy adult, father labourer The young man at whose house the students hanged themselves is an adult. He lives with his father at home. His father works as a laborer at a brick kiln. He goes to work at 6 AM. After his father left, he called the students to his house. CO said girl hanged herself in a dispute Sadar Area Officer Vikas Pratap Singh Chauhan said, “The young woman took this step due to a dispute in a love affair. Action will be taken based on the complaint from the family members. Further action will be taken based on the post-mortem report and evidence.”

stories.title: RPF constable suspended for chewing Gutkha:Officer catches him during speech; he says, 'My lips are naturally red'
stories.summary: An RPF constable was suspended in Gonda on charges of consuming gutkha. It is alleged that the constable was consuming gutkha during the RPF security conference on Wednesday evening. Arun Tripathi, Senior Divisional Security Commissioner of Lucknow Division, who was present at the conference, noticed the constable. He stopped his speech, reprimanded him, and ordered action. The constable's suspension order was issued on Thursday morning. RPF Inspector Anirudh Rai stated that after suspending the constable, he has been attached to Lucknow. Meanwhile, the suspended constable has denied consuming gutkha and attending the conference. He stated - he had not consumed gutkha, his lips are naturally red. Know the full story Brahmadev Kumar Dwivedi, from Saurauri village in Deoria, is a constable in the RPF. He was recruited as a constable in 1998. Before his suspension, he was posted in Gonda. On Wednesday evening, a security conference was held at the RPF barracks complex in Gonda. Many RPF officers and a large number of jawans were present. Senior Divisional Security Commissioner Arun Tripathi was addressing the jawans. During this, his eyes fell on Constable Brahmadev Dwivedi. According to officials, the constable was chewing gutkha. Seeing this, Arun Tripathi stopped his address and reprimanded him. He said that the Railway Protection Force is a disciplined force and such irresponsible behavior will not be tolerated. After the conference, considering the matter as departmental indiscipline, he gave instructions for action. Following this, the constable was suspended on Thursday morning. Officers said - Indiscipline will not be tolerated Arun Tripathi said that the Railway Protection Force is a disciplined force. Laxity or indiscipline at any level in security arrangements will not be tolerated. Constable said - My lips were red, I had not eaten gutkha Constable Brahmadev Kumar Dwivedi denied the accusation. He said, The officers were upset seeing my red lips. I had not consumed gutkha at that time. According to Brahmadev, the main reason for the action against him is taking a bike onto the platform. He said that he was going by bike to perform duty in the eastern yard, as the yard is quite long. The officers were more upset about this. RPF Inspector Anirudh Rai said- Constable Brahmadev has been suspended due to indiscipline. Consuming paan masala while on duty is wrong. He has been suspended and immediately attached to Lucknow.

stories.title: Foreigner runs sex racket across 6 states:Turkmen woman caught in Lucknow; doctor says no private-part surgery
stories.summary: Lola Kayumova, a woman from Uzbekistan arrested in Lucknow, has made several revelations during police interrogation. Police said, “She had married Lucknow resident Janak Pratap Singh, who allegedly left her around two months ago.” The investigation has also revealed that Lola owned two houses in Lucknow and was allegedly running a sex racket not only in Uttar Pradesh but also in five other states. Police had been searching for Lola for a year Lucknow Police had reportedly been looking for Lola for around a year. A few days ago, she returned to the city with a woman from Turkmenistan. The two women went to the same clinic where Lola had previously undergone cosmetic surgery on her face and private parts. FRO alerted before planned surgery This time, before the procedure could be carried out, the doctor informed the Foreigner Registration Office (FRO) about Lola’s presence. An FRO team immediately reached the clinic and arrested Lola and the Turkmenistan national accompanying her. Police said, “They recovered an Aadhaar card, PAN card and driving licence from Lola’s possession. She has since been sent to jail.” Surgeon denies performing private-part surgery Bhaskar reporter spoke to Dr Vivek, the surgeon who had treated Lola. He claimed that he had performed only a nose surgery and denied carrying out any procedure on her private parts. Dr Vivek said, “I was being defamed by claims that I performed private-part surgery on Lola.” Police are continuing to investigate the case and her alleged activities across multiple states. First see 2 pictures- Police investigation about Lola Woman from Turkmenistan gave reference details of Lola A woman from Turkmenistan came to Dr. Vivek's clinic on August 7 for treatment. A rule had already come into effect that if any foreigner comes to India for treatment, all information must be provided to the FRO (Foreigner Registration Office). As per this procedure, all documents from the doctor's clinic were shared with the FRO. The woman who came for treatment had a medical visa. Besides this, she also had several papers related to treatment in Delhi. Along with that woman, Lola had attached her Aadhaar card as her reference. Upon seeing this, the doctor's clinic immediately informed the FRO. With this help, the FRO and police took Lola into custody and after interrogation, arrested her. The person Lola claimed to have married is missing According to Lucknow Police, the person named Janak Pratap Singh with whom she claimed to have married and based on which documents were prepared, could not be traced. Lola says he abandoned her two months ago. In such a situation, it is not possible to say who Janak is. All documents have also been sent for verification. After the report comes, it will become clear whether they are completely fake or were prepared with someone's connivance in the department. Difficulty in interrogation due to inability to speak Hindi, English Meanwhile, Lola doesn't know Hindi, she knows only a little bit of Hindi. Her way of speaking English is also quite different. Due to this, the police faced considerable difficulty in interrogation. However, the investigation made it clear that Lola was running a high-profile sex racket while staying in Lucknow. Stayed in India even after passport-visa expired DCP South Mohammad Mustak informed that on June 20, 2025, information was received about helping foreign women stay illegally in India and taking financial benefits. Plastic surgery/operations were also performed to change the identity of some foreign women without necessary documentary procedures. A case was registered at Sushant Golf City police station in the matter. Based on investigation and information received from FRRO, police detained and interrogated the accused woman Lola Kyumova (45), daughter of Alimad Jamovna, resident of Tashkent, Uzbekistan. According to police, during interrogation she revealed that even after the expiry of visa and passport, she had been living in hiding in different states and districts of India for several years. It is alleged that she had also made Aadhaar card, PAN card and driving license along with other documents contrary to rules. The woman has given information about several other people being involved in her gang and conducting illegal activities with their support. Accused of running flesh trade in 6 states Police claim, “During interrogation, the woman also revealed running immoral flesh trade in different states and districts.” Information has emerged that several other women are also involved in this network along with her. Many other pieces of evidence have also been found from the woman's mobile phone. Based on these evidences, police are investigating the identification of other members connected to the gang and their roles. According to police, “Different addresses of hers have surfaced in Lucknow's Rajajipuram and Sushant Golf City areas. She has given her home address here.” Now read what the surgeon says about Lola- First came to tattoo removal clinic in 2025 Dr. Vivek Gupta says, “Lola first came to his clinic in February 2025. Lola had contacted to get a tattoo near her eye removed. She had all Indian documents. In which it was written about marriage to a person named Janak Pratap Singh.” He added, “As all documents were Indian, there was no need to inform the FRO and fill Form-C. Lola came to his clinic several times for treatment.” Nose surgery was called facial plastic surgery The doctor says, “After the treatment started, Lola later said that she had a problem with her nose, which caused her difficulty in breathing. Due to this, she underwent septo rhinoplasty of her nose.” He added, “Whenever she came to the clinic, it was for tattoo and nose surgery. But she defamed us by saying it was facial plastic surgery and private part operation. However, it is not possible that someone's face can be changed.” Dr. Vivek Gupta says, “I am a plastic surgeon and has to treat people in different ways. The rules for treating foreign nationals have changed, which the FRO department oversees, but somewhere the department has failed to make doctors aware.” He added, “Regarding how to work for the treatment of foreign people, it is difficult to fill the form on the FRO website. Later, providing patient information also becomes difficult.” This time I didn't make a mistake, I informed the FRO beforehand A year ago, an allegation was made against me that I did not provide information before treatment, whereas he had all documents of Indian origin. The second time when he brought another woman for treatment, this matter was raised again and I am being highlighted, although this time information was given beforehand. In the FIR filed a year ago, Dr. Vivek Gupta was made an accused. A case was filed against him by talking to Trijin Raj aka Arjun Rana's associate. After this, his name was removed from the investigation, whereas Dr. Vivek Gupta claims that he has neither met Trijin Raj nor does he know him. It is not known how his name was linked. Now understand the root of the entire matter- On June 21, 2025, police received information about a sex racket operating in Omex Hazratganj Apartment in Lucknow. In the raid, Holida and Nilofer from Uzbekistan were arrested. Both were staying here illegally. Police investigation revealed that the flat belonged to Doctor Vivek Gupta. Lola had brought these two young women to India. Holida and Neelofar had told during interrogation that through Lola Kayumova, they had met Dr. Vivek Gupta, who runs Minerva Clinic in Patrakarpuram and Ahimamau. Dr. Vivek Gupta had performed plastic surgery on both of them. Dr. Vivek was accused of also becoming an active member of the racket. He used to perform plastic surgery on girls associated with the racket, so that their look would appear Russian and they would look younger.

stories.title: Rahul Gandhi moves SC over disproportionate assets case:Challenges Allahabad HC order for ED-CBI probe
stories.summary: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi filed a petition in the Supreme Court on Thursday in a disproportionate assets case. In this, he has challenged the order of the Lucknow Bench of the Allahabad High Court, in which the court had directed CBI and ED to verify the allegations of disproportionate assets. The case will be heard on August 17. Rahul Gandhi has also filed a separate transfer petition in the Supreme Court. In this, he has sought to transfer the case from Allahabad High Court to Delhi High Court. This petition was filed on August 7. Actually, Karnataka BJP worker Vignesh Shishir had accused Rahul of disproportionate assets in the High Court. Following this, the court had said in its order in May that if the petitioner's complaint has been received, then the allegations made therein should be verified according to law. CBI or ED can take appropriate steps under the law. This news is being updated....

stories.title: Lost ₹3 lakh in PUBG, student stages kidnapping:Uses AI to fake taped-mouth photo, sends it to father and hides at friend’s house
stories.summary: A Class 11 student in Gorakhpur, Uttar Pradesh, allegedly staged his own kidnapping after losing ₹3 lakh while playing PUBG. With the help of his girlfriend, the 16-year-old created AI-generated images showing tape over his mouth and blood marks on his body to make it appear that he had been brutally assaulted. The student then sent the images to his father on WhatsApp and demanded Rs 1 lakh, threatening that he would otherwise receive his son’s body. Father alerts police after receiving threat The student’s father, a cloth merchant, panicked after seeing the photographs and immediately informed the police. Police placed the teenager’s mobile phone under surveillance and tracked his movements. Within around two hours, they located him at a friend’s house and took him into custody. Girlfriend helped create fake images During the preliminary investigation, police found that the student’s girlfriend, who lives in Delhi, had allegedly helped him prepare the AI-generated photographs. The incident took place around 8pm on Tuesday (11 Aug) in the Sikrigunj area, around 40 km from the Gorakhpur district headquarters. Police are investigating the circumstances behind the student’s PUBG losses and the role of his girlfriend in the staged kidnapping. Student stages own kidnapping after friends demand ₹3 lakh repayment The Class 11 student, identified as the son of Satyaprakash, lives with his family in the Dhanghat area of Sant Kabir Nagar. He studies at an English-medium school in Gorakhpur. According to police, the teenager had developed an addiction to PUBG and borrowed money from friends and acquaintances to continue playing. Over time, his outstanding debt reportedly reached around ₹3 lakh. Debt pressure led to fake kidnapping plan Police said, “The student came up with the idea of staging his own kidnapping after people began demanding that he repay the money.” He contacted his girlfriend in Delhi and asked her to create photographs that would make it appear as though he had been abducted and assaulted. According to the preliminary investigation, the girlfriend used AI tools to edit the student’s photographs and create images showing signs of an apparent assault. The teenager planned to use these photographs to convince his family that he had been kidnapped and demand money from them. Put mobile on flight mode, sent photo by connecting to Wi-Fi As part of the plan, the Class 11 student left home around 7pm on Tuesday (11 Aug), telling his family that he was going to Sikrigunj. After reaching the area, he switched his mobile phone to flight mode. He later connected the device to a friend’s Wi-Fi network to send the planned messages. AI-generated photo sent with threat At 9:47pm, the student sent a threatening message to his father, Satyaprakash, on WhatsApp along with an AI-generated photograph showing him as an apparent kidnapping victim. Alarmed by the message, Satyaprakash asked where he should send the money. The student responded by sending a bank account or payment number and asked him to transfer the money online. Father says he cannot make online payment Satyaprakash told his son that he did not have money available for an online transfer. The student then changed his demand and asked his father to arrange ₹2 lakh in cash. Suspecting that his son had genuinely been kidnapped, Satyaprakash went directly to Dhanghat police station and informed the police. Surveillance revealed the truth, student found at friend's house SP South Dinesh Kumar Puri informed, “The police put the student's mobile number under surveillance. The investigation revealed that the student's phone was in Sikriganj. After this, the police contacted Sikriganj police and provided complete information.” He added, “When the police team reached there around 2 AM at night, the student was found comfortably at his friend's house. The police took him along to the station. During interrogation, it came to light that the student had fabricated a false story of his kidnapping to repay a debt.”
