stories.title: Ganga swells in Kanpur, children take boats to school:Floods hit 80 UP villages; ghats submerged in Kashi, cremations disrupted
stories.summary: Heavy rain in the hills has caused the Ganga, Yamuna, Sharda and seven other rivers to swell across Uttar Pradesh, with more than 80 villages affected by floods. Farrukhabad is the worst hit, with flooding reported in 49 villages. The rising water has also disrupted life in Varanasi, Kanpur and Unnao, while 48 districts are under a rain alert today. Ghats submerged in Varanasi, cremations disrupted In Varanasi, floodwater has reached the steps of the ghats and submerged more than 100 small temples. At Harishchandra Ghat, the cremation area has been flooded. Cremations are now being carried out on the upper steps, forcing families to wait for two to three hours to perform the last rites. Children take boats to school in Kanpur The Ganga in Kanpur has risen close to the warning level, with floodwater entering more than five villages. Children are using boats to reach their schools. Hundreds of bighas of farmland have also been submerged. In Unnao, Ganga water has entered residential colonies. Several residents are staying on rooftops, while boats are being used in flooded streets. Sharda swallows 70 acres in Lakhimpur Kheri In Lakhimpur Kheri, the Sharda river has already swallowed around 70 acres of land as its water level continues to rise. In Raebareli, a five-foot-long snake entered a house amid the flooding. Although most cities across Uttar Pradesh are seeing sunshine today, 48 districts remain under a rain alert. Monsoon likely to strengthen again Professor Manoj Srivastava, a weather scientist at Banaras Hindu University (BHU) in Varanasi, said the monsoon clouds had temporarily moved away from Uttar Pradesh. He said a low-pressure area was expected to become active over the Bay of Bengal, which could strengthen monsoon activity across the state again. “Good rainfall is expected across Uttar Pradesh in the coming days,” Srivastava said.

stories.title: Mahant kills two youths, buries bodies in temple:Was having affair with one man’s sister, went with friend to confront; case revealed after 19 days
stories.summary: A mahant in Baghpat, Uttar Pradesh, allegedly murdered two friends and buried their bodies inside the temple premises. The bodies were recovered 19 days later, after police were tipped off about the killings. Police recovered the remains of Ankit, 25, and Israr, 32, at around 3am today (13 Aug). The temple’s mahant had allegedly fled before the police reached the spot, while his two disciples were taken into custody. Bodies identified from clothes and watches The bodies had decomposed significantly by the time they were recovered. Police identified the two men with the help of their clothes and watches. According to the preliminary investigation, the mahant’s disciples confessed to the crime and helped police locate and recover the bodies buried behind the temple. Ankit allegedly went to confront mahant Initial police inquiries suggest that Ankit’s sister was allegedly in a relationship with the mahant. On July 25, Ankit reportedly went to the temple with his friend Israr to confront him and question him about the relationship. Police suspect an argument broke out during the confrontation and escalated, following which the mahant allegedly killed both men. Bodies allegedly buried with disciples’ help After the alleged murders, the bodies were reportedly buried behind the temple with the assistance of the mahant’s disciples. The incident took place in the Chandinagar police station area, around 20 km from the Baghpat district headquarters. Police are continuing to search for the absconding mahant and are questioning the two detained disciples. See pictures Know the complete case in sequence Israr, 32, and differently-abled Ankit, 25, residents of Sigoli Taga, were close friends whose houses were located directly opposite each other. Israr worked as a labourer, while Ankit was unemployed. Israr’s father Ridku told police that his son had gone for a bike ride with Ankit on the afternoon of July 25. When neither returned by the following day, their families began searching for them. From the evening of July 27, both men’s mobile phones were switched off. On July 29, their families lodged missing-person complaints at Chandinagar police station. Police then began tracing their mobile numbers, locations and other possible leads. Mahant’s disciples allegedly reveal the murders Police said, “After nearly 19 days, an informer provided information on Wednesday (12 Aug) night that Mahant Naresh Nath of the Ganesh Temple in Lahchauda had allegedly murdered the two missing men.” When police reached the temple in evening to question the mahant, he was reportedly not present and had allegedly fled. Police detained two of his disciples and questioned them. During interrogation, they allegedly revealed that the bodies of both youths had been buried within the temple premises. Bodies recovered around 3am Police returned to the temple with a team at around 3am and began excavation based on the information provided by the disciples. The bodies were recovered from the rear portion of the temple premises. As they had decomposed, police identified them with the help of Ankit’s disability and the watch worn by Israr. A forensic team was called to the scene and collected evidence. The bodies were subsequently sent to Baghpat District Hospital for post-mortem examination. Police arrested both disciples and are now searching for the absconding mahant. Brother alleges affair with mahant led friends to temple confrontation Israr’s brother Fareed alleged that his brother and neighbour Ankit had been close friends for several years. He claimed, “Ankit’s sister was allegedly in a relationship with Mahant Naresh Nath of the Ganesh Temple in Lahchauda.” According to Fareed, “The two friends had repeatedly tried to convince her to end the relationship, but she did not agree.” ‘They said they were going to Rataul’ Fareed said, “On July 25, Israr and Ankit left home saying they were going to Rataul, but allegedly went to the temple instead.” He added, “They may have gone there to confront, counsel and warn the mahant, but we do not know what happened after they reached the temple.” The family later reported both men missing after they failed to return. Fareed said, "Police called the family today morning (13 Aug) and informed them that Israr had allegedly been murdered and that his body had been recovered from the temple premises. Family earlier travelled to Ghaziabad to identify another body Israr’s brother Fareed said, “The family had earlier travelled to Ghaziabad on Monday after receiving information about an unidentified body, fearing it could be Israr.” However, the family later confirmed that the body belonged to someone else. ‘Today, we found Israr’s body at the temple’ Fareed said, “Israr’s body was eventually recovered from a pit inside the temple premises in Lahchauda.” The recovery has left the family devastated, with relatives struggling to come to terms with his death. Police have sent the body for post-mortem examination as the investigation continues. Mahant allegedly moved into temple six months ago Israr’s brother Fareed said, “Mahant Naresh Nath is originally from Uttarakhand and had been living in a rented house in Sigoli Taga village until around six months ago.” According to him, “The mahant lived next door to Ankit. After his alleged relationship with Ankit’s sister became known, a dispute reportedly arose. Following this, Naresh Nath allegedly shifted to the temple premises along with his disciples.” Police: Mahant absconding, two disciples detained Chandinagar police station in-charge Rakesh Kumar said, “The bodies of the two youths who had been missing since July 25 were recovered after police excavated the temple premises.” He added, “The bodies have been sent for post-mortem, and the exact cause and manner of death will be established through the report.” The officer said, “The temple’s mahant, who is allegedly suspected in the murders, is currently absconding. His two disciples have been detained and are being questioned.” Police stated, “Information about the location of the buried bodies was obtained from the disciples. CCTV footage from the temple and surrounding areas is also being examined, while teams continue to search for the mahant.” Israr used to work as a laborer, leaving behind wife and 3 children Family members told Israr used to run his family by doing labor work. His family includes wife Firdaus and three children. Daughter Isra is 6 years old, while son Ayan is 5 years old and Faizan is 3 years old. There is mourning in the family after Israr's death. Meanwhile, disabled Ankit was the only brother among 5 sisters. He was unmarried and unemployed. Two of his sisters are married.

stories.summary: A doctor committed suicide in Gorakhpur on Thursday. The doctor jumped from the eighth floor of an apartment to end his life. Family members took him to a nearby private hospital in a blood-soaked condition, where doctors declared him dead. The incident took place in the Gorakhnath police station area. On August 5, the doctor had filed an FIR at AIIMS police station, accusing a female con artist and her gang of defrauding him of Rs 1.40 crore. He had been in shock ever since this incident. A case of fraud has been registered against the PhD female con artist, her officer father, her teacher husband, and others. Police have arrested the female con artist and her father and sent them to jail. The incident is reported to have occurred around 9:30 AM. Veterinarian Parmatma Singh (52) lived with his two children, a boy and a girl, on the eighth floor of Basant Enclave, located in Rajendra Nagar Colony of Gorakhnath area. His wife, Savitri Singh, is also a veterinarian. After this incident, she is inconsolable. Upon receiving information about the incident, the police of Gorakhnath police station reached the spot and are investigating. The doctor was currently posted in a block of Maharajganj district.

stories.title: Women in UP to get ₹50,000 each:₹20,000 first instalment before polls, followed by ₹10,000 each; Yogi govt plans scheme
stories.summary: The UP government may implement a major scheme to target the women's vote bank before the assembly elections. Under this, more than 50 lakh women will be given financial assistance of Rs 50,000 each. The first installment of Rs 20,000 will be given before the elections. After the elections, if the BJP government is formed, 3 installments of Rs 10,000 each will be given. Deliberations on the scheme have started within the government. In fact, after registering a big win in the Bihar assembly elections last year, BJP's focus is now on UP. Just as Rs 10,000 each was sent to women's accounts before the elections in Bihar, a similar scheme will be launched in UP. Government will target women before elections The Yogi government has geared up for the assembly elections. Amidst the Gen-Z movement, the government is considering a major scheme to woo the women's vote bank. A scheme is being considered for women's assistance, self-employment, and economic self-reliance. The scheme will be proposed through the Women Welfare Department. Under the scheme, providing financial assistance of Rs 50,000 to women is being considered. Priority to women from families below poverty line The government will prioritize women from SC, ST families, women from BPL families, and women from economically weaker families in the scheme. It may include women from families whose income does not exceed 12 lakh rupees. Women's scheme will be a game-changer People in the government believe that the scheme of cash incentives for women can prove to be a game-changer in the assembly elections. Such a scheme was first implemented in Madhya Pradesh, then in Maharashtra and Bihar assembly elections. Due to those schemes, BJP governments were formed there. Political analyst Virendranath Bhatt believes that providing cash assistance to women in Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, and Bihar has benefited them in elections. If the government implements a similar scheme in UP, it will definitely benefit the BJP in the elections. There are about 5.67 crore women voters in the state. If women receive cash, it will impact the elections. Women can also become game-changers in UP BJP had a big victory in the Bihar Assembly elections. NDA had won 202 seats there. The unprecedented support and votes of women were considered the basis for NDA's victory, which was more than expected. The reason for women's inclination towards NDA was the 10-10 thousand rupees sent to the accounts of Jeevika Didis before the elections. Ministers of the Yogi government, BJP officials, and political analysts also believe this. That is why, after Madhya Pradesh's Ladli Behna Yojana, Maharashtra's CM Majhi Bahan Ladki, and Haryana's Deendayal Lado Lakshmi, BJP is going to implement a game-changer scheme in UP as well to secure the votes of women and daughters. Challenge of Mission 2027, Pressure of a Big Victory BJP-NDA had won in Haryana, Maharashtra, Delhi, and Bihar. After this, the UP Assembly elections- 2027 are no less than a big challenge for UP CM Yogi, BJP, and ideological organizations. Although CM Yogi has already registered the record of being CM for the longest time and running a BJP government for the longest time. However, given the results in Bihar, the pressure for a similar massive victory has increased. The assembly elections in UP will commence by the first week of January- 2027. Therefore, the government is going to launch a scheme for women as soon as possible. Understand: What is Bihar's Jeevika Didi Model? The NDA government led by CM Nitish Kumar in Bihar implemented the Mukhyamantri Mahila Rojgar Yojana (Chief Minister Women Employment Scheme). Its objective was to connect one woman from each family with self-employment. For this, one woman from each family was given financial assistance of 10 thousand rupees before the assembly elections. After starting the employment, the government will assess it. Following this, a maximum financial assistance of two lakh rupees will be provided to further expand the work. The Nitish government transferred 10-10 thousand rupees into the accounts of 25 lakh women. Approximately 500 crore rupees were spent on this. In the assembly elections, the NDA received a massive majority with 202 seats. After this, all political analysts say that the 10-10 thousand rupees transferred to the accounts of Jeevika Didis (women associated with Jeevika self-help groups) played a significant role in this massive victory. Now understand why BJP is targeting women voters? Target one, achieve all Political analysts believe - BJP strategists have understood that by targeting one woman in a family, she influences 5 votes. Especially, in families where women are given financial assistance, their votes are almost certain to go in favor of the concerned ruling party. In UP too, there are about 7.25 crore women voters. 98 lakh women in UP are engaged in self-employment The State Rural Livelihood Mission is running in UP to make women self-reliant. Under this, women's self-help groups of 10 women each are formed and linked to self-employment. Financial assistance is also provided by the government on subsidy. Currently, 98,76,389 women from 8,99,398 families are associated with these groups in UP. Women can become the counter to SP's PDA BJP leaders believe that providing significant assistance to women before the assembly elections can counter SP's PDA. In the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, SP's PDA issue worked. As a result, BJP's seats decreased from 64 to 34. After the Lok Sabha elections, in the BJP legislative party meeting, CM Yogi himself admitted that if elections were held today, BJP would get 188 seats in UP. That is why BJP is trying to woo women voters.

stories.title: Monsoon to remain active in Varanasi for next 6 days:Ganga water level starts receding, small temples submerged; boat operations resume
stories.summary: The monsoon has become active again in Varanasi, bringing the possibility of changing weather conditions across the city and neighbouring districts over the next six days. The Meteorological Department has forecast light to heavy rainfall at different places during this period, with thunderstorms and lightning also likely. Thunderstorms expected on Friday Rain accompanied by thunder and lightning is expected in Varanasi on Friday (14 Aug), with the possibility of thunderstorms in several areas. The department has also issued a heavy rainfall alert for August 15 and 16, indicating that rain activity could intensify during the weekend. Humidity and low pressure keeping skies cloudy Today (13 Aug), Varanasi recorded a temperature of around 32°C. Wind speed was about 3 kmph, while relative humidity stood at 74%. Weather officials said, “High humidity and the influence of a low-pressure system could keep skies cloudy and favour rainfall over the coming days.” See picture Now know what lies ahead The Meteorological Department has forecast thunderstorms accompanied by rain and lightning in Varanasi and adjoining areas on Friday (14 Aug). There is also a possibility of lightning strikes during the spell, prompting officials to advise people to remain cautious during adverse weather. Heavy rain alert for August 15-16 According to the department, Varanasi and surrounding areas could receive heavy rainfall on August 15 and 16. Rain accompanied by thunder and lightning is also likely to continue on August 17 and 18. Bay of Bengal system to drive rainfall Weather scientist Prof Manoj Srivastava said, “Rainfall activity is expected to continue for the next four days due to a low-pressure area that has developed over the Bay of Bengal.” Ganga water level decreased, but the pace is very slow The water level of the Ganga in Varanasi has started receding, but the decline remains slow. Over the past 36 hours, the river level has fallen by around 11 cm and currently stands at 63.60 metres. River falling by just 1 cm in six hours The pace of decline remains sluggish, with the water level dropping by only around 1 cm in six hours and about 2 cm over 12 hours. Ghats and riverside areas hope for relief According to the Central Water Commission, the Ganga’s water level in Varanasi is expected to continue falling. The gradual decline has raised hopes of relief among people living near the ghats and riverside areas. Ban on boat operations lifted The ban on boat operations imposed during the rise in the Ganga’s water level has now been lifted, bringing relief to boatmen in Varanasi. However, the administration and concerned departments have advised people to remain cautious while travelling on the river as the water level is still being monitored. Tulsi Ghat steps emerge as floodwater recedes With the Ganga’s water level falling and floodwater receding, the steps of Tulsi Ghat have started becoming visible again. The development is being seen as a sign of normalcy gradually returning to the area. Connectivity between ghats yet to fully resume Despite the improvement, connectivity between several ghats has not been completely restored. Officials expect movement and other activities along the ghats to return to normal only after the Ganga continues to recede steadily.

stories.title: Sharpened sword for 2 days, then killed contractor:Accused’s homes locked in Gorakhpur; police care for dog, cow
stories.summary: Electricity department contractor Shiv Kumar Tripathi was allegedly killed in Gorakhpur on August 8 in an attack involving a sword and sickle. The main accused’s house in Ahiraula is around 500 metres from the contractor’s residence. Police have arrested eight accused in connection with the murder, following which their houses have remained locked. Police personnel have been deployed outside the properties as a precautionary measure. Police feed dog and cow left at locked house A German Shepherd and a cow were left at one of the accused’s houses after the family members fled following the incident. With no one to care for them, the animals were reportedly left without food and water. For the past five days, police personnel deployed in the area have been feeding and providing water to the dog and cow. Murder allegedly linked to 2024 revenge killing Police investigation indicates that the murder was not the result of a sudden dispute but was allegedly linked to an old rivalry stemming from the 2024 murder of Aadesh Chaudhary. According to police, the contractor’s cousins were allegedly involved in Aadesh Chaudhary’s killing. The latest attack is believed to have been carried out as revenge for that murder. One of the accused, a Class 12 minor from Aadesh Chaudhary’s family, allegedly attacked Shiv Kumar with a sword. Police said, “The accused told investigators that he had sharpened the sword for two days after buying it so that it could inflict deeper injuries.” The murder has left the Ahiraula village tense, with police maintaining a presence around the homes of the arrested accused. Villagers hiding in homes, afraid even to speak The Dainik Bhaskar team reached Ahirauli village on Wednesday (12 Aug). There was silence in the streets. In the afternoon, village women were huddled inside homes talking. When asked anything, people were refusing to tell. To the extent that they were even pretending to be unaware about any incident that had occurred there. At Shiv Kumar's house, his only son Advocate Aditya Tiwari is sitting in white clothes, repeatedly breaking down remembering the incident. Meanwhile, there is a continuous stream of visitors throughout the day. People are consoling Aditya. From inside the house, the intermittent sounds of crying and wailing of Shiv Kumar's mother Savitri, wife Sandhya Devi and married daughter Nidhi Tripathi can be heard. The helpless, blood-soaked face of Shiv Kumar visible in the video is haunting the family. His father has passed away. He has two brothers, Siddhanath Tripathi and Ramkumar Tripathi. Attacked with a sickle while eating at Brahma Bhoj Actually, 2 years ago in 2024, Aadesh Chaudhary, the cousin of Rahul Chaudhary from the same village, was murdered. Contractor Shiv Kumar Tripathi (52)'s son and associates were accused of the murder. All of them had gone to jail. Since then, Rahul and his family harbored hatred towards Shivkumar. According to police, “On August 8, Shiv Kumar had gone to attend a Brahma Bhoj (community feast) in the village. He was sitting on the ground eating food. Just then, Rahul Chaudhary (30) attacked Shiv Kumar on the head from behind with a sickle. He fell down seriously injured.” Officials added, “When people present there intervened, the accused fled from the spot. The family hosting the Brahma Bhoj took Shiv Kumar in an auto to the hospital. On the way, Rahul, along with his minor brother and 8 others, stopped the auto.” They stated, “The accused had sticks and sharp weapons with them. Villagers tried to stop them, but the accused dragged Shiv Kumar out of the auto and took him 200 meters away. There, Rahul's minor brother came with a sword.” Officals further added, “They chased Shiv Kumar on the road and attacked him. He fell on the road. After that, they killed him with multiple blows. Then the accused fled from the spot. During this time, some youth present there made a video of the incident.” Rival families lived just 500 metres apart The Chaudhary family lives around 500 metres from the house of contractor Shiv Kumar Tripathi. The two families had been at odds since the 2024 murder of Aadesh Chaudhary, son of Deepu Chaudhary. Aadesh was shot dead during a Hari Kirtan in 2024. Shiv Kumar’s son and some of his relatives were named accused in the case and were subsequently jailed. Release of contractor’s son fuelled resentment Deepu Chaudhary is the eldest of four brothers. Deepu, Vikas and Pramod live and work in Mumbai, while two of Deepu’s sons, Vivek and Abhishek, are studying away from home. In Ahirauli village, Pramod’s minor son Vinod, who is studying in Class 12, and his nephew Rahul Chaudhary live with the family. The Chaudharys are considered a financially well-off family in the village. However, the murder of Aadesh had created deep resentment between the two families. According to the police investigation, tensions escalated further after Shiv Kumar’s son was released from jail. Police suspect that the long-standing anger and desire for revenge ultimately led to the contractor’s murder. Rahul displayed photos with weapons Rahul Chaudhary, identified by police as the main accused in the contractor’s murder, was reportedly fond of weapons and frequently shared photographs with them on social media. Posters featured BJP leaders Rahul was also preparing to contest the district panchayat elections from Ward No. 39 of Sikrigunj. As part of his campaign preparations, he had reportedly put up banners and posters at several locations. The banners carried his photograph alongside those of the BJP state president and the Chief Minister. Murder video surfaces on social media On August 11, Betiyahata councillor and lawyer Vishwajit Tripathi posted a video purportedly showing the contractor’s murder on Facebook. Tripathi alleged that police personnel pressured him to remove the video. Police also reached the court and reportedly attempted to take him to the police station, but returned after lawyers objected. Minor allegedly chased contractor before attack The video appears to show a minor chasing the contractor on the road before attacking him with a sword. During the attack, the contractor can be seen pleading with folded hands and asking to be spared. However, the attacker allegedly continued striking him. After apparently believing that the contractor had died, the accused fled the spot. In this regards, SSP Dr. Kaustubh said, “Police have arrested all 8 accused in the case and sent them to jail. Sikriganj police station in-charge Anjul Chaturvedi has been immediately line-attached on charges of negligence. Investigation of the case is ongoing.”

stories.title: Farrukhabad floods:31 houses swept into Ganga in 14 days; life savings lost, woman says, ‘My daughter’s wedding was planned, now we have no home’
stories.summary: “Last year, the Ganga swallowed our house. I took a loan to build another one, but now the river is about to take that too. My daughter’s wedding is approaching, but we have nothing left.” Tears welled up in Gyanadevi’s eyes as she spoke. She could not continue, while her daughter sitting nearby also broke down in tears. Gyanadevi lives in Bilawalpur village, around 10 km from Farrukhabad. The Ganga is now flowing just 50 metres from her house, with severe erosion leaving the building on the verge of collapse. 31 houses washed away in 14 days The situation is particularly grim in Dilip’s Madaiya village, where 31 houses have been swallowed by the surging Ganga in just 14 days. Only three to four houses remain. Fearing they too could soon be washed away, residents have started demolishing them themselves to recover whatever belongings they can and move them to safer locations. Villagers fear entire settlement could disappear Residents fear that continued rise in the Ganga’s water level and ongoing bank erosion could destroy the remaining houses as well. If the erosion continues at the same pace, villagers fear the entire settlement could eventually disappear into the river. Embankment breached as Ganga erodes riverbank The rising Ganga in Farrukhabad has breached a section of an embankment, allowing the river’s current to flow into surrounding areas. After causing severe erosion, the water has now moved nearly 1 km from the original point. Floodwaters have surrounded 48 villages, triggering anger among residents who fear further damage to homes and farmland. Villagers question ₹7.5-crore project Residents said an embankment costing around ₹7.5 crore was constructed before the monsoon to protect the area from the river’s rising waters. However, they alleged that the structure failed to withstand the Ganga’s pressure for even a few months, raising questions over the quality and effectiveness of the project. Due to flooding, roads have been submerged, and boats are the only means of transportation left. 1 lakh people have been shifted to safe locations. The situation is such that to reach Bilawlpur village, about 10 km from the district headquarters, one has to travel by boat for 5 hours. People are taking grains and remaining household items to safe places. House completed just two months ago Gyanadevi said, “My family had earlier lived in a village around 1 km away, where we had a four-room house with a veranda.” She added, “However, as the Ganga began eroding the riverbank, floodwaters reached our home and submerged it. We then built another house, which was completed in June this year.” She stated, At the time, we had no idea that the river would eventually change course and reach our new home after eroding the banks." ‘We made a mistake by building here’ Gyanadevi now regrets choosing the location for their second home. She said, “We made a mistake by building our house here. If we had bought land somewhere else, we would not have faced this situation today.” The family had invested all its savings in the new house. Now, with the Ganga threatening to swallow it as well, Gyanadevi says they have been left with almost nothing. ‘Crops, house, everything is being lost’ Gyanadevi’s husband Hansram stood outside their house in a torn shirt, repeatedly looking at the walls and their belongings. He later began removing bricks stored on the roof, hoping they could be reused if the family manages to build another house somewhere safer. He said, “Riverbank erosion has been a problem in the area for the past three to four years, with several houses already washed away.” ₹12.5 lakh house now under threat He stated, “This year, an embankment was built in our village to stop the erosion. We trusted it and built our house here, spending around Rs 12.5 lakh. But after the rains, the embankment itself was washed away. It was made of mud. Now our house is also on the verge of collapsing.” He recalled that the area did not face flooding on this scale around a decade ago. With repeated floods, villagers are now able to grow only one crop a year. The family had built the house hoping to arrange their daughter’s wedding. They had also raised 17 cows and goats, but the floods have put their home, livestock and livelihood at risk. ‘There was going to be a wedding at home’ Hansram’s 18-year-old daughter Shalini sat quietly a short distance from the family’s threatened home. She said, “The family had been preparing for a wedding, but the flood and erosion had left them uncertain about what would happen next.” When asked where the family would go if the house collapsed, Shalini struggled to respond and became emotional. After a brief silence, she said, “No officer comes to help us. Those who did come turned back halfway through the village.” ‘There were houses here, now nothing remains’ Village resident Sarvesh said, “My house was also destroyed by riverbank erosion. My uncle’s house stood next to it, but one of the structures collapsed this morning.” He stated, “There were two to three more houses a little further from here. Where we are standing now, there were houses. But look around — nothing is left.” ‘Crores were spent, but what did we get?’ Sarvesh expressed anger over the failure of the embankment built to prevent erosion. He asked, “Officials told us that the embankment had been constructed and the village land would no longer erode. Crores of rupees were spent on it, but where did that money go?” He said the authorities could instead have provided land at a safer location. He added, “It would have been better if they had given us land somewhere else. We could have built our houses there. The money is gone, and now our houses are gone too. We are left wandering around helplessly.” ‘No ration left, we do not know where to go’ Santosh Kumar said, “Severe erosion had already caused extensive damage in the area last year, with entire settlements being washed away.” He added, “In five villages, only two to four houses are left. If the erosion continues at this pace, more people will suffer losses.” He further stated, “Many residents had already abandoned their homes in villages surrounded by floodwaters”. According to him, government assistance has remained limited. He also added, “Officials came a few days ago and distributed ration before leaving. That stock has also run out. Now we do not know where to go or what to do.” See people's troubles in 2 pictures- Ganga water level inches towards danger mark In Farrukhabad, the Ganga is flowing just 5 cm below the danger level of 137.05 metres, raising concerns over further flooding and erosion. As water levels continue to rise, 48 villages have effectively been cut off and turned into islands after connecting roads were submerged. Administration starts boat services With road connectivity disrupted, the administration has started operating boats to maintain access to the affected villages. Irrigation Department officials have warned that the situation could deteriorate further if the Ganga continues to rise at the current pace. In this regard, ADM Arun Singh said, “There is flood water in 22 villages coming under Sadar tehsil. The government is providing assistance of ₹1.20 lakh. We have prepared a list of flood victims and sent it to the government. Relief camps and cattle centers have been set up.”

stories.title: ₹50,000 earned in one night, women also humiliate them:Male sex workers in Lucknow-Kanpur see growing trend; their hidden world
stories.summary: Male escorts, or gigolos, say their work is often seen as easy because their clients are women, many of them from affluent families. However, they describe the profession as risky, with concerns ranging from police action and financial uncertainty to abuse and health risks. A Dainik Bhaskar team spoke to two men from Lucknow, aged 28 and 34, who have been working in the profession for 4-5 years. Their identities have been withheld to protect their privacy. How they enter the profession One of the men said he entered the profession through friends after the Covid-19 pandemic, when he was living in Mumbai. He initially took up the work for fun and earned ₹6,000-₹7,000 from his first assignment. He gradually became comfortable with it and continued. According to him, appearance, personality and physical fitness are important in the profession. Escorts maintain their fitness through workouts and protein-rich diets and generally avoid intoxicating substances. However, some clients pressure them to drink. Lucknow and Kanpur emerge as new markets While demand is traditionally higher in metropolitan cities, the men said the profession has expanded to Lucknow and Kanpur. They claimed that escorts and clients are familiar with specific meeting spots, particularly in areas of Gomti Nagar. They also alleged that escorts have to pay members of their network to use certain spots. The amount varies, with some locations charging around ₹2,000 and others ₹3,000 a day. The men said senior members of their networks handle external arrangements, including dealing with the police and managing access to locations. Newcomers generally depend on these networks for work. Most bookings come through referrals According to the escorts, referrals are the main source of bookings. A satisfied client may recommend an escort to other women in her social circle, which also helps new clients feel more comfortable. They said many clients come from wealthy families and include wives of officers and women whose husbands are major businessmen living abroad. Earnings can reach ₹10 lakh a month Income varies significantly depending on the number of bookings. One escort said he can earn ₹2-2.5 lakh a month when work is steady, while some others in the profession earn ₹5-10 lakh. He charges around ₹20,000 for a full night and ₹10,000-₹12,000 for 2-4 hours. More established escorts can charge ₹30,000-₹40,000, and in some cases up to ₹50,000 for a night. However, income is not guaranteed. He said there are times when he gets no work for an entire month. Clients mostly middle-aged women The escorts said many of their clients are women aged 35-40, although some are 60 or older. Younger clients are comparatively uncommon. They described most clients as belonging to affluent sections of society and said they may have to meet 10-12 clients as part of their work. Police, abuse and health risks The men described several risks associated with the profession. They said fear of the police remains a major concern, while meeting unknown clients can also be dangerous. Some clients allegedly become aggressive after drinking, abuse the escorts or refuse to pay. The men said such incidents can affect their self-respect, particularly when clients are dissatisfied despite the services provided. They also raised concerns about sexual health. Although they said they generally take precautions, some clients allegedly refuse to allow protection, creating a risk of HIV transmission. One escort said he has begun considering leaving the profession because of the emotional and practical difficulties involved. Fraud in the name of gigolo jobs The report also highlights cyber fraud conducted through fake ‘Gigolo Club’ and ‘Gigolo Job’ s. Fraudsters allegedly demand money for registration, medical tests or hotel bookings. People are therefore advised to be cautious about such offers and verify claims before making payments. What the law says Supreme Court advocate Ayush Shukla said there is no separate law specifically governing gigolos or male prostitution in India. He explained that prostitution itself is not directly criminalised, but activities covered by the Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act (ITPA) can attract legal action. According to him, consensual private meetings between adults over 18 do not by themselves constitute a crime, but monetary transactions can create legal complications.

stories.title: Man stabs girlfriend, asks, ‘Now will you marry me?’:Boyfriend rants beside body; daughter says ‘cut off the killer’s hands and feet’
stories.summary: ‘My mother has been murdered. She was stabbed in the head and both her ears were cut off. I know him. A call came in Ajit’s name. Mommy said she would be back soon, but she never returned. Ajit killed my mommy. I want him to be stabbed too, his ears, hands and feet cut off. He should be hanged. I want him dead.’ These are the words of Baby’s two devastated daughters in Bulandshahr. On the night of August 11, Baby’s lover, Ajit, allegedly stabbed her 17 times with a knife. The attack was so brutal that her heart was severely damaged. Even after the murder, Ajit allegedly showed no remorse. He remained beside Baby’s body for about an hour, muttering angrily about her refusal to marry him and repeatedly saying, ‘Will you marry me now?’ The incident took place in the Khurja Kotwali area, around 25 km from the district headquarters. First, know what happened Baby (38), originally from Premnagar, Delhi, had been married to Pankaj from Bulandshahr for 15 years. The couple have two sons and two daughters, aged between 8 and 13. They live in Shivlok Colony. The accused, Ajit Thekedar (42), lived in a rented room around 200 metres from their house and worked at a utensil manufacturing factory in Khurja. Ajit’s wife had left him. He and Baby had been in a relationship for around one-and-a-half years. Ajit wanted to marry her, but Baby was unwilling and had gradually distanced herself from him. Police suspect that Ajit, angered by this, planned the murder. Neighbours said they heard loud noises coming from Ajit’s room on Tuesday night and informed the police. Officers arrived shortly afterwards and opened the door, where they found Baby lying on the floor and Ajit sitting beside her. Blood was scattered across the room. Baby was taken to hospital but died on the way. Daughters describe the night After their mother’s death, all four children were inconsolable. The elder daughter said Ajit had called her mother in the evening. ‘When Mummy was leaving, I asked where she was going. Papa had gone to work. Mummy said she would return soon. My elder brother also went with her. After some time, he came back and said Uncle Ajit had sent him back from near the toll booth. Mummy did not return.’ The younger daughter, crying after seeing her mother’s body, said: ‘They stabbed my mommy in the head and cut off both her ears. Stab that man too and cut off his hands, feet and ears. He should die just as my mother died.’ The children said that after their father left for work, all four siblings had stayed with their mother. When Pankaj returned at around 9.30pm, he asked about Baby and repeatedly called her phone. There was no response, and the phone was later switched off. Police arrived some time afterwards and took him with them. Husband: ‘I called her 35-40 times’ Pankaj said he returned from the shop at around 9.30pm and noticed that Baby was missing. The children told him she had gone to buy groceries. ‘I called her 35-40 times, but there was no answer. Her phone was switched off at around 10.30pm. At midnight, policemen came and said an officer wanted to speak to me. When I reached the police station, I learnt that my wife had been murdered.’ Neighbours found blood inside the room Neighbours said Baby had visited Ajit’s room previously as well. On Tuesday night, they heard loud noises coming from the room and became suspicious. Local residents gathered outside and looked inside, where they saw blood spread across the floor. They then alerted the police. Ajit allegedly remained beside the body According to police and neighbours, Ajit was sitting beside Baby’s body with a knife in his hand when officers arrived. He allegedly kept muttering angrily, ‘Will you marry me now?’ No one initially dared to enter the room, prompting the police to intervene. Ajit reportedly did not attempt to flee even after the police arrived. Post-mortem finds 17 deep wounds The post-mortem conducted on Wednesday, August 12, found 17 deep wounds on Baby’s body. Most of the stab wounds were on the left side of her chest and had severely damaged her heart. After the body was handed over to the family, relatives refused to perform the last rites and placed it on the Delhi-Aligarh Highway, blocking traffic. Pankaj said the family wanted immediate action against the accused and demanded that he be killed in an encounter before they would perform the last rites. The highway remained blocked for around an hour. Police teams from four stations and Khurja CO Shobhit Kumar reached the spot. The family agreed to remove the body after the CO assured them of action. Pankaj performed Baby’s last rites at around 5pm on Wednesday. Baby’s sister Parveen said, ‘Just as our sister was killed, we want Ajit’s body to be brought before us in the same condition. We appeal with folded hands to Yogi and Modi ji to have him hanged. Baby’s four young children are suffering. Who will now place a mother’s hand on them? Is there anyone who can give them a mother’s love?’ Accused sent to district jail Khurja CO Shobhit Kumar said- After the post-mortem, the body was handed over to the family. The blockade was cleared after we assured them of action. The accused will receive severe punishment through the court. A case has been registered and the accused has been sent to the district jail.

stories.title: IAS officer shot seven times says life at risk:"Give it in writing if security won’t be increased, I’ll go to court"
stories.summary: IAS officer Rinku Singh Rahi has expressed concern over his security in Jalaun. He has alleged that despite repeated requests, no action is being taken on his demand to increase his security arrangements. Rinku Rahi has also made a related post on social media X. In it, he has written that the security threat remains serious. Despite continuous requests, security arrangements are perhaps deliberately not being increased. Requests are continuously being made on all currently available platforms. But for some reason, no one seems to be paying attention? If they simply provide in writing that "there is no need to increase security," then the court can be approached. But even that is not happening. “As always, if these letters are made public to clarify his security and the actual situation, then some people will, as always, accuse him of making the letters public to get media attention. Should one really wait for an accident to happen?” Rahi also mentioned a Facebook page named 'Justice For Rinku Singh Rahi' in his post. He claimed that this page was run by his supporters. They compiled and published various posts. This Facebook page has been removed by the administration. Came into discussion due to these controversies 5 days ago, the Bar Association had levelled allegations against Rahi's working style On August 4, the Jalaun Bar Association announced a boycott of revenue courts starting August 5, raising serious questions about Rinku Singh Rahi's functioning. A letter was issued by Omnarayan Singh, Vice President of the Bar Association. According to it, advocates had complained to District Magistrate Rakesh Kumar Pandey three times about SDM (Judicial) Rinku Singh Rahi. The Bar Association alleged that Rinku Singh Rahi talks about passing one-sided orders in court in the absence of advocates and litigants. Additionally, lawyers alleged that they were subjected to rude behavior in court, which affects the judicial process. The Bar Association had warned that the boycott of revenue courts would continue until there was a change in the working style. IAS Officer's Dispute Occurred in Municipal Council 10 Days Ago 10 days ago, a dispute arose in the Orai Municipal Council regarding an investigation. IAS officer Rinku Singh Rahi had reached the Municipal Office at 2 PM. He had started looking at files related to irregularities. On this, the Executive Officer present there had raised an objection. After this, a debate started between the two. IAS officer Rinku Singh Rahi had told the Executive Officer - "Show the order. After all, in which order is it written that I will not be shown the records? Show me that order, I will leave immediately." The Executive Officer alleges that Rinku Singh Rahi had arrived with some of his private people. They were making videos while viewing the files. Actually, an investigation was underway regarding allegations of corruption in the Orai Municipal Council. Rinku Singh was also part of this investigation team, who was the SDM of Jalaun at that time. However, after his transfer to Orai, his role had ended. On June 29, the IAS officer had pushed the BJP block-chief On June 29, Block Chief Ramraja Niranjan had accused Joint Magistrate Rinku Singh Rahi of assault. The Block Chief had also shown a video of Joint Magistrate Rinku Singh. In it, Rinku Singh was seen pushing and shoving. He was seen slapping the Block Chief's mobile phone, making it fall to the ground. After that, he pushed him forcefully with both hands, sending him backward. The Block Chief had complained about this to DM Rajesh Kumar Pandey. Resident of Hathras, first became PCS then IAS Rinku Singh Rahi was born on May 20, 1982, in Hathras into a Dalit family. He is a resident of Usva village in Sasni police station area. Rinku's father, Soudan Singh Rahi, the elder of two brothers, supported the family by running a flour mill. Due to the family's weak financial condition, he studied in a government school. After passing 12th grade with good marks, he received a scholarship. With its help, he completed B.Tech from Tata Institute, Jamshedpur. In 2004, Rinku Singh passed the PCS examination. During his job, he appeared for the UPSC Civil Services examination under the disabled quota. In 2021, he secured the 683rd rank and became an IAS officer. In his family, his wife Sulakha has been a yoga teacher. He has a 10-year-old son, Dhruv Rahi. His uncle, Raghuveer Singh Rahi, was the district president during the BSP rule.

stories.title: FIR against 28 vehicles in Atiq’s son’s convoy:Prayagraj toll manager alleges barriers were broken, attempt made to run him over
stories.summary: Action has begun against 28 vehicles that were following Mafia don Atiq Ahmed's son Umar while he was being brought on parole in Prayagraj. The police have registered an FIR against the drivers of all those vehicles. This action has been taken based on the complaint of Jaiprakash Yadav, Assistant Manager of Nawabganj Toll Plaza. It is alleged that on Saturday evening, these 28 vehicles broke the toll barrier and passed without paying the fee. When attempts were made to stop these vehicles, the employees were assaulted. There was also an attempt to run them over. The employees somehow moved aside and saved their lives. According to the complaint, the incident occurred on August 8, around 3:50 PM, at toll booth number three. Atiq Ahmed's elder son, Mohammad Umar, was being brought from Lucknow to Prayagraj with a police escort. It is alleged that the drivers of the vehicles in the convoy started breaking the barrier at high speed and passing without paying the toll fee. When toll employees tried to stop the vehicles, they were verbally abused. They were threatened with death. The police are now identifying the vehicles based on their numbers. See 2 pictures Know why Mohammad Omar was taken from Lucknow to Prayagraj Aban Ahmed, the youngest of mafia Atiq Ahmed's five sons, died three days ago on August 6 in a road accident in Jhansi. He was going to meet his second brother, Ali Ahmed, who is imprisoned in Jhansi jail. On the way, the speeding car lost control and collided with a divider. In this accident, Aban and his companion Sonu, who were sitting in the front seat of the car, died on the spot. Three more people in the car were injured. After Aban's death, his two elder brothers, Mohammad Umar and Ali Ahmed, who are imprisoned, filed an application for parole in the High Court. They had sought permission to attend Aban Ahmed's funeral in Prayagraj. On August 7, the Allahabad High Court granted permission to both to attend the funeral with several conditions and restrictions. After parole was granted, both were sent to Prayagraj on August 8 with police security. Mohammad Umar was taken from Lucknow jail and Ali Ahmed from Jhansi jail to Prayagraj in a police van. Convoy of private vehicles grew as they entered the Prayagraj border As soon as they left for Prayagraj, their close associates' vehicles started following their vehicles. The convoy of supporters' vehicles continuously increased as they entered the Prayagraj border. By the time they reached Kasari-Masari, several vehicles were seen in both convoys. According to the complaint filed by Jaiprakash Yadav, Assistant Manager of Nawabganj Toll Plaza in Prayagraj, with the police, Umar Ahmed was being brought in police custody. After the government vehicles passed, about 25 to 30 private vehicles followed them. The drivers of these vehicles broke through the boom barrier at high speed without paying the toll fee and proceeded. Attempt to run over toll workers, lives saved by moving aside When toll workers tried to stop the vehicles, it is alleged that the drivers abused them and threatened to kill them. The complaint also states that some vehicle drivers drove their vehicles at high speed towards the employees with the intention of crushing them, due to which the employees somehow moved aside and saved their lives. In this incident, the boom barrier of the toll plaza was damaged. According to the assistant manager, the toll management also incurred revenue loss due to vehicles passing without paying toll fees. The complainant also stated that revenue loss occurred due to vehicles passing without paying toll. Report based on vehicle numbers The complaint also stated that some vehicle numbers were incomplete and many had no numbers at all. These included Mahindra XUV, Creta, Thar, Scorpio, Swift, WagonR, Dzire, Fortuner, Brezza, and many other vehicles. The complaint also recorded the numbers of several vehicles. Based on the complaint filed by Jaiprakash Yadav, Nawabganj police registered a report in the matter and started an investigation. Such a crowd was seen again for the first time after Atiq's death Three years ago, on April 15, 2023, after the murder of Atiq Ahmed and his brother Ashraf, such a large crowd gathered for the Atiq family in Prayagraj once again. However, this time the occasion was not for a political show of strength, but for the funeral of the family's youngest son, Aban, after his death. Nevertheless, the long convoy seen with both sons who came on parole and the crowd gathered in Kasari-Masari certainly reminded the city of that old image, when Atiq's name was taken with dominance in Prayagraj. Nawabganj Police Station In-charge Pankaj Awasthi said- Investigation is being conducted based on the CCTV camera footage installed at the toll plaza, statements of toll employees, and the vehicle numbers recorded in the complaint. Through the footage, it will also be ascertained which vehicles passed by the spot at the time of the incident and which vehicle damaged the barrier.

stories.title: Why was Brij Bhushan acquitted in sexual harassment case?:Court asked complainants why they went back to meet him after the incident
stories.summary: How did UP strongman BJP leader Brijbhushan Sharan Singh get acquitted in the case where allegations of sexual harassment by women wrestlers caused an uproar from Parliament to the streets? To find the answer, 'Dainik Bhaskar' spoke to the panel of lawyers who fought Brijbhushan's case. They gave 5 major reasons. We learned from the lawyers which evidence the court considered weak and which witnesses it did not trust. Read on what evidence and witnesses the Delhi Rouse Avenue Court based its decision on August 3. 1- What discrepancies did the court find in the witnesses' statements? Advocates say - The court also examined the statements of the main victim witness. According to the court, changes in the place, year, and dates of incidents emerged in statements given at different times. 2- If sexual harassment occurred, why did the victim go to meet Brijbhushan? The court also noted the meetings between the victim and the accused after the alleged incidents. The verdict stated that some incidents were claimed to have occurred in public places, but at that time, no objection was raised by any eyewitness or relative. The court also noted that after their marriage in December 2018, the victim and her husband went to Brijbhushan Sharan Singh's house to seek blessings. Pictures of this were also presented in court. 3- Two female wrestlers denied the allegations in court In the case, two victim witnesses denied allegations of misbehaviour against Brijbhushan in court. They told the court that they were pressured to make allegations against Brijbhushan. According to them, they were told that until Brijbhushan was removed from the post of WFI president, the future of wrestlers from Haryana would be ruined. They also said that they were given complaints prepared in English, which they were asked to translate into Hindi and memorise. 4- Court also found contradictions in other allegations The court also mentioned inconsistencies in the statements of other witnesses. One witness claimed that the incident occurred on February 28, 2018, in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan. But according to the official match schedule, their match was on March 1. Meanwhile, another had refused in writing to have the alleged incident site inspected with the police. According to the court, the prosecution could not provide a satisfactory reason for this. 5- What did the court say regarding the complaints? The court also noted that there was no written complaint or official record of sexual harassment against Brijbhushan before the sit-ins and protests began. The verdict also raised questions about the language of the complaints and their similarities. The court found that there were several contradictions in the prosecution's story and that it failed to prove the allegations beyond a reasonable doubt. What was the court's final decision? After reviewing all these statements, documents, and other evidence, the trial court acquitted Brijbhushan Sharan Singh and Vinod Tomar of all charges. This means the court held that the prosecution failed to present sufficient and reliable evidence to prove the charges. Now understand the whole case Based on the complaint of six female wrestlers in 2023, an FIR was registered against Brijbhushan Sharan Singh at the Connaught Place police station in Delhi. Police had filed a charge sheet against him under sections like outraging the modesty of a woman, sexual harassment, stalking, and criminal intimidation. WFI former assistant secretary Vinod Tomar was charged under the section of criminal intimidation.

stories.title: Sunny Deol says families struggled to recover after 1947 Partition:'We showed it in the film, and Punjab was affected the most'
stories.summary: Bollywood actor Sunny Deol said that he has heard many stories related to the 1947 partition from his elders. Many families were broken then. "How they struggled to recover later, this is what we have tried to show in the film 'Bantwara 1947', Sunny said during the film's promotion in Lucknow. Sunny and his son Karan Deol had a conversation with Dainik Bhaskar. During this, Sunny talked about the film's story, memories related to partition, and his expectations for the film. Additionally, Karan talked about the film's shooting, his father's company, and his father's behaviour towards him. Both father and son also shared their experiences of coming to Lucknow. Read the full interview Question: Many films have been made on partition before. How different will this film be? Answer: There are many topics, like in films, on which a lot of work has been done. What has been tried to be told in this film, perhaps no one has said or told it yet. The partition had the most impact in Punjab. People there didn't know what would happen when they woke up tomorrow. It shows how a family breaks, recovers, and comes together during partition. Question: Karan, how challenging was it to play a character in this film? Answer : This film was completely a different zone for me. I worked very hard. For this, I went to Adishakti Acting Workshop. I worked a lot with Raj and Aamir sir. [In the middle of Karan's answer] Sunny Deol said, “Raj Santoshi celebrated this story a lot and everything happened.” Question : Your enthusiasm and passion in this film felt like that of the film Gadar. Did you remember Gadar during the shooting? Answer : We had heard this story in 2010. Since then, this story had settled within us. Aamir had also heard this story, then we told Aamir (Khan) that we would make it and the film was made. Question: What did you remember while shooting? How much did you feel that pain? Answer: We grew up listening to our elders sitting in the house where we spent our childhood, talking about stories of partition. We felt very sad listening to their stories, thinking that such things also happened. At that time, those stories settled within us, and when this story was narrated, we connected with it very quickly. Then all the old things came back to us. Question: Sunny ji, you shot Gadar in Lucknow. How do you remember the city? Do you like the taste, language, or buildings here? Answer: I can never forget the experience I get from Lucknow. People give a lot of love. I always feel special here. Whenever I come, I think about when I will get to visit Lucknow again.

stories.title: IPS officer’s father orders firing at woman's house:Victim alleges accused wants to grab her land, threatened to kill her
stories.summary: In Sitapur, 20 to 25 rounds of firing took place at a woman's house on Sunday. This caused panic among the locals. The father of Mayank Bajpai, a trainee IPS in Jharkhand, is accused of orchestrating the firing. The woman stated, "Around 2 PM, 24-25 armed people arrived and started firing indiscriminately. They dragged me outside and threatened to kill me. My land is located along National Highway 30 (the road connecting Uttarakhand to Andhra Pradesh), which the accused want to seize." Bullet marks were found on solar panels and the house's walls. Police recovered empty cartridge casings from the scene. Some suspicious individuals have also been taken into custody and are being interrogated. The incident occurred near Adhauri Bypass Mod in the Maholi Kotwali area. See 2 pictures The woman said, “We registered the land in 2018” Munish, a resident of Adhauri Bypass, is a farmer. According to his wife Shobhana Shukla, she is originally from Deoria village. In 2018, she registered a sale deed for 19 biswa (8265 square feet) of land on Adhauri Bypass. The cost is approximately one and a half crore rupees. She is living with her family in a house built on a part of the land. The rest of the land is also under her possession. IPS's father bought land in 2022, dispute since then Shobhana said - Mayank Bajpai, a resident of Kamhera village, is an IPS officer. He is posted as a trainee IPS in Jharkhand. Mayank's father, Vipin Bajpai, registered the sale deed for the land in 2022. This means both parties claim the same land. The dispute has been ongoing since then. According to Shobhana, about two months ago, the decision regarding the land at Maholi Tehsil came in her favour. Despite this, people from the other side are trying to occupy the land. Allegation of firing on people who arrived in a DCM According to Shobhana, on Sunday at 2 PM, about 24-25 people arrived at her house in a DCM, armed with weapons. As soon as they reached outside the house, they started hurling abuses. After this, rapid firing took place. At the time of the incident, Shobhana was alone at home. Her husband and children had gone to Deoria village. Upon receiving information about the firing, the police arrived at the scene. The police recovered empty shells from the crime scene and detained several suspects for questioning. After the incident, there was an atmosphere of fear among the local residents. Inspector said - Case will be registered against the accused Inspector JB Pandey said- The woman has given a written complaint. A case will be registered. Police found empty shells from the spot. All allegations, including firing, are being investigated. Further action will be taken based on that. Who is IPS Mayank Bajpai? Mayank Bajpai secured the 149th rank in UPSC 2024. This was his third attempt. His father, Vipin Bajpai, is a farmer. The family left their village in 2002 and settled in Sitapur. Mayank has two brothers and one sister. He completed his initial schooling in Sitapur, then pursued graduation and post-graduation from Delhi University.

stories.title: Youth stabbed to death with rod in Lucknow:Friend plots murder after victim threatened to expose sale of his mother’s anklet
stories.summary: A 22-year-old youth was murdered in Lucknow by stabbing a rod into his stomach. His friend had sold his mother's anklets. When he found out about this, he told his friend that he would inform his family. To this, the friend replied, "You'll only tell them if you're alive." After this, the friend, along with his father, attacked him. The youth's body was found lying outside his house on Sunday morning. Upon receiving information, the police arrived and sent the body for post-mortem. The incident took place in the Madiyav police station area. A video of this entire incident has also surfaced. In this case, the police stated that a named FIR has been registered against Sumit and his father Mathura, based on the complaint of Shubham's brother Shivam. Both have also been arrested. Further action will be taken based on interrogation and the post-mortem report. CCTV images: Shubham himself had sold anklet A few days ago, Sumit sold an anklet. Shubham was the one who had helped him sell that anklet. However, a few days later, Shubham found out that Sumit had sold his mother's anklet. At this, he told Sumit, "I will tell your mother. Why did you sell her anklet through me?" Sumit got angry with him over this. One day, they had a fierce quarrel. After this, the matter calmed down. However, Sumit decided to take revenge on Shubham. On Saturday evening, he called Shubham out of his house on the pretext of going for a walk. Around 10 PM, Sumit, along with his father Mathura, murdered Shubham. Father-son seen attacking in CCTV CCTV footage related to the incident has also surfaced. In it, Shubham Soni is seen in a black shirt. He goes out of an alley. After this, he runs back inside. Meanwhile, 2 people attack him. During this, some people also come running from the other side and stab Shubham in the stomach with a rod. After this, everyone is seen leaving, holding onto each other. Shubham somehow stumbles forward. Unable to walk, he stands leaning against a wall. In a bloodied state, Shubham cannot stand for long. He falls face down on the ground. Mother said ‘They called my son and murdered him’ Mother Malti Soni said- My healthy son was called and taken from home at 7 PM on Saturday. Those people first made my son drink alcohol. Then they hit my son with bricks and stones. After that, they pierced an iron rod into his stomach. My son used to drive a four-wheeler. I don't know what kind of fight happened between these friends that they killed him and threw his body at our doorstep and left. My son's body was found lying outside the house on Sunday morning.

stories.title: Elderly man defrauded of ₹8 Lakh:Scammer posed as ‘Ambani’ on video call; police launch investigation
stories.summary: A very serious and shocking case of cyber fraud has emerged from the Pipiganj area of Jungle Kaudia police station in Gorakhpur. Here, 75-year-old elderly Lalman Sahni was trapped in a highly planned manner by cunning cyber criminals. In this fraud, technology, psychological pressure, and the names of big personalities were used in such a way that the victim did not suspect anything for a long time. Actually, the entire matter started with a video call. The person making the call claimed to be the country's big industrialist "Mukesh Ambani". Not only this, during the conversation, another person was presented as a famous actor, which made the call seem completely genuine and trustworthy. The fraudsters maintained their manner of conversation, language, and confidence in such a way that the elderly person came completely under their influence. Trap laid by showing the dream of 'becoming a millionaire' Fraudsters presented a fake investment scheme, claiming that investing ₹10 lakh would yield returns of up to ₹40 crore. By repeatedly calling, citing big names, and creating pressure to make quick decisions, they mentally prepared the elderly person. Gradually, they became convinced that this was a big and safe investment opportunity. Money transferred to different accounts When trust was fully established, the fraudsters started getting money transferred to different bank accounts. The victim sent a total of approximately ₹8 lakh in multiple installments. Each time, they were assured that a big return would come after the process was completed. After sending the money, when no returns came for a long time and the fraudsters stopped answering calls, the elderly person became suspicious. Attempts were made to contact them again, but the numbers were found to be switched off. After this, they realized that they had become a victim of cyber fraud. Cyber cell engaged in investigation The victim immediately lodged a complaint at Pipiganj police station. The police have registered an FIR and started investigating the case with the help of the cyber cell. The investigation is examining mobile numbers, bank account details, UPI transactions, and digital trails to track down the accused. Experts say that cyber fraudsters are no longer limited to just calls or messages, but are using video calls, deepfake technologies, and the names of prominent personalities. This makes people believe that the person on the other end is genuine, when in reality it is completely fake. Especially elderly people and those with limited technical knowledge are becoming easy targets. Such cases have surfaced before Several cases of fraud through investment and video calls have already surfaced in Gorakhpur and surrounding districts. Each time, fraudsters adopt new technologies and new methods to trap people, which makes catching them challenging as well. Expert advice: Avoid such fraud

stories.title: Krishna Janmabhoomi kar seva halted, shila pujan held:4 detained, including woman leader, while trying to enter Mathura Shahi Masjid for Jalabhishek
stories.summary: The proposed Kar Seva at Shri Krishna Janmasthan in Mathura has been postponed. Chitrakoot Peethadhishwar Swami Sachchidanand Maharaj announced this on Saturday evening. He said- Keeping in view the Kanwar Yatra and the month of Sawan, the Kar Seva has been postponed for now. The Kar Seva could disturb the atmosphere of the holy month of Sawan. However, on Sunday around 10 am, the havan-puja of stones for temple construction began at Chitrakoot Peeth Ashram. These pink stone blocks have been brought from Rajasthan. Actually, on 4 July, Chitrakoot Peethadhishwar Swami Sachchidanand Maharaj had announced Kar Seva on 9 August for the liberation of Shri Krishna Janmabhoomi, on the lines of the Ram Mandir movement in Ayodhya. Meanwhile, after the call for Kar Seva, the security arrangements at Shahi Idgah Mosque have been increased. Police have detained four people, including Akhil Bharat Hindu Mahasabha's Agra district president Meera Thakur, who were going to the mosque premises for Jalabhishek. See the pictures First read what Swami Sachchidanand Maharaj said... Swami Satchidanand Maharaj said that in view of the Kanwar Yatra and the month of Sawan, the date of the Kar Seva to be held at Shri Krishna Janmabhoomi has been postponed. As long as Sawan is ongoing and Kanwar pilgrims are on their journey, no such work will be done that could spoil the atmosphere or create any major problem. The Kar Seva has not been cancelled, nor has the organization backed down. It has been postponed for now after the decision of the Akhara Parishad. All saints work under the Akhara Parishad and receive directions from there. The Parishad has decided that the Kar Seva program to go to Shri Krishna Janmabhoomi should be kept suspended for now. Announced Kar Seva on 4 July Swami Sachchidanand Maharaj had announced Kar Seva on 9th August, giving the slogan "One More Push" on 4 July. In support of this, he had also met Sadhvi Ritambhara at Vatsalya Ganga Ashram in Haridwar on 12th July. He had said that efforts were made at several levels, including the court in the Shri Krishna Janmabhoomi case, but no solution was found. Therefore, the decision for Kar Seva was taken. After the announcement of Kar Seva, the police had issued notices to Swami Sachchidanand Maharaj along with several saints, sadhvis and religious leaders of Braj. Allegation of complicating the case in court Swami Sachchidanand Maharaj alleged that the Muslim side is complicating the case in court. He said that attempts are being made to obstruct the hearing by citing the Places of Worship Act, 1991. He demanded daily hearing of this matter. His claim is that the 1968 agreement is being cited, whereas the people with whom this agreement was made were not part of the Shri Krishna Janmasthan Trust. He said that the matter is only being complicated and that is why the announcement of Kar Seva had to be made. Will welcome if reconciliation happens Regarding the reconciliation talks underway at the Legal Services Authority on the Supreme Court's directions, Swami Sachchidanand Maharaj said that if reconciliation happens, he will welcome it. He said - We will welcome them, garland them. Wherever their place is built, we will also go there and lay a brick. Along with this, he appealed to the Muslim side to leave Shri Krishna Janmasthan. First consignment of pink stones arrived from Rajasthan The first consignment of pink stones from Banshipur village in Rajasthan for the construction of Shri Krishna Janmabhoomi Temple arrived at Chitragupta Peeth Ashram on Friday. On Sunday morning, the worship of these stones began amidst Vedic chanting. Havan-yagna is also being performed at the ashram. Swami Sachchidanand Maharaj informed that these stones will be carved by artisans from Odisha. After that, they will be used in temple construction. Episodes from Braj culture and Lord Shri Krishna's birth to his childhood pastimes will be carved on the stones. He informed that an order for 50 thousand cubic meters of stone has been placed for temple construction. In the first consignment, 350 cubic meters of stone has already arrived. Further consignments of stones will continue to arrive in a phased manner. Ashram is built on Vrindavan-Radhakund road Swami Sachchidanand Maharaj's Chitragupta Peeth Ashram is located on Vrindavan-Radhakund Road. It is about one kilometer inside on the road going from Julhaindi village to Konhai village, about 20 kilometers away from Vrindavan. The ashram built on about 6 bighas has two gates. After entering from the first gate, there is a place of worship, saint's room, kitchen and other facilities.

stories.title: People confined to homes amid leopard scare in Moradabad:Alert on Kanwar route; leopard mauls woman to death, leaves farmer critically injured
stories.summary: "Three days ago, a leopard mauled a woman to death and injured a farmer. On Thursday at 2 PM, two leopards were seen roaming around. Forest department employees were right there. Around 7:30 PM, a third leopard also arrived. All three leopards sat comfortably until 9 PM. If the forest department wanted, they could have easily caught them. Can't understand whether these forest department people are catching leopards in this 'Lalapur' or rearing them." These words were spoken by Mahipal Singh of Lalapur village in Moradabad. Actually, in the Thakurdwara area of Moradabad adjacent to the Uttarakhand border, which falls in the buffer zone of Jim Corbett, 3-4 leopards have been creating terror for the past 10 days. A population of about 1 lakh within a radius of approximately 20 km is living in fear. Being a Kanwar route, alert posters have been put up at various places. People have stopped going out alone or in pairs. Families are not sending children to school. To know in detail about the terror of the leopard- 50 employees of Forest Department are searching for leopards; 13 cages have been set up A team of more than 50 forest experts from the Forest Department has been called from 6 different districts. They have been tasked with catching the leopards. Thermal drones have been procured from Pilibhit Tiger Reserve to search for the leopards. Meanwhile, tranquilizing experts who have come from Agra are also keeping watch here. To catch the leopards, the Forest Department team has identified locations across the entire area and set up 13 cages. Arrangements are being made for 20 more cages. However, despite all these efforts, the Forest Department team has so far been unsuccessful in catching the leopards. See 2 pictures When daughter reached field; leopard was mauling and eating mother On Monday, 3rd August, in Lallapur Piplasana village of Surjan Nagar police station area in Thakurdwara, a leopard mauled a woman to death in a sugarcane field. Santosh Devi, wife of Virendra Saini from the village, had gone to the field on Monday morning to collect green fodder for the cattle. During this time, the leopard attacked her. Santosh's daughter Sheetal said that the forest department is unable to catch the leopard. After 8 PM, the forest department teams also leave with their vehicles. After his mother's death, police and administration officials only gave assurances to the family. They have promised ₹5 lakh compensation, a job for one family member, and to catch the leopard soon. Attacked farmer on third day after killing woman After taking the life of a woman in Lalapur Peeplasana village on Monday, the leopard attacked a farmer on Wednesday morning in the Dilari area about 10 km away. Farmer Babu was removing sugarcane leaves in the field around 7:45 am. During this time, a leopard that emerged from the bushes suddenly attacked him. Hearing Babu's screams, nearby villagers reached the spot. Seeing the crowd of people, the leopard fled towards the forest. The farmer was seriously injured in the attack. Villagers took him to the Community Health Center. After primary treatment, he was referred to the district hospital in Moradabad. Farmers say - How can we bring fodder from the fields Farmers said that now they are afraid to go to the fields. It has also become difficult to bring fodder for the cattle. Officers come during the day. They give assurances and leave. At night, leopards roam around the village and nearby areas. Another farmer said that the forest department team sets up chairs on the roads during the day and sits there, but as soon as night falls, they leave from there. Posters warning about leopards put up on Kanwar route Due to the Kanwar Yatra, Kanwariyas are also passing through the Thakurdwara area. Keeping this in view, the police and forest department have put up posters at various places on the Kanwar route. These appeal to passersby to be cautious of leopards and wild animals. Police patrolling has also been increased along the entire route. Due to fear of leopards, villagers are avoiding going to their fields. Many families have also stopped sending their children to school for now. DM-SSP reached the village and took information about leopard rescue DM Rajendra Pensiya and SSP Satpal Antil reached Lalapur Peeplasana village on Saturday evening. They held a meeting and talked with the villagers. They appealed for cooperation in the campaign to capture the leopard. The officials instructed the forest department team to capture the leopard soon. The villagers assured full cooperation in the campaign. After this, the DM and SSP also checked the forest department's tranquilizer gun.
