stories.title: Mayawati's attack on BJP-AAP:Raises issues from Ravidas Gurughar wall demolition to unemployment, says ‘Govts focus on profiteering instead of public welfare’
stories.summary: Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) chief Mayawati criticised the BJP and the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) for allegedly politicising the name of Sant Ravidas. She said that when the holy Gurughar of Santguru Ravidas in Tughlakabad, Delhi, was demolished on August 10, 2019, the AAP was in power. Similarly, the government that demolished the wall of the Gurughar in Dhaleta village, Punjab, was also the AAP government, she said. In protest, members of the community across the country took to the streets democratically but had to face lathi charges, tear gas, arrests and legal cases. She said many people were also jailed during the movement. Now that elections are approaching, the AAP and BJP are organising various programmes in the name of Sant Ravidas for political gain, she alleged. Even today, devotees are forced to bow their heads in a tin shed Mayawati said society needs to remain vigilant against the politics of both parties. She appealed to people to spread the message of Sant Guru Ravidas's ideals of respect, equality and justice among the masses. The BSP chief said the land belonging to the Gurughar was also taken away, and even today, devotees are forced to visit and bow before Guruji in a temporary iron-sheet shed. She said this situation hurts the sentiments of millions of devotees and remains etched in the community's memory. She alleged that, with the Punjab elections approaching, the BJP was trying to divert the community from the goal of Begumpura by organising a Kalash Yatra in the name of Santguru Ravidas. Meanwhile, in the case involving the demolition of the Gurughar wall in Dhaleta village, Punjab, arrests were made when the Sangat and BSP raised their voices, she said. According to Mayawati, the AAP government later had to bow to pressure and rebuild the Gurughar. She appealed to society to remain vigilant against the politics of the BJP and AAP. She also called upon the Sangat to participate in the 'End of Subjugation and Resolution of Begumpura Santguru Ravidas Samman Yatra'. Policy to provide work to every hand is necessary Mayawati also targeted the central and state governments over issues including unemployment, inflation, poverty, illiteracy, the healthcare system, migration, women's insecurity, paper leaks and corruption. She said that during its tenure in Uttar Pradesh, the BSP had created around 2.25 lakh new government posts in the police and Panchayati Raj departments. Along with this, by lifting the ban on recruitment, government jobs were provided to lakhs of people from all sections of society. Mayawati said that even after being out of power, the BSP had long been demanding that the central and state governments take effective steps to address issues such as inflation, extreme poverty, unemployment, illiteracy, the deteriorating healthcare system, backwardness, forced migration, women's insecurity, paper leaks and corruption. However, she said, governments were not showing the expected seriousness on these issues. Vacant posts in government departments should be filled immediately Referring to the movement by unemployed youth, Mayawati said educated young men and women had made issues such as unemployment and an uncertain future a subject of national debate through a 36-day protest at Jantar Mantar in Delhi. In view of these problems, she said the central and state governments should immediately take steps in the interests of the poor, labourers, youth, women and other hardworking people. She said governments would have to pay special attention to government employment. Along with stopping the process of selling national assets to private hands, time-bound recruitment, free from paper leaks and corruption, should be launched for millions of vacant posts across all government departments. Mayawati said that if even one member of a family secures a government job, it would directly benefit millions of families. According to her, this would also provide social and economic security to SC, ST and OBC communities, which has been weakened by the ineffective implementation of reservation. Governments should abandon the mindset of profiteering The BSP chief said all governments should abandon profiteering and a business-oriented approach focused on making profits, and honestly implement the humanitarian and welfare policies and principles of the Constitution. She said a policy of 'work for every hand' could help address millions of problems in the interests of the country and its people. CJP makes unemployment a subject of serious debate Mayawati praised the movement of the 'Cockroach Janata Party (CJP)'. She said the organisation had made burning issues such as unemployment a subject of serious debate of national importance. Educated young men and women, troubled by an uncertain future, staged a 36-day protest at Jantar Mantar in Delhi. Its impact was so widespread, she claimed, that even the country's Education Minister had to lose his position. She told the central and state governments that they should now immediately focus on the real problems faced by around 125 crore poor people, labourers, youth, women and other hardworking citizens of the country. In particular, she called for concrete steps to create employment opportunities and secure the future of young people, while prioritising the concerns of millions of families suffering from unemployment. She also demanded an end to the ongoing deadlock in the current session of Parliament over issues concerning protesting students and unemployed youth at Jantar Mantar. Mayawati said these issues should be properly debated and discussed in Parliament so that the practice of government Bills becoming laws without adequate discussion could be stopped.

stories.title: ₹26 lakh BMW superbike seized in Kashi:Rider revved it to sound like gunfire, pleaded with cops, ‘I made a mistake’
stories.summary: Varanasi Police seized a BMW superbike worth ₹26 lakh after its rider allegedly spent the past 10 days riding through roads, neighbourhoods and residential colonies while making firing-like sounds with a modified silencer. According to complaints, whenever someone passed by the biker, he would make a loud, explosion-like sound, frightening people. After receiving several complaints, police had been searching for the rider. Late on Sunday night, police were conducting checks near Englishia Line. During the operation, the youth approached on his bike while making loud noises. Police stopped him and took him to the police station. After being caught, the youth began apologising to the police. He said, “Sir, I made a mistake... I will not do it again.” The incident took place in the Sigra police station area. Now read the full case in detail... Bike bought 15 days ago The arrested youth has been identified as Shivang, son of Satish Chand Maurya, a resident of Manduadih. He told police that he had bought the BMW bike around 15 days ago. He then had its silencer modified. He also said that he had not yet received the bike's number plate. Complaints had been coming in for a week Sigra Police Station in-charge Shivakant Mishra said complaints had been coming in for around a week about an expensive bike being ridden at high speed in the area and its silencer producing firing-like sounds. Residents were being disturbed by loud, explosion-like noises late at night. Following the complaints, police began searching for the rider. On Sunday night, while conducting checks near Englishia Line, police stopped the youth and brought him to the police station. No number plate; silencer also modified The investigation found that the bike was manufactured by BMW and was worth around ₹26 lakh. It did not have a number plate. Its silencer had also been modified, causing it to produce loud, firing-like noises and sparks. During questioning, Shivang admitted his mistake and apologised to the police. He assured them that he would not repeat it. Youth says, 'I made a mistake, please forgive me' Sigra Police Station in-charge Shivakant Mishra said- The young man has admitted his mistake. The bike has been seized for violating the Motor Vehicles Act and pollution-related rules. The young man was released after the necessary legal action.

stories.summary: The Tiranga Yatra has started in Gorakhpur under the leadership of Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath. The CM is walking on foot, holding the tricolor in his hand. A large number of people are also participating in the yatra with him. Great enthusiasm is visible among school children and women. Tricolors are being waved everywhere and 'Jai Shri Ram' slogans are echoing. Before the start of the yatra, the Chief Minister garlanded the statue of Mahatma Gandhi. After this, he joined the yatra holding the tricolor. The Chief Minister will walk about 3 kilometers. The yatra is now moving towards Yatayat Chauraha. Earlier, in his address, CM Yogi said, The tricolor is the mantra of freedom. He stated that it is the duty of every citizen to honor the brave heroes who made sacrifices. The CM also appealed to people to take the tricolor home and take selfies with it. The Chief Minister said that it is important to remember the contribution of the revolutionaries of the freedom movement. The tricolor is not just a flag, but the identity of the country's freedom and sacrifice.

stories.title: Huge crowd in Kashi, Mahakumbh-like arrangements:3 lakh devotees offer prayers; brother-in-law and sister-in-law die in Farrukhabad
stories.summary: Today is the second Monday of Sawan, and Shiva temples across Uttar Pradesh, including those in Varanasi, Ayodhya and Prayagraj, are witnessing huge crowds of devotees. Chants of ‘Har Har Mahadev’ can be heard across the state. Around 3 lakh devotees have so far had darshan of Baba Vishwanath. A 3-km-long queue has formed outside the temple. 3 lakh devotees visit Baba Vishwanath; 3-km queue outside temple ADCP Vaibhav Bangar said the Ganga Dwar has been closed due to the rising water level of the Ganga. This has led to larger crowds at the temple. As a result, arrangements similar to those made during the Maha Kumbh have been implemented. The lanes leading to the temple and ghats have been made one-way to manage the crowd. Devotees are getting only one second to perform Jalabhishek of Baba Vishwanath. On the second Monday of Sawan, Baba Vishwanath is giving darshan to devotees in his Gauri-Shankar form. The temple's CEO and SDM showered flower petals on devotees. The Baba Vishwanath Dham has been decorated with 50,000 flowers, while red carpets have been laid for devotees. Congress MP from Saharanpur, Imran Masood, showered flower petals on Kanwariyas. He also distributed fruit to them with his own hands and served them kheer. See pictures Two Kanwariyas killed after tractor-trolley runs them over in Barabanki In Barabanki, three young men travelling by motorcycle to Lodheswar Mahadeva temple for darshan were run over by a tractor-trolley. Two of them died, while the third suffered serious injuries. Kotwal Amit Singh carried the injured man in his arms to the vehicle and arranged for him to be taken to hospital. Devar-bhabhi killed in road accident while returning from Kanwar pilgrimage In Farrukhabad, a devar and his bhabhi died in a road accident late on Sunday night while returning from their Kanwar pilgrimage. The two were travelling by motorcycle to Mainpuri after collecting Ganga water for the Kanwar. A motorcycle suddenly collided with their bike, causing both of them to fall on the road. At the same time, a speeding pickup drove over their heads, killing them both.

stories.title: Abaan’s friends Umar, Zaid critical:One has ruptured lung, the other behaves strangely; Atiq’s son Ahzam recites Fateha at graves
stories.summary: Atiq's youngest son, Abaan, was laid to rest on Saturday, August 8, following his death in a road accident. The condition of his injured relatives, Umar and Zaid, has become critical. Umar was initially undergoing treatment at Ashutosh Hospital in Prayagraj. He has three broken ribs, fractures in his arms and legs, and severe lung problems. Doctors suspect that his lung has ruptured. On Saturday evening, when his condition deteriorated significantly, he was shifted to Medanta Hospital in Delhi. He underwent surgery on Sunday. The condition of the other injured person, Zaid, is also critical. His condition worsened on Sunday morning, after which he was taken to Delhi and shifted to the Military Hospital. Zaid has two broken ribs, a fractured arm and fractures in both legs, along with a wound near his neck. He also suffered a severe head injury and has been speaking incoherently and behaving unusually. Zaid was initially admitted to Aman Hospital in the city. On the doctors' advice, he was shifted to Delhi for further treatment for his brain injury. The condition of the third friend, Farooq Ahjam, who was travelling in the car, is stable. He suffered injuries to his hands and feet, along with minor wounds at several places. He has been admitted to Kareli Hospital. On the second day after Abaan's burial, brother Ahjam visits his grave On Sunday, Abaan's brother Ahjam once again visited his brother's grave and offered Fatiha. Relatives and friends were also present with him. Ahjam offered Fatiha not only at Abaan's grave, but also at the graves of his father Atiq, brother Asad and uncle Ashraf. Among Muslims, family members traditionally visit a grave to recite Fatiha on the second and third days after burial. They then visit after Friday prayers and recite Fatiha again on the 40th day. Ahjam spends time at his aunt's house and in the mosque A mournful atmosphere prevailed in Hatwa after Abaan's burial. On Sunday, people continued arriving from morning until evening to meet Ahjam and offer condolences to the family. Ahjam spent most of his time at his aunt's house or in the mosque. The village's main mosque is only around 100 metres from the house where Abaan's body had been kept. Ahjam would sit at home with friends and relatives before going to the mosque, where he would spend time. People who came to meet and console him also met him at the mosque. Ashraf's daughters call out to Ali and Umar, but police stop them from meeting On Saturday, Ali, who is lodged in Jhansi jail, and Umar, who is lodged in Prayagraj jail, arrived on parole to attend the funeral of their younger brother Abaan. During the burial at Kasari Masari cemetery, members of the Atiq family appeared emotional in the presence of Umar, Ali and Ahjam. At one point in the cemetery, three children of their late uncle Ashraf stood as the funeral procession passed. When Umar and Ali walked a few steps away, Ashraf's 12-year-old daughter Swaliha called out, "Brother." Umar and Ali recognised her voice in the crowd and suddenly stopped. Swaliha was with her 10-year-old younger sister Alia and seven-year-old brother Abdullah. Umar quickly picked Abdullah up in his arms. Both brothers kissed his forehead. Meanwhile, as the two girls began moving towards Umar and Ali, police stopped them. An IPS officer told them, “Meet only according to the High Court's order.” Umar told the policemen, "Hey, she's my little sister." However, the police replied, "No... meeting everyone is not allowed." Umar and Ali became emotional. Their sisters also began crying, but the police did not allow them to meet. Ali gets angry at police restrictions; Umar calms him down Another emotional moment occurred at Kasari Masari cemetery when Ali became angry over the police restrictions. Umar immediately hugged him and calmed him down. After Abaan's burial, Umar and Ali put soil on the grave. The police then asked Ali to move away. Ali loudly said, "Hey, let us recite the Fatiha!" Seeing Ali become angry, the crowd also began making noise. Umar immediately hugged him and said, “Have patience... be quiet.” As the crowd grew louder, Umar put his finger to his lips and signalled everyone to remain silent. Abaan was travelling to Jhansi jail to meet his brother when he died in road accident Abaan died in a road accident in Jhansi on Thursday morning, August 6. He was travelling from Prayagraj to meet his brother Ali, who is lodged in Jhansi jail. He was travelling in a Creta car with four friends. At around 10.30am, the car hit a divider on the highway while the driver was trying to avoid an animal. Abaan and his friend Sonu died in the accident, while three others were injured. The bodies of Abaan and Sonu were brought from Jhansi to Hatwa village in Prayagraj in the same ambulance at around 4am on Friday. Abaan was laid to rest at 7pm on Saturday, August 8. Was travelling with friends and relatives to meet Ali in jail Sonu, who died alongside Abaan, was his friend and a resident of Hatwa. He regularly spent time with Abaan and the others as a close friend. Umar, who was injured in the accident, is also a resident of Hatwa and a close relative of the Atiq family. After the houses in Chakia were demolished, Abaan, Ahjam and other family members began living at Umar's house in Hatwa. Umar was regularly with Abaan and Ahjam. Farooq, who was injured, was a friend of Ahjam and Abaan. He is a resident of Mohatsiganj. His father, Mohammad Farooq, worked in the office of Atiq's PA. He has also previously been jailed. Mohammad Zaid, who was injured, is a relative of Atiq. He is the son-in-law of Atiq's sister and was also regularly with Ahjam and Abaan.

stories.title: Ram Mandir donation theft case:Champat Rai back in race for general secretary post after VHP's clean chit, seers' backing
stories.summary: Champat Rai, who resigned as general secretary of the Ram Mandir Trust after allegations surfaced in connection with the alleged theft of temple donations, is once again being considered for the post. According to sources, Rai was given a clean chit at the Vishva Hindu Parishad's (VHP) national meeting in Delhi on July 22. The following day, several prominent seers in Ayodhya held a meeting in his support and demanded that he be reappointed as general secretary. Since then, Rai has been meeting seers and mahants regularly. He has been visiting temples, discussing the management of the Ram Temple and seeking to rebuild confidence in his leadership. Seers: If investigation clears Rai, he should return Swami Rajkumar Das, head of Ramvallabhakunj and a member of the Ram Mandir's religious committee, said Rai was considered innocent by the seer community. "If he is cleared in all the investigations, it would be welcome if he is appointed general secretary again," Das said. He said Rai's return would help strengthen the management of the Ram Temple and serve the interests of the Sanatan community. Das also highlighted Rai's contribution to the Ram Mandir movement and its construction, both alongside the late Ashok Singhal and after his death. Seers met in Ayodhya a day after VHP meeting The VHP held its national meeting in Delhi on July 22. The following day, on July 23, prominent seers from Ayodhya gathered at the Tulsidas Naturopathy Hospital premises of the Maniram Das Chhawani Trust. The meeting was held in support of Rai. Those present included Mahant Kamal Nayan Das, Swami Rajkumar Das, Mahant Mithilesh Nandini Sharan, Akhara Parishad spokesperson Mahant Sanjay Das, Vaishnav Akhara Parishad spokesperson Mahant Gaurishankar Das, Tulsidas Chhawani Mahant Janardan Das and Ramkachahari Mahant Shashikant Das, among others. During the meeting, the seers highlighted Rai's contribution to the Ram Mandir movement and described the allegations against him as a conspiracy. They also called for his reappointment as general secretary of the Ram Mandir Trust. Rai's supporters seek backing from seers Sources said people close to Rai had approached seers and mahants at various temples and sought their support for him. The sources claimed the atmosphere changed after the campaign for his support gained momentum. They also said opposition to Rai within the VHP eased after signals from senior leadership. The seers subsequently focused on Rai's contribution to the Ram Mandir movement and described the allegations against him as an alleged conspiracy. Rai's supporters have also pointed to his age of 81 and claims that he does not maintain bank accounts. According to people close to him, Rai is also planning to give up his share of his ancestral property. They said this is his only property and that he may soon transfer it to his brother through a legal registration. No decision on September 2 expected Rai could be given charge of the Ram Mandir Trust's general secretary post again within the next two to three months, according to sources. The Trust had deferred the appointment at its July 19 meeting. Its next meeting is scheduled for September 2. However, sources said the Trust is unlikely to take a final decision on the general secretary's post at that meeting either. Acting general secretary Krishnamohan also active Meanwhile, acting general secretary Dr Krishnamohan has stepped up his activities. He has been visiting the Ram Mandir to review its arrangements and holding discussions with members of the religious committee to improve its functioning. Six days ago, he visited the Ayodhya branch of the State Bank of India to review the Trust's bank accounts and locker arrangements. Bajrang Lal Bagda also in contention VHP international general secretary Bajrang Lal Bagda is also being discussed as a possible candidate for the post. Bagda was appointed international general secretary of the VHP in February 2024. As a result, Rai and Bagda are currently the two names being discussed for the general secretary's position. Rai observing silence during Chaturmas Amid the allegations linked to the donation theft case, Rai is staying at the Teerth Kshetra Bhawan in Ayodhya and observing a period of silence during Chaturmas. Sources claim that efforts could be made to restore his reputation after the vow ends. The authorities are currently awaiting the final report of the Special Investigation Team (SIT), which is investigating the alleged donation theft. Meanwhile, Rai has remained in Ayodhya and continues to express his views on decisions related to the Trust, according to sources. Eight arrested on June 25; Rai resigned the next day Rai and Ram Temple Trust trustee Dr Anil Mishra resigned on June 26 in connection with the donation theft case. The first FIR was registered late on June 25 following a complaint by Trust member Krishna Mohan. The FIR did not name Rai, Mishra or other senior Trust officials. Later that night, eight people, including Ramshankar Yadav alias Tinnu, were arrested.

stories.title: Why do Samajwadi Party Congress want to weaken Owaisi?:AIMIM got twice the votes of SP candidates' losing margins on several 2022 UP seats
stories.summary: With six months to go before the Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections, Asaduddin Owaisi's All India Majlis-e-Ittehadul Muslimeen (AIMIM) has started strengthening its presence in Muslim-dominated areas of western UP. Over the past one-and-a-half months, Owaisi has held four major rallies in Bahraich, Bijnor, Saharanpur and Moradabad — areas traditionally considered strongholds of the Samajwadi Party (SP) among Muslim voters. Muslim MLAs from the SP represent these areas. The crowds at Owaisi's rallies and his aggressive speeches have raised concerns within opposition parties, particularly the SP. The SP and Congress are now reportedly trying to bring influential Muslim leaders from AIMIM into their camps. AIMIM diverted Muslim votes from SP in 2022 AIMIM contested 97 of Uttar Pradesh's 403 Assembly seats in the 2022 elections and secured a vote share of 0.49%. Although its statewide vote share was small, the party secured between 5,000 and 25,000 votes in several constituencies where it had focused its campaign. In at least seven to eight seats, the SP's losing margin was significantly smaller than the number of votes secured by AIMIM candidates. In other words, had AIMIM not contested those seats, or had some of its votes gone to the SP, the party could have won several of these closely fought contests. Who are the AIMIM leaders on SP-Congress radar? National spokesperson Asim Waqar leads the list AIMIM national spokesperson Asim Waqar has recently appeared to take a softer position towards the INDIA bloc and Congress leader Rahul Gandhi. During a television debate, he described Rahul Gandhi as a potential future Prime Minister. He also responded to attacks on SP chief Akhilesh Yadav by Om Prakash Rajbhar. When Dainik Bhaskar asked Waqar about his political future, he did not rule out the possibility of moving to another party, although he did not openly confirm any such plan either. SP in touch with AIMIM district presidents in western UP The SP and Congress are reportedly keeping an eye on AIMIM district presidents in Saharanpur, Moradabad, Rampur and Meerut. A switch by these leaders could potentially bring parts of their local organisational networks with them. Moradabad AIMIM district president Wasim Mohid Farghani said Owaisi himself had offered an alliance to the SP. "Our aim is to raise our voice against injustice faced by Muslims. However, I cannot say anything at present about whether I would join the SP or Congress in the future," he said. Rampur AIMIM district president Farid-uz-Zafar said the SP was giving representation to Muslims, but its representatives were unable to raise the community's concerns strongly. "Nobody knows what turn politics will take," he said. Saharanpur AIMIM district president Wasim said the party would contest the election strongly under Owaisi's leadership. "However, members of my family have previously been associated with the SP and Congress. Nobody knows what circumstances may arise in the future," he said. Owaisi takes aggressive line on Muslim issues, draws Gen Z crowds Jaigam Murtaza, who tracks Muslim politics in western UP, said Owaisi had hurt the SP's prospects in the 2022 Assembly elections. He said the SP lost several seats in Muslim-dominated constituencies by margins of 5,000 to 10,000 votes, where AIMIM candidates had divided the Muslim vote. In western UP, the SP-Rashtriya Lok Dal (RLD) alliance had expected a consolidation of Muslim and Jat votes. However, AIMIM candidates split the Muslim vote in several constituencies, allowing BJP-led candidates to win closely fought contests. Owaisi has become active six months ahead of the 2027 election. A significant number of young, including Gen Z voters, have attended his rallies. Murtaza said this was significant because both Akhilesh Yadav and Rahul Gandhi were trying to attract young voters. Owaisi has largely focused his rallies on Muslim-majority constituencies. He has accused the SP of taking Muslim votes but failing to take a strong stand on issues concerning Muslim leaders, including Azam Khan, and the wider community. AIMIM's political footprint in UP is growing Political analysts say AIMIM still faces several challenges in Uttar Pradesh, but its electoral footprint has expanded since it first contested the state Assembly election in 2017. The party fielded candidates in 38 constituencies in 2017 and secured a vote share of 0.24%. Its candidates, however, lost their deposits in most of the seats they contested. In the 2022 Assembly election, AIMIM contested around 95-97 seats and secured more than 450,000 votes. Its vote share rose to around 0.49%. The party has also made gains beyond Assembly elections. In the 2023 urban local body elections, AIMIM won five municipal or panchayat chairperson posts and 77 councillor seats. In the Meerut mayoral election, AIMIM's candidate came close to winning and finished second, ahead of the SP. The party's growing political presence has prompted both the SP and Congress to consider their strategies ahead of the 2027 election. What do SP and Congress say? SP: 'We welcome people with a secular ideology' SP spokesperson Azam Khan said the party would welcome AIMIM leaders if they shared its secular outlook. "If people with a secular ideology join us, they are welcome. We do not support politics based on any religion, whether it is Hindu or Muslim. Anyone who stands with the Constitution and social justice is welcome in the party," he said. He added that the SP would stand with anyone fighting against what he described as the exploitation of young people. Congress: 'It would be good if Asim Waqar joins' Congress spokesperson Surendra Rajput said the party would welcome AIMIM spokesperson Asim Waqar if he decided to join Congress. "Whether AIMIM leaders will join Congress is a matter for the party leadership to decide based on their suitability. If the leadership seeks our opinion about any leader, we will certainly give it," he said. Owaisi's four rallies and the SP's Muslim MLAs Bahraich — Matera Owaisi began his campaign on June 14 by announcing AIMIM state president Shaukat Ali as the party's Assembly candidate from Matera. SP's Maria Shah is the sitting MLA from the constituency. She is the wife of former minister Yasar Shah. Organisers claimed around 80,000 people attended Owaisi's rally. Bijnor — Najibabad At a 'Paigham-e-Ittehad' programme on June 29, Owaisi targeted the SP, BSP and Congress. SP's Tasleem Ahmed is the sitting MLA from Najibabad. Organisers claimed that around 80,000 to 100,000 people attended the rally. Saharanpur At his July 18 rally in Saharanpur, Owaisi raised issues ranging from Azam Khan's Jauhar University to Muslim political representation. The constituency has two SP Muslim MLAs, Ashu Malik and Umar Khan. His aggressive speech was followed by loud slogans from the crowd. Moradabad At the July 25 rally in Moradabad, organisers claimed that more than 50,000 people attended. It was here that Owaisi made an open offer of an alliance to the SP, saying it was time to talk now and warning the party not to regret the decision after the election. The SP has so far not held any talks with Owaisi over an alliance.

stories.title: Flood hits 40 villages in Farrukhabad, people sleep on roads:Families say lifetime savings destroyed; rain alert issued across UP’s 75 districts
stories.summary: Rainfall in the hills has caused 10 rivers, including the Ganga and Yamuna, to swell across Uttar Pradesh. In Farrukhabad and Bijnor, Ganga water is flowing over the highways, while several roads have been submerged. Around 40 villages are in the grip of flooding, with dozens of villages cut off and turned into islands. Residents have been forced to leave their villages and homes and live in tents along the roads. Many are also being forced to sleep on the roads at night. In Farrukhabad, 21 houses have already been swallowed by the Ganga. Residents are demolishing other houses that have come under threat from riverbank erosion themselves, so they can salvage materials such as bricks and steel rods and reuse them to rebuild their homes once the situation improves. Women broke down in tears as they watched their houses being demolished. Crying, they said, 'We built our home by saving every penny, but the flood has destroyed our life's earnings. Where will we go now?' Yamuna reaches ghat steps in Mathura; routes submerged in Vrindavan The water level of the Yamuna has reached the steps of the ghats in Mathura. The parikrama route at Keshi Ghat has been submerged in Vrindavan. Devotees are wading through around one foot of water to complete the parikrama. Around 25 km from Kanpur city, the water level of the Ganga has reached the Brahmavart Ghat. At the 'Brahma Ki Khunti' temple, the khunti has been submerged. Ganga water has reached Manikarnika Ghat in Kashi. The routes connecting all 84 ghats have been submerged. Flood hits Saharanpur after heavy rain; Delhi-Yamunotri Highway submerged Meanwhile, Saharanpur received such heavy rainfall on Monday that the Gangarav River suddenly went into spate. The bridge built over the river was damaged. River water began flowing over the Delhi-Yamunotri Highway. Three to four feet of water accumulated on roads and in residential colonies. Water also entered homes and shops, while cars and motorcycles were half-submerged. Rain alert issued for all 75 districts; heavy rain possible in Lalitpur and Mahoba The Meteorological Department has issued a rain alert for all 75 districts of Uttar Pradesh today. Heavy rain is possible in Lalitpur and Mahoba. Compared with last year, the state has received 136 mm less rainfall since June 1. By August 9 last year, Uttar Pradesh had received 437 mm of rain, which was 2% above normal. This year, the state has received 341 mm so far, which is 20% below normal. See photos of rainfall and floods- Monsoon to remain more active in southern UP for next three days Lucknow meteorologist Atul Kumar Singh said- The low-pressure area that had formed over south-western Uttar Pradesh has now weakened. The monsoon trough is extending from Delhi and Agra towards the east-central Bay of Bengal. In addition, another low-pressure area formed over south West Bengal and adjoining northern Odisha is moving north-westwards. In such a situation, the monsoon will remain more active in the southern parts of Uttar Pradesh over the next three days.

stories.title: Gen Z makes up 15% of UP voters:Just 3% vote shift could decide the government; BJP plans youth outreach strategy
stories.summary: With the Uttar Pradesh Assembly election only six months away, political parties are turning their attention to Gen Z voters, who account for around 15% of the state's electorate. Past election trends show that governments in Uttar Pradesh can be made or unmade by relatively small differences in vote share. If even 3-5% of Gen Z voters shift their preference, it could have a major impact on the electoral outcome. The BJP, Samajwadi Party (SP), Congress and Chandrashekhar Azad's party are all working on strategies to win over young voters. Here is a look at how small differences in vote share have translated into large differences in seats in previous elections, and what political parties are doing to attract Gen Z. 3.24% higher vote share gave SP a majority in 2012 The 2012 Assembly election saw a direct contest between the Samajwadi Party and the Bahujan Samaj Party. The SP secured 29.15% of the vote, just 3.24 percentage points more than the BSP's 25.91%. Yet, that relatively small difference translated into a huge gap in seats. The SP won 224 seats, while the BSP managed only 80 — a difference of 144 seats. The BJP secured around 15% of the vote and won 47 seats. 7.22% more votes gave NDA 148 extra seats in 2022 The 2022 Assembly election produced a similar pattern. The BJP-led NDA secured 43.82% of the vote and won 273 seats. The SP-led alliance received 36.60% of the vote and won 125 seats. A difference of 7.22 percentage points in vote share therefore translated into a gap of 148 seats. Gen Z could influence the outcome in 80-120 seats The recent mobilisation of Gen Z has increased political parties' focus on this voter group. Uttar Pradesh has around 13 crore voters, of whom an estimated 2.07 crore, or 15%, belong to Gen Z. If even a substantial section of these voters votes as a single bloc, they could potentially influence the outcome in 80-120 Assembly constituencies. In the 2022 Assembly election, 99 seats were decided by margins ranging from 1,000 to 10,000 votes. The BJP won 55 of these seats and the SP 35. The Rashtriya Lok Dal won three, while the NISHAD Party and Suheldev Bharatiya Samaj Party won two each. The Congress and BSP won one seat each. Young voters pose a major challenge for ruling BJP Sanjay Singh, an office-bearer of the Association for Democratic Reforms (ADR), which analyses election data, said Gen Z voters would remain a major challenge in the 99 seats won by margins of less than 10,000 votes in the 2027 election. "The BJP is in power, so the challenge before it is how effectively it can connect with young voters," he said. Singh also pointed to a decline in support for the BJP among young voters over successive elections. According to his research, around 85% of young voters supported the BJP in the 2014 Lok Sabha election. The figure fell to around 70% in 2019 and further to 50-55% in 2024. He said this represented a decline of around 30-35 percentage points in three elections. Gen Z makes its own political choices Lucknow-based educationist Pankaj Agrawal said Gen Z does not have an established political leader or party and is instead heavily influenced by Instagram and wider social media trends. Thousands of young people took to the streets to protest issues such as the NEET paper leak and new UGC rules, showing that they were willing to raise concerns about their future without relying on political parties, he said. Agrawal also pointed to protests at Jantar Mantar, where young people from families that support the BJP or the RSS also joined demonstrations against government policies. "This shows that young people can make political choices independent of their family's views," he said. How political parties plan to win over Gen Z BJP and RSS plan direct engagement with young voters Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath is expected to hold direct interactions with Gen Z voters. Students pursuing professional courses at different universities will be invited to participate. The proposed interactions will be two-way, with students also getting an opportunity to ask questions and raise their concerns with the Chief Minister. The Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) has divided Uttar Pradesh into two regions — east and west. Regional RSS functionaries will visit universities to interact with Gen Z, understand their concerns and assess their expectations. The findings from these interactions will be shared with the government and BJP organisation to help shape their future strategy. BJP plans youth advisory committees The BJP also plans to create "Youth Advisory Committees" to establish a direct channel between young people and the government. The committees will include youth representatives, student leaders, competitive-exam aspirants, young entrepreneurs and social-media influencers. The initiative will initially operate at district level, with plans to expand it to the block level. The aim is to ensure that issues affecting young people reach MLAs and the government directly. BJP trains leaders to connect through social media The BJP is also training its representatives and leaders to communicate with young voters through reels, social media trends and X. The objective is to receive quick feedback on issues such as employment and competitive examinations and communicate the party's position directly to young people. SP focuses on influencers and young MPs Akhilesh meets more than 200 influencers SP chief Akhilesh Yadav has held a meeting with more than 200 digital content creators and influencers from across Uttar Pradesh. The party wants to reduce its dependence on traditional media and reach young voters directly through YouTube, Instagram and Facebook. The strategy includes providing influencers with data and facts on issues such as paper leaks, unemployment and inflation so they can create content around them. The party also plans to use local languages and dialects to connect with young people in rural areas and small towns. For the 2027 election, the SP is planning a dedicated digital war room to coordinate with content creators and build support for the party online. SP promotes its young MPs SP MPs Pushpendra Saroj and Priya Saroj, among the youngest MPs in the party, are also being promoted heavily on social media. Reels and short videos highlighting their speeches and comments on youth-related issues such as Agniveer, student protests and paper leaks are being circulated. Short documentaries focusing on their struggles and political journeys are also being shared to help first-time voters connect with them. Congress plans direct youth outreach Rahul Gandhi to hold more youth interactions Rahul Gandhi interacted with students in Prayagraj on August 8 as part of the party's youth outreach programme. Congress spokesperson CP Rai said around 1.74 lakh students had registered online for the "Goonj" programme. He said Rahul Gandhi is expected to hold similar interactions in two to three more districts of Uttar Pradesh. NSUI and Youth Congress to expand membership The Congress is also planning dedicated programmes to bring more Gen Z voters into the party. According to the party spokesperson, its Uttar Pradesh in-charge will interact with young people in different districts. The party has also asked its youth organisations, the National Students' Union of India (NSUI) and Youth Congress, to focus on expanding membership in colleges and universities. Social media could decide the youth vote Gen Z is less likely to be influenced by traditional rallies and political speeches and more likely to respond to the social-media environment around an issue. For political parties, the challenge is therefore not simply to reach young voters but to address the issues that directly affect them — employment, competitive examinations, education, inflation and their future prospects. The party that gets this balance right could gain a crucial advantage in the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly election.

stories.title: Man takes selfie with 11-month-old daughter, throws her into Yamuna:Couple fought on moving bike; girl’s birthday was 3 days away
stories.summary: A father threw his 11-month-old daughter into the Yamuna after a fight with his wife in Agra. Before this, he also took a selfie with his daughter. After throwing his daughter, the father started pushing his wife into the river. When the woman screamed, a crowd of people passing by on the bridge gathered. Passersby somehow rescued his wife by freeing her from the husband. The wife said - We were going to Agra to buy clothes for our daughter. Her birthday was three days later, on 17 August. On the way, my husband stopped the bike on the bridge on the pretext of taking photos. After that, he threw our daughter into the river. After hearing the woman's account, the passersby severely beat up the accused husband. After that, they handed him over to the police. The incident occurred on Friday at 3 PM at Akbara Bridge in Sikandra. A video of this has also surfaced on social media. 2 images related to the incident Now read the complete case Rinku, a resident of Badmaghi village in Baldev, was going to the market on a bike with his wife Lakshmi and their 11-month-old daughter. On the way, he got into an argument with his wife over something. Rinku suddenly stopped the bike on Akbara bridge. He told his wife that he wanted to take a photo with their daughter. Rinku took a selfie with his daughter. Immediately after this, he threw his daughter into the Yamuna River. As soon as his wife ran to the bridge railing, Rinku started pushing her into the river as well. But when Lakshmi raised an alarm, passersby on the bridge gathered at the spot. Husband became aggressive when people beat him Lakshmi told the passersby that her husband had thrown their daughter into the Yamuna. Now, he is trying to push me into the river too. As soon as people heard this, they became enraged. After rescuing the wife from her husband, they started beating him. During this, Rinku also became aggressive towards the people. Upon receiving information, the police team reached the spot. The accused Rinku was taken into custody and sent to the police station. Meanwhile, a search operation has been started in the Yamuna River to find the child. Wife said - We were going to Agra to buy clothes for daughter Laxmi said, ‘’My marriage took place on 14 June, 2024. After marriage, I started being harassed for dowry. My in-laws threw me out of the house. I stayed at my maternal home in the village of Jatoli Kadmi Deeg, Bharatpur for 6 months. After that, my husband called me back. He was not happy about having a daughter. He used to quarrel every day. For the past two to three days, Rinku's behavior had changed. He was pretending to love the child. Today he said, let's go to Agra. We need to buy clothes for the child. As soon as we reached Yamuna Bridge, Rinku stopped the bike. He said he wanted to take photos with the child.'' 'Husband killed only daughter before her birthday' Mother Laxmi said that I had only one daughter. Her birthday was on 17 August. My husband Rinku took my daughter's life before that. I had no idea that he was planning to kill the child. DCP City Syed Ali Abbas said - In the Sikandra area, a man threw his daughter into the Yamuna from a bridge. PAC divers have been deployed into the river. The divers are conducting a search operation in the river for the girl. The accused husband is being interrogated regarding the incident. Domestic discord has emerged during the investigation.

stories.title: Naib tehsildar’s car runs over grandfather-grandson, kills both:Angry crowd surrounds vehicle in Hathras; police rescue staff
stories.summary: A road accident occurred on Friday around 7 PM on the Mathura-Bareilly National Highway in Hathras. The vehicle of the Naib Tehsildar of Sikandra Rau collided with two oncoming motorcycles. A grandfather and his 6-year-old grandson riding on one motorcycle died on the spot in the accident. Meanwhile, the youth riding on the second motorcycle was seriously injured. The police have taken him to the hospital. The bodies have been sent for post-mortem. Angry people blocked the road, after the accident. The police cleared the traffic after persuading them. The incident is from near Salempur village in the Hathras Junction police station area. Now know the complete matter 56-year-old Subhash Chandra, a resident of village Thulai, was a farmer. He had a 6-year-old grandson named Daksh. On Friday evening, both were returning to the village on a bike. Subhash was riding the bike, and Daksh was sitting with him. During this time, the vehicle of the Naib Tehsildar, coming from the opposite direction, collided with their bike. Subhash and Daksh died on the spot after the collision. Meanwhile, Sonu from the same village, who was riding another bike, was seriously injured. The police took him to the district hospital, from where doctors referred him to Aligarh in critical condition. Both bodies were sent for post-mortem. Villagers surrounded the vehicle and created a commotion After the accident, a large number of villagers gathered at the spot. They surrounded the Naib Tehsildar's vehicle and started a commotion. During this time, the vehicle was also vandalized. The villagers raised slogans against the police and administration. They also had an altercation with the officials present at the spot. Police rescued officers and employees from the crowd As soon as the information was received, police reached the spot. Police safely evacuated the Naib Tehsildar and other employees from the crowd. Considering the situation, police force from several stations was called to the spot. Upon receiving information about the incident, Additional District Magistrate Sadar and Additional District Magistrate Sasni, along with other officers, also reached. Villagers blocked the highway for some time. Officers pacified them by counseling, after which the jam was cleared. Police have sent both bodies for post-mortem and have started an investigation into the accident.

stories.title: ATS picks up 2 suspects from Hapur mosque:Siblings in Kanpur under suspicion of Pakistan links; major action ahead of 15 August
stories.summary: UP ATS and the Central Intelligence Agency detained four suspicious individuals in Kanpur Dehat and Hapur a day before Independence Day. Two people were apprehended from each location. The first operation took place in the Bahadurgarh area of Hapur on Friday around 5 AM. The UP ATS team detained two suspicious youths from a mosque. Both had arrived at the mosque on a bike. Shortly after, the ATS team reached the mosque. Both were taken to Meerut for interrogation. The second operation took place in Bara village of Kanpur Dehat on Wednesday. Here, the Central Agency team detained a brother and sister. The team searched the house for about 30 minutes and confiscated mobile phones of all family members. Kanpur Dehat police received information about this on Friday. In both cases, there is suspicion that the suspects have contact with Pakistan and are involved in monetary transactions. However, no official confirmation of any suspect's Pakistani connection has been made yet. First, know about the action in Hapur Dehat According to the Masjid Intazamiya Committee, both youths arrived at the Qureshiyan Mosque located in Sherpur village under Bahadurgarh police station area on a bike around 5 am on Friday. They parked their bike outside the mosque and went inside. Just 10 minutes later, the ATS Meerut team arrived. Both were taken into custody. Both youths had reached the mosque without any prior acquaintance. According to local people, they have been identified as Mohammad Sameer and Salman. Information has been received that both work in a local factory. However, their identity and the reason for reaching the mosque have not been officially confirmed. According to local people, the ATS team reached there just a few minutes after both reached the mosque. This suggests that the agency was already monitoring their activities. However, no official information has been given by the police or ATS in this regard. Police said- The situation will be clear after investigation Security agencies are gathering information about the identity of both youths, their local contacts, purpose of reaching the mosque, and recent activities. Their mobile phones and items found with them are also being examined. Bahadurgarh police station in-charge Indrakant Yadav informed that information has been received through social media about two suspicious youths being caught at Qureshiyan Mosque in Sherpur village. Both are said to be residents of another area. ATS has taken them into custody. The matter is being investigated. Now know about the action in Kanpur Dehat On Wednesday morning, a team from security and intelligence agencies arrived in three vehicles at Bara village in Akbarpur Kotwali area. The team searched the house of Bakar Khan (30) and his sister Uruj Fatima (32) for about 30 minutes. After this, both were taken into custody and taken to Delhi for questioning. Mobile phones of other family members have also been seized for examination. Local police received information about the case on Friday. According to sources, agencies suspect that Bakar Khan and Uruj Fatima have contacts with Pakistan. Allegations of money transactions with Pakistan against both are also being investigated. It has emerged that investigating agencies found suspicious chats in their mobile phones and digital activities. Agencies are trying to find out who they were in contact with and what their relationship is with people present in Pakistan. Pakistani citizens also own land in Bara village Bakar Khan's mother said that on Wednesday around 6:30 AM, about 10 people arrived at their house in three vehicles. They showed their identity cards and said they had come from Delhi. After that, the officials started searching the house. They checked every single item kept in the house. They also checked the mobile phones of family members. After searching for about 30 minutes, the officials took Bakar Khan and Uruj Fatima along with their mobile phones with them. The team also confiscated the mobile phone of their younger daughter. The mother says that it has been about 60 hours since both were taken away, but the family has not received any information about them. Many people from Bara village have relatives living in Pakistan. Some Pakistani citizens also own land in the village, which has now been declared enemy property. It is being reported that local families cultivate this land. SP said - We don't have information about the case yet Kanpur Dehat SP Shraddha Narendra Pandey said that- A team from the Central Agency had come. While investigating a case, the team took both Bakar Khan and Uruj Fatima along with them. What the case is about, we don't have information about it. Kanpur Dehat Police received information about the case through ATS Kanpur Unit. After which the local police is also investigating the matter

stories.title: ‘How dare it bite me’:Man bites cobra after killing it; snake had bitten him three times
stories.summary: A young man confronted a cobra under the influence of alcohol in Barabanki. The snake bit the young man three times. Even after this, the young man did not let go of the snake. He wrapped it around his wrist. The snake kept biting the young man, but he did not release it. He killed the snake and then tried to bite it with his mouth. Neighbors kept trying to get the snake away from the young man, but he did not agree. On one side, 4-5 people were pulling the snake; on the other side was the young man. He was muttering angrily...how dare it bite me. The incident occurred on Thursday at 8 pm; the video surfaced on Friday. First see 2 pictures... Cobra emerged from neighbor's house In the village of Bairanaamau Manjhari in Mohammadpur Khala, Sanjay (35), son of Sonelal, lives with his family. The family includes two children, his parents, and a sister. His wife has passed away. The young man is a farmer. On Thursday around 8 PM, a cobra snake emerged at neighbor Chandar Yadav's house. Sonelal arrived intoxicated and started trying to catch the snake. Roamed around village with dead snake in hand Even after being bitten three times by the snake, Sanjay did not relent. He caught the snake and killed it with a stick. He started roaming around the house with the dead snake in his hand. Seeing him roam like this, crowd gathered. Neighbors stopped Sanjay and advised him to get treatment. A video of the incident has also surfaced, in which Sanjay's sister Rekha and some villagers are trying to make him release the snake, but he is not ready to let it go. Attempted to bite the dead snake In an intoxicated state, Sanjay was repeatedly saying, 'This will bite me; how dare it.' People kept trying to explain, but he was not ready to listen to anyone. Sanjay even tried to bite the dead snake with his teeth. According to the villagers, the snake was about three and a half feet long. Village head representative Sher Bahadur, Ramchander, RK Chauhan, Ramlakhan, Baithu, and Subedar, along with others, identified the snake as a cobra. The youth's family members and villagers somehow calmed him down. Even after being bitten by the snake three times, Sanjay was not ready to go to the hospital. Reached CHC after an hour; doctors sent him home The village head was informed about the incident about an hour after the snake bite. After this, the village head immediately took the youth along with his family members to CHC Suratganj. Doctors gave him an anti-venom injection and administered glucose. He was sent home after his condition became normal. According to villagers, the police were not informed about the incident. CHC Superintendent Dr. Rajarshi Tripathi said that such actions should not be taken after a snake bite. After a snake bite, one should immediately go to the hospital without wasting time. The youth was sent home after his condition became normal.

stories.title: Teacher dies inside car:Wife breaks down, daughter cries, ‘Papa, wake up, let’s go home’
stories.summary: A government teacher died while sitting in his car in Sitapur. His body was found around 10 AM on Friday morning, in the seat next to the driver in a car parked by the roadside. The car door was open. Seeing the car parked for a long time, nearby shopkeepers became suspicious. They went closer, called out, and shook the body, but there was no movement. Upon receiving information, the police arrived at the scene. Shortly after, the wife and daughter of teacher Radheshyam Patel (50) arrived at the scene. Seeing her husband's body, the wife became distraught. She clung to the body and started crying. The daughter, crying, said - 'Dad, you just left home, please get up and let's go home.' Death is suspected to be due to a heart attack. Police have sent the body for post-mortem. The incident occurred near the Fire Brigade Office in the city Kotwali area. See two pictures related to the incident Going to school by car, it got a puncture on the way Radheshyam Patel, a resident of Ismailpur locality in Kotwali Dehat, was a teacher at the aided school Janata Madhyamik Vidyalaya Sonari. Besides his wife Anuradha Patel, the family includes a daughter Yashasvi (21) and a son Anoop (18). The family said that Radheshyam left for school at 7:30 AM on Friday in his Maruti-800 car. He had travelled 15 km from home when suddenly the car's rear tire punctured. He stopped the car on the roadside and started changing the tire himself. Eyewitness shopkeeper said - took out the spare tire then sat in the car Eyewitness shopkeeper Azhar said - When the tire punctured, he himself took out the spare tire to change it. He took the tire out of the boot and placed it near the car. Then perhaps he suddenly felt some anxiety. He went and sat in the car. After that, he did not come out of the car again. According to Azhar, we thought he might have sat in the car due to fatigue. So we didn't pay much attention. I got busy with bike servicing work in the shop. About two hours later, by 10 o'clock, the car was still seen standing there. Its door was open. When we became suspicious, we went closer. There we saw that he was lying unconscious on the car seat. We tried to wake him up. But when there was no movement, we informed the police. Police arrived at the scene. They gathered information from the people nearby. Clerk who worked with him informed the daughter Retired clerk Sushil Kumar Srivastava, who had worked with the teacher, said - My house is in the lane opposite to where Radheshyam's car broke down. I retired from this school 6 months ago. I received a call from the school cook saying that Radheshyam had not come to school today. I called his daughter and found out that he had left in the morning. Meanwhile, a boy from the neighbourhood informed that Radheshyam sir's car was parked in front, and he was found unconscious in the car. After this, I reached the spot. Immediately, I called his daughter. -

stories.summary: Allahabad High Court Lucknow Bench: राष्ट्र की सुरक्षा में लगभग 38 वर्षों तक अपनी सेवाएं देने वाले पूर्व वायुवीर इन्द्रेश कुमार को आखिरकार न्याय मिल गया। इलाहाबाद उच्च न्यायालय की लखनऊ पीठ ने एक महत्वपूर्ण और दूरगामी प्रभाव वाले निर्णय में भारत सरकार, रक्षा मंत्रालय द्वारा दायर याचिका को खारिज करते हुए पूर्व वायुसेना कर्मी के दिव्यांगता पेंशन के अधिकार को बरकरार रखा है। न्यायालय ने स्पष्ट निर्देश दिया है कि पूर्व वायुवीर को तत्काल प्रभाव से नियमानुसार दिव्यांगता पेंशन तथा उससे संबंधित सभी लाभ उपलब्ध कराए जाएं। यह फैसला न केवल इन्द्रेश कुमार के लिए राहत लेकर आया है, बल्कि देशभर के पूर्व सैनिकों और सशस्त्र बलों के कर्मियों के अधिकारों की दृष्टि से भी एक महत्वपूर्ण नजीर माना जा रहा है।

stories.title: Rahul Gandhi’s Savarkar defamation case quashed by SC:Required sanction was not obtained; case relates to 2022 Bharat Jodo Yatra remarks
stories.summary: The Supreme Court on Friday quashes a defamation case against Congress MP Rahul Gandhi over alleged objectionable remarks against Veer Savarkar and spreading hatred in society. The Uttar Pradesh government tells the court that official sanction to prosecute Rahul Gandhi was not obtained. The Supreme Court says that without the required legal sanction, the case cannot continue. A bench of Justice Dipankar Datta and Justice Sheel Nagu heard the matter. The court said in its decision- In the affidavit filed by the government, the Additional Solicitor General and the complainant's lawyer have admitted that the necessary sanction was not obtained in this case. In such a situation, the complaint and all orders issued by the magistrate are quashed. Made remarks against Savarkar in November 2022 The controversy is related to a speech given by Rahul Gandhi during his 'Bharat Jodo Yatra'. Addressing a rally in Akola district of Maharashtra on November 17, 2022, Rahul had made remarks against Savarkar. Following this, advocate Nripendra Pandey had filed a private criminal complaint against him. It was alleged that Rahul deliberately insulted Savarkar. His comment was a well-thought-out conspiracy to defame Savarkar. High Court's order was challenged in the Supreme Court The lower court (Magistrate Court) had taken cognisance of this complaint and issued a summons to Rahul Gandhi. Against this, Rahul Gandhi had approached the High Court. The Lucknow bench of the Allahabad High Court, while hearing the petition on April 4, 2025, had said that Rahul Gandhi can file a review petition in the Sessions Court, and therefore, there is no need for the High Court's intervention at this stage. Rahul Gandhi had challenged this decision of the High Court and the summons order in the Supreme Court.

stories.title: Yogi calls Congress-SP responsible for 1947 killings:Says, 'No one could have harmed India if Modi had been PM then'
stories.summary: CM Yogi responds to Shivpal Yadav’s remark about Azam Khan, accusing the SP of wanting to make him home minister and of triggering riots if it returns to power. Speaking at a Partition Horrors Remembrance Day event in Lucknow on Friday, Yogi Adityanath said SP leaders were now defending a person after whom a university was built, alleging that he was responsible for India’s Partition and Independence-related events. Without naming Azam Khan, Yogi said, “They are saying that if we come to power, we will make him home minister. They want to trigger riots again.” He also alleged that the person had arranged for rioters from Muzaffarnagar and Saharanpur to be brought to the then chief minister’s residence and honoured. Yogi said, “Look at the shameful thinking of these people. They are making such arguments in support of someone who got the rioters of Muzaffarnagar and Saharanpur honoured at the then CM’s residence.” Yogi’s remarks came two days after Shivpal Yadav met Azam Khan, who is lodged in Rampur jail, and said that the SP would make him home minister if it formed the government and would avenge all the alleged injustices against him. Earlier on Friday, the BJP organised a silent march in Lucknow. Yogi, wearing a mask, participated in the half-kilometre march before addressing the programme at Lok Bhawan. Key points from CM Yogi’s speech Yogi also targeted Congress, accusing it of betraying the country. He said Congress leaders remained silent in 1947 and wanted to gain power by any means. He alleged that the party’s intentions remain unchanged even today. He said Sanatanis, Sindhis and Punjabis were driven away from the places where they were born during Partition, while land that Pakistan had not even asked for was handed over to it. 1. ‘The Sanatan nation was divided for the sake of power’ CM Yogi said the entire country was observing Partition Horrors Remembrance Day, calling it one of the darkest chapters in the history of humanity. He said crores of Hindus were forced to leave their own motherland and birthplace, while lakhs of Hindus, Buddhists, Sikhs and Jains were massacred, with no one listening to their suffering. Yogi said the lust for power had reached such a level that a Sanatan nation was divided. He added that the day should also encourage people to learn from those dark chapters of history, as merely remembering the tragedy would not solve the problem. He questioned why the crisis occurred, who was responsible for it, how many perpetrators were punished, and how long India would continue to pay the price for Partition. 2. ‘Hindus were massacred in Bangladesh, but these parties remained silent’ Yogi said the questions surrounding Partition still remain before the country today. He said history should not be treated merely as a subject to study for exams, but as an opportunity to take pride in India’s glorious past and learn from and correct past mistakes. He said this was the thinking behind Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s decision to observe Partition Horrors Remembrance Day. Yogi alleged that those who remained silent in 1947 and were focused only on gaining power continue to follow the same approach even today. He said they have aimed to gain power at the cost of the country. “You must have seen the massacre of Hindus in Bangladesh, but these parties remained silent even then,” Yogi said. He alleged that they feared speaking out would upset their vote bank. He further accused such parties of treating power as personal property and a family inheritance for their own interests. According to Yogi, this mindset leads them to betray the country and create chaos and disorder. 3. ‘India was enslaved because of internal divisions and caste, regional differences’ CM Yogi said there were two major reasons why India became enslaved: internal differences and divisions based on caste and region. He said conspiracies continued alongside these divisions, and those behind them succeeded. As a result, the country was enslaved because people could not fight together. “People thought, ‘The attack is happening to someone else; why should I speak?’ The entire country had to pay the price for this,” Yogi said, adding that even India, which had remained united since ancient times, was eventually divided. 4. ‘Attempts were made to trigger riots in UP over the CAA’ Yogi said he was surprised when Prime Minister Narendra Modi introduced the Citizenship Amendment Act (CAA). He said there was no reason to oppose the legislation, which provided citizenship to Hindus, Jains, Buddhists, Parsis and Christians who had been persecuted and forced to leave Afghanistan, Pakistan or Bangladesh and had lived in India for at least five years. “There was nothing in it about taking away the land of Muslims, Congress or the Samajwadi Party,” he said. However, he alleged that attempts were made to organise protests and trigger riots at several places in Uttar Pradesh, including Lucknow, Kanpur, Meerut, Bulandshahr, Muzaffarnagar and Saharanpur. Yogi said it was fortunate that Uttar Pradesh had a “double-engine” government at the time. He questioned why the CAA was being opposed and alleged that the SP and Congress were supporting the protests from behind. He also called these parties the “real culprits” of the 1947 Partition and said, “If Narendra Modi had been the prime minister at that time, no one could have harmed India.” Azam had built university in Maulana Mohammad Ali Jauhar’s name The CM also referred to the university established by SP leader Azam Khan in the name of Maulana Mohammad Ali Jauhar. Azam Khan established Jauhar University in 2005. It was named after renowned freedom fighter Maulana Mohammad Ali Jauhar, who led several movements against British rule. Mohammad Ali Jauhar served as president of both the Muslim League and the Congress. After India’s Independence, most members of his family moved to Pakistan. On 15 July, the Rampur district magistrate ordered the demolition of 38 of the university’s 40 buildings. However, Moradabad Divisional Commissioner Anjaneya Singh’s court stayed the DM’s order. The matter is currently pending before the court. See 2 pictures-

stories.title: 16-year-old kills father, then dies after jumping before metro:Angry over restrictions; mother lived separately in Noida
stories.summary: A 16-year-old boy allegedly killed his father while he was asleep in Noida and later died by suicide after jumping in front of a Metro train, police said. After the alleged killing, the teenager changed his blood-stained clothes, placed a photograph of his father in the room and offered a garland as a tribute. He then locked the room, took his father's mobile phone and bag, and went to a Metro station. After spending some time at the station, he jumped in front of a train. Police found his father's mobile phone and the room key in the teenager's bag. They contacted his mother, who arrived at the spot along with the boy's uncle. During questioning, the family told police that the teenager lived with his father, while his mother lived separately in Noida. Father found dead inside locked room The police took the boy's mother and uncle to the room on Thursday night. They opened the door with the key and found the body of 45-year-old Raju Sharma inside. Initial investigation suggested that Raju had imposed several restrictions on his son's movements. He had also stopped the boy's studies after Class 11. Police suspect that the teenager was distressed by these restrictions and allegedly killed his father early on Wednesday, August 12. He died by suicide at around 7am the same day. The incident took place in the Phase 3 police station area of Noida. Raju was a private tutor. He had divorced his wife 12 years ago and had been living with his only son. Raju lived in Noida for 21 years Raju was originally from Bokaro Steel City in Jharkhand. His father had worked for SAIL. Raju moved to Noida with his wife in 2005. He later lived with his only son in a rented room in the Ajnara Society area. He held an MCom degree and taught children through private tuition and online classes. Blood stains found inside room Police said the teenager's body was found near a railway line on Wednesday. During a search, officers found his father's mobile phone and the room key in his bag. Police used the mobile phone to contact his mother, who arrived and identified her son's body. Raju's brother, Arun Sharma, also reached the spot and told police that his brother was missing. The police questioned the mother, who said Raju had a short temper and had imposed several restrictions on his son. She said the teenager was often upset by them. This led police to suspect that the teenager might have killed his father before taking his own life. Police then took the mother and uncle to Raju's room. A strong smell was coming from inside. When they opened the door, they found Raju's body. Blood-stained clothes believed to belong to the teenager were found inside the room, along with blood stains on the walls. A forensic team collected samples from the scene, while the blood-stained clothes were sent to a laboratory for examination. Neighbours noticed little interaction between father and son Neighbour Kaushal said he rarely saw the teenager outside the house. The boy mostly stayed indoors and was only occasionally seen when he went upstairs to dry clothes. Ram Avtar Tiwari, another resident of the building, said the father and son rarely spoke to each other. He said the teenager prepared his own food and collected water himself. The father and son would generally exchange things only when necessary.

stories.title: Computer operator beaten to death:Names attackers in video before dying; FIR against 6, including former block chief and ration dealer
stories.summary: A computer operator with the Supply Department in Pratapgarh was beaten to death. At around 7 pm on Thursday, he was returning home from work when the accused, who were lying in wait, attacked him with sticks, iron rods and the butt of a revolver. The attackers fled after leaving him, believing he was dead. Family members reached the spot after being informed by local residents and took him to hospital. Doctors declared him dead. Before his death, the computer operator named six attackers, including a former block chief. A video of his statement has also surfaced. The incident took place in the Lilapur police station area, around 15 km from the district headquarters. Based on a complaint by the family, police have registered an FIR against six named accused, including the former block chief and his brother, who is a ration dealer. The 32-year-old computer operator, Saurabh Vishwakarma, got married a year ago. He has a four-month-old daughter. His wife, Aanchal, broke down after seeing her husband's body. Here is the full case in sequence Saurabh Vishwakarma (32), a resident of Sindhora village in the Lilapur police station area, worked as a contractual computer operator in the Supply Department. He was the youngest of three brothers. His elder brother Sushil Vishwakarma drives a taxi, while his other brother Sonu Vishwakarma is a farmer. According to the family complaint, Saurabh was returning home from the Supply Office in Lalganj between 7 pm and 7.15 pm on August 13. When he reached around 150 metres beyond Gajadhar Inter College, Saurabh Tiwari (32), Daroga Tiwari (30), Sonu Tiwari (30), Anuj Tiwari (32) and others surrounded him. The accused brutally assaulted him. Hearing Saurabh's cries for help, local residents reached the spot. They informed Saurabh's friends Sonu Upadhyay and Shubham Pandey about the incident. Both reached the spot and took Saurabh to the Medical College for treatment, where doctors declared him dead. As soon as the incident was reported, ASP Brijnandan Rai reached the spot with a police team and took details of the incident. Police have been deployed in the area in view of the tension. Read full news in chronological manner Before dying, he said: They hit me with a gun butt and broke my leg Before his death, the computer operator said, "Daroga Tiwari and the son of his brother Bade Tiwari, along with 8-10 people, beat me with sticks. They hit my neck with the butt of a gun and also broke my leg." Family says accused had opened fire at their house four months ago The family said Sanjay alias Bade Tiwari is the former block chief of Laxmanganj, while his brother Sonu Tiwari is a ration dealer. The accused allegedly developed a grudge after Saurabh refused to approve a ration card-related work for Sonu. Four months ago, the accused had also allegedly fired 6-7 rounds at their house. The family said Saurabh was killed because of this dispute. Father-in-law demands encounter of accused Saurabh's father-in-law, Sajjan Vishwakarma, said, "Our demand is that all the accused should be arrested. After their arrest, they should be killed in an encounter and their houses should be demolished with bulldozers. Saurabh's wife should be given a government job. The government should also provide financial assistance for his four-month-old daughter." Friends took him to the hospital Hearing Saurabh's screams after the attack, people from the vicinity reached the spot. They informed his friends Sonu Upadhyay and Shubham Pandey about the incident. Both reached the spot and took Saurabh to the medical college for treatment, where doctors declared him dead. A video from before Saurabh's death has also surfaced. In it, he has also named the accused and said- Daroga Tiwari and his brother Bade Tiwari's son, along with 8-10 people, assaulted me with sticks. They hit my neck with a rifle butt and also broke my leg. Firing at home four months ago Family members said that Sonu Tiwari, brother of former block head Bade Tiwari of Laxmanpur, who is a ration dealer. The accused had harbored enmity after Sonu's ration card work was not approved. About four months ago, the accused had also fired 6-7 rounds at their house. Due to this animosity, the accused have murdered Saurabh. Police force deployed, body sent for post-mortem Considering the tension in the area after the incident, police force was deployed. ASP Brijnandan Rai reached the spot with the police team and gathered information about the incident. The body was taken into custody and sent for post-mortem. Brijnandan Rai informed that a case has been registered based on Saurabh's complaint. It is a case of old enmity. The accused are being searched for. One accused, Daroga Tiwari, was arrested on Friday morning.
