stories.title: Student reaches police outpost over no teaching at school:Says, 'Ma’am keeps using phone, what will happen to our future?'
stories.summary: In Kanpur Dehat, a 12-year-old seventh-grade student reached the police outpost with a complaint about not being taught. He told the outpost in-charge, "Teachers don't teach, they use their phones all day. Older students beat younger children, and children keep playing in the ground." He asked, What will happen to our future? The policemen were surprised to hear the student's words. A head constable took him to the school. In front of the police, the female teacher started scolding the student and threatened to beat him. The police explained to the teacher and advised her not to do so. The incident took place on August 10, around 12 noon. The video of the incident surfaced on Thursday. The student studies in the seventh grade at a government school in Rasdhan, about 30 km from the district headquarters. On the instructions of the BSA, a notice has been issued to the headmaster and the accused teacher. See pictures Know full story Sanjeev Mishra, a resident of Rasdhan, is a farmer. He has five children - four sons and one daughter. 12-year-old Madhav is the fourth child. He studies in the seventh grade at the government composite school in the village. On August 10, Madhav reached the Rasdhan police outpost in his school uniform. The policemen were surprised to see him. When asked the reason for coming to the outpost, he said that he had come to complain about his school. Madhav said that there is no studying in school. Teachers are busy using their phones. Children keep playing in the ground all day. Older students beat him up frequently. No action is taken even after complaining. I am very troubled. He said that when he left school for the outpost, the madam was still talking on the phone. After hearing the student's complaint, the head constable of the outpost took him to the school. In front of the police, the teacher threatened the student A conversation took place between the student and teacher Saima Khan in the presence of policemen at the school. The police asked the teacher about the student's complaint. During this, the teacher started scolding the student and threatening to hit him. The policemen made a video of the incident. Read conversation between the student and the teacher Teacher: Why did you go to the police? Whatever the problem is, tell me directly. Student: You don't listen. Who should I tell? Teacher: We don't listen? I will hit you so much right now, I will beat you until your mind is set straight. When the teacher flared up, policemen stopped her from talking to the child in that manner. After pacifying both of them, the policemen returned. Investigation on BSA's instructions, Notice to Headmaster and Teacher After the video surfaced, on the instructions of BSA Ashish Pandey, the Block Education Officer (BEO) reached the school and investigated. He spoke to students and school staff and submitted his report to the BSA. Based on the report, the BSA issued show-cause notices to Headmaster Anupam Kumar and teacher Saima Khan. Both have been summoned to the BSA office for clarification. According to the BEO, some students had beaten the complainant student. He went to the teacher to complain about it, but at that time the teacher was talking on the phone and did not listen to him. Annoyed by this, the student reached the police outpost. Outpost In-charge said - The complaint was about lack of studies Rasdhan Outpost In-charge Prashant Singh said- A child had come to the outpost with a complaint. The outpost's constable took him to school. The child was complaining about the lack of studies in school. The matter was not serious, but the way the teacher scolded the child in front of the police personnel was wrong. BSA said - There was a dispute among children Basic Education Officer Ashish Pandey said- There was a dispute among the children. The police post is right next to the school, so the child went there. The Block Education Officer went to the spot and investigated. The child's parents were also called to the school. According to them, the child becomes a bit aggressive. For now, he has been counselled.

stories.title: Auto driver's Son files murder FIR:Body found floating in Varuna River on 6 August; acid found in vehicle
stories.summary: On the night of August 6, 2026, an abandoned auto-rickshaw was found on the Varuna Bridge in the Cantt police station area of Varanasi. The auto-rickshaw number was UP65 ET8037. During the investigation, the police found the auto-rickshaw belonged to Gyanchand Sonkar, a resident of Ardali Bazar, Cantt police station. A bottle of acid was found in the auto-rickshaw. Upon searching, Gyanchand's body was found floating in the Varuna River below the bridge. In this regard, on the night of August 13, the police registered a murder case based on the complaint. The deceased's son, Satish Sonkar, filed a murder complaint with the Cantt police. Based on this, the police have registered a case and started action. Murder on 6 August Satish stated in the complaint given to the police, My father Gyanchand Sonkar used to drive his private auto-rickshaw. He had no enmity with anyone, nor did he have much to do with anyone at home. When he did not return home by 11 PM on the night of August 6, I called his number.When I called, the police answered the phone and asked who I was, so I explained everything, upon which they called me to the Varuna Bridge. Body found floating in Varuna Satish said, Upon reaching there, the auto was found abandoned, and a half-empty bottle of acid was found further ahead. After this, we and the police started searching for father. When searched in the Varuna river below, father's body was found floating there, upon which he was pulled out. Someone has murdered my father. In such a situation, a complaint has been lodged with the police today. In this regard, Cantt Police Station in-charge Raj Kishore Pandey said, Based on the complaint of the deceased Gyanchand's son, a case has been registered under BNS Section 103(1) and the search for the murderer is underway. He will be apprehended soon. Had said a constable was following On August 6, upon finding the body, Satish had said that father had been troubled for a long time and was repeatedly saying that a constable was following him. In such a situation, the police are also investigating that angle. Currently, the search for the murderer is being conducted using CCTV footage.

stories.title: CCTV shows doctor jumping to death from 8th floor:Note blames conwoman Garima; sister breaks down, daughter says, ‘Papa, come back’
stories.summary: A doctor in Gorakhpur died by suicide after jumping from the eighth floor of his apartment on Thursday. A CCTV camera captured his final moments, while a note found in his pocket named alleged fraudster Garima Singh and her gang as responsible for his death. Dr Paramatma Singh left his flat at around 9.10 am, went to the basement and took a lift to the eighth floor before reaching the terrace. He jumped from the building shortly afterwards. Residents took him to a nearby private hospital, where doctors declared him dead. Daughter returns from school, says ‘Papa, please come back’ Singh’s 12-year-old son Arihant and seven-year-old daughter Parnika, known as Binni, were called home from school after the incident. When Binni saw her father’s body, she broke down and repeatedly said, “Papa, please come back.” She later clung to her elder brother and cried. Singh’s wife, Dr Sumitra Singh, also works as a government veterinary doctor. His younger sister Ranjana Singh said Sumitra had called her two days earlier, telling her that Paramatma was under severe stress over a loan-related matter. Ranjana said she had planned to visit and speak to him but could not reach him in time. Post-mortem finds multiple fractures A post-mortem examination found multiple fractures and serious internal injuries. The report said his neck, ribs, legs, spine and arms had suffered fractures. His body was taken to his ancestral home in Mau after the post-mortem. His last rites are scheduled for Friday. Who is Garima Singh? According to the police, Garima Singh, who holds a PhD, allegedly ran a loan fraud operation with her father Dhruv Narayan Singh and others. Police said she targeted railway officials, doctors and teachers by promising to arrange loans or help them close existing loans. Four cases have been registered against her so far this month, while six more complaints have been received. Police allege that around ₹10 crore may have been taken from 10 people. Garima and her father have been in jail since August 3. Seven days before his death, Dr Paramatma Singh had filed a complaint alleging that Garima had cheated him of ₹1.40 crore. Doctor allegedly took loans from six banks According to the complaint, Garima contacted Singh in February 2026 through a relative. She allegedly claimed that she could help close his existing home loan through a new personal loan. Police allege that Singh was made to take loans from six banks and transfer the money to accounts linked to Garima. She initially paid two instalments but later allegedly stopped making payments and threatened his family. FIR filed against Garima and associates Based on a complaint by Singh’s cousin Dileep Singh, Gorakhnath police registered a case of abetment of suicide against Garima Singh and her alleged associates on Thursday evening. Police may question Garima in jail as part of the investigation. SSP Dr Kaustubh said police would also invoke the Gangsters Act against Garima and other members of the alleged gang. Their financial activities are being investigated, and police are examining their bank accounts and properties allegedly linked to the fraud. Paramatma Singh, originally from Mau, had settled in Gorakhpur several years ago. He lived with his wife and two children in a two-bedroom flat at Basant Enclave in Rajendra Nagar. He was posted as a government veterinary doctor in Nautanwa, Maharajganj, while his wife was posted in the Siswan block of the same district.

stories.title: 'He called me his daughter, we only took a photo':Sister denies any relationship with Mahant; 2 friends buried in Baghpat temple
stories.summary: My brother left home on the 25th. Everyone searched for him a lot, but he was not found anywhere. Today it was revealed that he was killed and buried in the Ganesh temple. I have no relation with the Mahant. He used to say that I consider you my daughter. He had taken a photo with me in Haridwar, but I have no connection with him. This is what Ankit's sister said, who is rumored to be having an affair with the Mahant. In Baghpat, Mahant Naresh Nath of Ganesh Temple killed and buried 2 friends, then plastered over it and installed tiles. On Thursday (August 13), the police arrested 2 disciples of the Mahant. One disciple made several revelations in his confession. The case is from the Chandinagar police station area, 20 km away from the district headquarters. Know the full case In Sigoli Taga village, Ankit (25) lived with his mother and 5 sisters. He was the only son of the house. 2 sisters are married. Ankit was unmarried and unemployed. Israr's (32) house is right in front of his house. Israr used to support his family by working as a laborer. His family includes his wife Firdaus and 3 children. On the afternoon of July 25, Ankit and Israr left on a bike. When both did not return until the next day, their family members started looking for them. But, nothing was known about either of them. Calls were made to both their phones, but the mobiles were not picked up. From the evening of July 27, both their mobiles were switched off. Missing person report filed 4 days later On July 29, a missing person report was filed at Chandinagar police station. When both did not return even after 8-10 days, the police became active. The police checked call details, last known locations, and questioned villagers. In this, the name of Mahant Naresh Nath of Ganesh Temple located in Lahchaura came to light. Both were last seen near the Ganesh Temple. The police also learned about an affair between the Mahant and Ankit's sister. Accused Mahant absconded upon getting a hint Police raided the temple on Wednesday (August 12) night, but Mahant Naresh Nath (40) got wind of it and fled. Police found his disciple Ujjwal in the temple. Initially, he tried to mislead the police, but broke down under strict interrogation. Later, police also arrested another disciple, Krishna Yadav. Now read the confession of accused Ujjwal Ujjwal told the police - On August 25, Ankit and Israr came to the ashram very angrily. At that time, Mahant Naresh Nath, his 14-year-old son, I, and Krishna Yadav were present in the ashram. The Mahant calmed Ankit and Israr. He said that I will solve your problem, but first, have tea as prasad. Mixed intoxicant in tea and gave it to them The Mahant had already mixed an intoxicating substance in that tea, which made both of them unconscious as soon as they drank it. After that, the Mahant took out a poisonous injection from his car and administered it to both of them. When I asked that they would die, the Mahant told us to remain silent. Engaged minor son in watch duty Naresh Nath had told me that I charge 40 thousand for performing a marriage, but I will get your marriage done for free. Meanwhile, Krishna Yadav was lured with the promise that I would teach him tantra vidya (occult knowledge). After this, Krishna and I together dug a 6-foot deep pit. The Mahant's 14-year-old son had also come to the ashram. He was made to stand at the gate for watch duty. Phone thrown 10 km away to mislead Upon their death, they were buried in a pit. Tiles were installed over that pit. To mislead the police, Israr's phone was thrown 10 kilometers away in the jungle. When the police removed the tiles, the decomposed bodies of Ankit and Israr were found. They were identified by their clothes and watches. The bike Ankit and Israr used to reach Ganesh Temple has not yet been recovered. Sister was living at her maternal home after marriage One of Ankit's sisters had come to live at her maternal home after marriage. Earlier, the mahant used to live in Ankit's neighborhood and performed worship. However, his conduct was not good. Because of this, the villagers had expelled him from the village. After this, he started living with his two disciples at Ganesh Temple, 2 km away from the village. There had been fights many times before It is believed that Ankit and Israr had gone to convince the Mahant regarding his affair with their sister. There had been fights over this many times before. When the sister was asked about her affair with the Mahant, she denied it. The sister says that the Mahant used to call her his daughter. She had no relationship with him. A month and a half ago, we went to Haridwar with our family. The Mahant told me that I was like his daughter. During that time, he took a photo with me. All the talks about an affair are just rumors. I have no relationship with him. Baghpat SP Suraj Rai said that The dead bodies of both youths have been recovered from the temple. The Mahant's disciples, Ujjwal and Krishna, have been arrested. The search for the Mahant and his son has been intensified. 6 police teams are involved. The accused Mahant is originally from Uttarakhand. A police team has also been dispatched to Uttarakhand.

Meanwhile, the BJP government, which boasts of building the most expressways in UP, is on the back foot. In today's UP Explainer, find out if the opposition will be able to capitalise on this issue in the assembly elections and draw votes to its side? How will the BJP avoid this damage? Why is the Lucknow-Kanpur Expressway sinking repeatedly? Is this the most sinking expressway till date? Yes, in terms of scale and duration, this is the most sinking expressway. However, the government or NHAI has not officially stated this. But, based on the number and duration of incidents recorded in media reports, this is the picture that emerges What loss will the BJP suffer due to the poor construction of the Lucknow-Kanpur Expressway? Political experts say that this has dealt a blow to BJP's development model and good governance image. Even before this, the issue of poor construction of several expressways in UP has been raised, but there were no elections then. So everything was managed. But, it doesn't seem to be happening here. This can be understood as follows How big an issue will the Lucknow-Kanpur Expressway become in the elections? Political analysts are divided on this. Some talk about its widespread impact. stories.title: Farrukhabad-Budaun highway submerged, barricades installed:44,000 people from 62 villages forced to leave their homes; evacuation announcement made
stories.summary: After the surge in the Ganga river, the Farrukhabad-Badaun highway has been submerged. At two places, two to three feet of water has accumulated for 100 to 150 meters. Traffic has been stopped by putting up barricades. Due to the flood, more than 44 thousand people from 62 villages have been forced to leave their homes. Floodwater has started reaching some of the relief camps that were set up. Children and women have been sent to other camps. The Ganga river is continuously eroding its banks. It is flowing 1.5 km away from its original course. As a result, 32 houses have collapsed so far. Seeing the deteriorating situation, NDRF (National Disaster Response Force) has been called in. PAC personnel are transporting people stranded in the water to safe places with the help of boats and steamers. Having to travel 14 km extra to go to Badaun Among the villages in Farrukhabad that are affected by floods, the highest number, 27 villages, are in Amritpur tehsil. The people there say - 'This is the sign of Amritpur, water on both sides of the road.' Every year, as the water level of the Ganga rises, this road is bound to get submerged. In 2025, the State Highway remained blocked for 15 days. Until now, vehicles going from Farrukhabad to Badaun used to go via Rajepur Tiraaha to Badaun. However, currently, the State Highway near Chitrakoot village has been submerged. Police duty has been assigned on the highway to prevent people from going onto the submerged road. Police are diverting vehicles from the Dabra area towards Badaun. People have to travel about 14 km extra. No shelter in relief camps, they are living on house roofs Chitrakoot village is near the State Highway. The entire village is submerged. We met Rajpal amidst the water. He says - the village is filled with water all around. There is also a risk of snakes and scorpions. People have to commute through these paths. A relief camp has been set up near the village. Only 10 to 20 people come here, because only that many names have been registered. Many people's names were not registered. They are forced to live on the roofs of their houses, waiting for the water to recede. Some have gone to their relatives' homes. This situation has persisted for 10 days. Last year's flood lasted for 30 days. Lost homes, set up tents by the roadside, then removed from there too Sukhdev, standing near us, says- Many houses in the village were submerged. Distressed people started living in tents by the roadside. Just 2-3 days ago, the administration announced (by beating drums) that this place is also dangerous and must be vacated. People were asked to go to relief camps. Those who are trapped on the roofs of their houses are not even getting clean drinking water. Ration and water are being delivered by boat, but the fear persists. People are somehow making ends meet. Tehsildar flared up when asked about water filling in the camp To understand the atmosphere of the relief camp, we reached the Pharmacy College in Chitrakoot village. The relief camp was set up here. The government school in the village was flooded. Because of this, a part of the school was also running in a section of the relief camp. Water has slowly started filling up outside the relief camp as well. SDM Shweta Sahu and Tehsildar Shashank Singh had arrived here. We asked the Tehsildar - "Floodwater has started filling up here, what are the preparations?" He angrily said - "Those who come to the camp will stay inside or will they roam outside? There is no water inside, is there?" We asked - "They will go outside for other needs." The Tehsildar said - "You tell us what we should do, because we don't know anything." Ration dealer said - A dam was built after 14 years, but it didn't even last a few months 12 villages in Farrukhabad Sadar Tehsil are flooded. Due to erosion in Rampur Dafarpur, several houses were swallowed by the river. On the boat going towards this village, the village's ration dealer, Subhash Chandra, was met. He says - Since 2012, it happens every year that after the water level in the Ganga rises, floods occur. People asked officials to build a dam so that the entire village could be saved from erosion. The Irrigation Department built a dam, but it didn't even last a few months. Some grain was sent by the government, which is being distributed among the people trapped in the flood. 'One house washed away, the other is saved so we are demolishing it' About 50 meters away from the strong current of the Ganga river, Meerawati was getting the debris of her broken house loaded onto a boat with her relatives. She says - We had an old house in this village. It was submerged in the river just 4 days ago. We were building another house here, but now this one is also going to be submerged. We are demolishing it and taking the bricks. Everyone here is troubled. Food and drink are not available. We have lost everything from our farm to our home. Now we don't understand where to go? House filled with water, cows and goats are on the road 56-year-old Jabar Singh lived his entire life in the village and did farming. He says - we have cows and goats, the house is submerged in water. The animals are on the road. The fields are also flooded. Now, when the water recedes, we will return. We will rebuild our house here again. Every year there is a flood, and there is a lot of talk about help, but the truth is that people like us don't even get a penny. Who does the administration help, I wonder? Santosh from Madaiya village says, In our area, it's not just the problem of floods, the current of the Ganga is also eroding the land. Last year, the situation was very terrible. The entire Prithvipur village was eroded. These people did build a dam. But, it could not withstand the current of the Ganga. People are distressed, they are just surviving. 3 situations of flood, see in pictures 1. Erosion of Ganga river People are demolishing their houses themselves Crops submerged

stories.title: Farmer gifts vegetables after district magistrate resolves dispute:Three-year wait for land measurement ends after direct intervention by Agra DM
stories.summary: A farmer in Uttar Pradesh's Agra visited the District Magistrate's office on Friday carrying a kilogram of fresh vegetables to thank the District Magistrate after his long-pending land measurement dispute was resolved. The farmer, Ram Prakash, placed a bag of kakoda (spiny gourd) on District Magistrate Manish Bansal's desk and said, Sir, thank you very much. My work is finally done. Please accept these vegetables I have brought for you. Smiling at the gesture, the District Magistrate replied: This is priceless. How can I refuse such a gift? Farmer had waited three years for land measurement Ram Prakash, a resident of Basai Arela in Bah tehsil, had been trying to get his agricultural land measured for the past three years. He alleged that despite repeated complaints, the Revenue Inspector and the lekhpal (village revenue official) kept delaying the process instead of carrying out the measurement. Complaint raised during grievance hearing On July 6, during a public grievance redressal programme, the farmer presented his complaint directly to District Magistrate Manish Bansal. Taking immediate note of the matter, the District Magistrate sought an explanation from the concerned officials and expressed displeasure over the delay in conducting the land measurement. Following his directions, the revenue authorities completed the measurement, resolving the long-pending dispute. Gift from his own farm Grateful that the issue had finally been resolved, Ram Prakash returned to the Collectorate on Friday during the public hearing session. He brought one kilogram of kakoda harvested from his own field as a token of appreciation. The farmer said he had submitted several applications over the past three years and had approached previous officials as well, but no action had been taken until the District Magistrate intervened. DM accepts the 'priceless' gift District Magistrate Manish Bansal said the farmer had brought the vegetables with genuine affection and gratitude. The farmer brought such a priceless gift with great affection. How could I return it? I gladly accepted it. He added that all revenue officials had been instructed to ensure timely disposal of public complaints, not only during Tehsil Day programmes but also through regular public grievance hearings.

stories.title: Yogi says SP goon sparked Sambhal riots:'Now pleading for mercy; Bareilly rioter seeks forgiveness from jail'
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath on Friday launched a sharp attack on the Samajwadi Party, accusing it of encouraging riots, protecting mafias and disrupting the functioning of the State Assembly. Addressing a public gathering in Ambedkar Nagar, the Chief Minister claimed that a "Samajwadi Party goon" was responsible for the violence in Sambhal and alleged that the accused was now pleading for leniency. Referring to another alleged rioter from Bareilly, he said the man was currently in jail and seeking forgiveness. "A Samajwadi Party goon incited the riots in Sambhal. The government has brought him to his knees. A goon from Bareilly used to organise riots. Today he is suffering in jail and is saying, 'Please let me go, I made a mistake. It won't happen again.'" Alleges Samajwadi Party disrupted Assembly proceedings The Chief Minister also accused Samajwadi Party legislators of creating disruptions during the Assembly session. He said the opposition prevented the House from functioning when the government sought to introduce welfare measures in the Budget. According to him, the proposals included schemes to honour social reformers such as Sant Ravidas, Dr B.R. Ambedkar and Chhatrapati Shahu Maharaj, besides increasing honorariums for Anganwadi workers, fair-price shop dealers and village watchmen. “They did not allow the Assembly to function, but we are not going to stop.” See two pictures... Inaugurates projects worth over ₹706 crore During his visit, the Chief Minister inaugurated and laid the foundation stones for 194 development projects worth more than ₹706.81 crore in the Jalalpur, Alapur and Tanda Assembly constituencies. He also distributed approval letters and certificates to beneficiaries of various government welfare schemes. 'SP has no interest in development' Yogi Adityanath said the government had presented a supplementary Budget of ₹59,000 crore during the recent Assembly session, but alleged that SP created disruptions and prevented meaningful debate. He claimed the party was not interested in development or the welfare of poor people. 'SP flag once symbolised fear' The Chief Minister alleged that under previous SP governments, riots frequently occurred in cities such as Meerut, Aligarh, Moradabad, Saharanpur, Bareilly, Lucknow and Kanpur. He claimed that criminals travelled in vehicles displaying SP flags and were involved in extortion. "Today our government is taking strict action against such elements." 'Every district had a mafia under SP' The Chief Minister further alleged that the previous SP government had patronised different types of mafias in every district, including sand, land and forest mafias. He claimed Uttar Pradesh had now become both "mafia-free" and "curfew-free". He warned that anyone attempting to threaten traders or interfere with young people's future would be sent to jail and their illegally acquired assets would be confiscated. Highlights welfare initiatives The Chief Minister said the government was promoting local cuisines from every district and providing free food grains to around 16 crore beneficiaries. He also highlighted medical interventions for children with hearing and speech impairments, saying some beneficiaries had received treatment and certificates during the event. Referring to encephalitis, he alleged that nearly 1,200 children used to be affected under previous governments, while accusing SP leaders of showing little concern. 'Ayodhya's development troubles SP and Congress' Yogi Adityanath said Uttar Pradesh had earned greater respect across the country and claimed that the development of Ayodhya had become a source of discomfort for both the Samajwadi Party and the Congress. He accused both parties of opposing Lord Ram and said his government was developing Ayodhya, Kashi, Mathura-Vrindavan and Vindhyachal as major religious centres. He also noted that he was the first Chief Minister to visit Govind Dham in the area. Takes swipe at Akhilesh Yadav Without naming SP president Akhilesh Yadav directly, the Chief Minister mocked his daily routine. "He used to wake up around noon, post a tweet in the afternoon, receive advice from his uncle, then go to the gym. By evening, he would be busy elsewhere and would not even know where he was. A person who cannot manage himself cannot run a state." He added that anyone threatening to incite riots would face strict action. 'Those harassing women or traders face jail' Concluding his speech, the Chief Minister said his government would not tolerate crimes against women or intimidation of traders. He said offenders would face either imprisonment or the strictest legal consequences. The Chief Minister also said around 15 crore people in Uttar Pradesh were receiving free food grains and nearly 10 crore beneficiaries were covered under the Ayushman Bharat health insurance scheme.

stories.title: New audio of BJP MLA facing sexual harassment allegations:Names UP Bahubali, says, ‘I’ll have them killed before they kill me’
stories.summary: A fresh audio clip allegedly featuring Sultanpur BJP MLA Vinod Singh, who is facing allegations of sexual harassment, surfaced on Friday. In the recording, the MLA is heard speaking to the woman who has accused him of attempting to rape her. During the conversation, he allegedly claims that two local strongmen, Sonu Singh and Monu Singh, are plotting to kill him and says he could have them killed before they act against him. The woman responds mostly with brief acknowledgements such as "Yes" and "Ji" throughout the conversation. Speaking to Dainik Bhaskar, the woman confirmed that the audio was genuine and said the conversation took place in May 2026. Woman has accused MLA of attempted rape On Wednesday, the woman accused the BJP legislator of attempting to rape her and threatening to kill her. She alleged that the MLA called her to his residence after threatening that her daughter would be raped if she refused to meet him. She further claimed that he attempted to sexually assault her, touched her private parts and tore her clothes. According to her complaint, she managed to push him away and escape. Excerpts from the alleged conversation Earlier audio had also surfaced Another audio clip had surfaced earlier in which the MLA was allegedly heard speaking to the woman's husband. In that conversation, the MLA says: Who are Sonu and Monu Singh? Vinod Singh has had a long-standing rivalry with brothers Chandrabhadra Singh, popularly known as Sonu Singh, and Yashbhadra Singh, known as Monu Singh. According to Monu Singh, he was attacked at a court premises in 2014, during which one Jainendra Sharma was arrested. He has alleged that police call detail records showed Vinod Singh was in regular contact with the attackers, leading to the MLA being named as an accused in the case. Sonu Singh was elected MLA twice, in 2002 and 2007, on a Samajwadi Party ticket. Monu Singh has served as a block chief. Their father, Indrabhadra Singh, was also an MLA from the Isauli Assembly constituency. According to the report, Indrabhadra Singh was murdered in 1996. In 2006, Sonu and Monu allegedly orchestrated the killing of Sant Gyaneshwar in retaliation for their father's murder. Monu Singh has reportedly faced around 19 criminal cases, including charges of murder, attempted murder, rioting and offences under the Gangster Act and Goonda Act. Woman's allegations The woman held a press conference in Delhi on July 3, accusing Vinod Singh of attempting to rape her and issuing death threats. She alleged that the MLA told her, "If you do not do as I say, I will ruin you." She further claimed that 12 to 15 people had been deployed to follow her and that she had received threats of an acid attack and threats to kill her husband and children. She said she had approached the police, but no action was taken on her complaint. MLA denies allegations Vinod Singh has denied all the allegations. He claimed that the woman's husband is facing cases of forgery and cheating and alleged that the accusations were fabricated to avoid arrest and to defame him. "I have full faith in the court. The truth will come out during the investigation," the MLA said.

stories.title: Postmaster siphons off ₹1.4 crore from customers:Withdraws money from accounts and fixed deposits in Sambhal, issues fake receipts
stories.summary: An assistant postmaster who gambled with customers' money was arrested on Friday in Sambhal. He embezzled 1.4 crore rupees of account holders in the post office. According to the police, Deepak Kumar used to take the money deposited in customers' accounts and FDs. In return, he would give them fake receipts. The matter came to light when the police investigated after receiving complaints from customers. It was found that the accused had invested the embezzled amount of 1.40 crore rupees in online betting platforms like Dream-11. So far, 7 cases have been registered against the accused. The case is from the Bahjoi area. This entire case of fraud with customers is from the Bahjoi post office located in Chandausi tehsil. Bahjoi police on Friday arrested accused Deepak Kumar from the Bahjoi-Sambhal road. At 2:30 PM, SP Krishna Kumar Bishnoi and CO Stuti Singh disclosed the matter. According to the police, on August 6, several account holders had lodged a complaint at Bahjoi police station. Post office customers alleged that money was withdrawn from savings accounts without their knowledge. Police investigation revealed that Assistant Postmaster Deepak Kumar, a resident of Saimar Tola, used to withdraw money from accounts and issue fake receipts. On August 7, after receiving two more complaints, a total of 7 cases were registered against Deepak. Deepak returned money to some people on complaint Police investigation also revealed that the accused assistant postmaster had returned money to some account holders. The police are conducting a financial investigation into the entire matter. The police are also trying to ascertain whether the actual embezzled amount and the number of victims are not higher than this. The police are also investigating whether other employees of the Post Office department are involved in this embezzlement. SP Krishna Kumar Bishnoi said - Deepak Kumar was posted in Chandausi in 2023-24. After this, he was transferred to Bahjoi. The investigation revealed that he embezzled a total of 1 crore 40 lakh rupees. He used to take money from people for FD and savings accounts but did not give valid receipts for it. He used to invest that money in online betting.

stories.title: Atiq Ahmed's jailed sons granted parole for brother Abaan's funeral:Deputy CM Maurya brushes aside questions on fatal road crash
stories.summary: The Allahabad High Court on Friday granted parole to slain gangster-turned-politician Atiq Ahmed's jailed sons, Ali and Umar, allowing them to attend the funeral of their younger brother, Abaan, who died in a road accident. The order was passed at around 3.30 pm. Ali is lodged in Jhansi Jail, while Umar is imprisoned in Lucknow Jail. Officials said it could take six to seven hours for the brothers to reach Prayagraj after the court order reaches the respective prisons. As a result, Abaan's burial may take place late on Friday night or on Saturday. Meanwhile, the family has kept Abaan's body in a deep freezer until the funeral. Will Shaista Parveen attend? Attention has also turned to whether Atiq Ahmed's wife, Shaista Parveen, will attend the funeral. Shaista has been absconding since 2023 and did not attend the funerals of either her husband Atiq Ahmed or her son Asad after their deaths. Abaan, 21, will be buried at the family's ancestral cemetery in Kasari-Masari, where Atiq Ahmed, his father Firoz Ahmed, brother Ashraf and son Asad are also buried. Deputy CM dismisses questions on Abaan's death During a visit to Prayagraj, Uttar Pradesh Deputy Chief Minister Keshav Prasad Maurya was asked by reporters about Abaan's death. Responding briefly, he said road accidents occur every day and questioned why the incident was being treated differently. Abaan died while travelling to meet jailed brother Abaan died on Thursday morning in a road accident near Jhansi while travelling from Prayagraj to meet his brother Ali in jail. He was travelling in a Creta SUV with four friends when the driver reportedly tried to avoid an animal on the highway. The vehicle crashed into a road divider. Abaan and one of his friends, Sonu, died in the accident, while three others sustained injuries. Their bodies were brought from Jhansi to Hatwa village in Prayagraj by ambulance early on Friday morning. Family stores body until funeral The family has placed Abaan's body in a deep freezer at his aunt's residence in Hatwa village while waiting for the parole process to be completed. Two additional deep freezers have also reportedly been arranged to preserve the body until the funeral takes place. A family member who travelled to Jhansi to receive the body reportedly said, "He belonged to Allah, and Allah has taken him back," a remark similar to one made by Atiq Ahmed's brother Ashraf after the police encounter killing of Atiq's son Asad in 2023. According to family members, Ali, who is in jail, was devastated after learning of his younger brother's death and reportedly did not sleep or eat throughout the night.

stories.title: Protest in Lucknow with CRPF jawan’s body:Wife questions how he could shoot himself three times; vows to get commandant dismissed
stories.summary: The family of a Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) jawan staged a protest in Lucknow early Friday, placing his body on Budheshwar Crossing and blocking the Lucknow–Hardoi highway for nearly two hours. Senior police officers reached the spot and persuaded the family to end the protest. The body was later taken to the family's native village in Hardoi district for the last rites. Wife rejects suicide claim The deceased jawan, 37-year-old Vineet Singh, was posted with the 112th Battalion of the CRPF in Manipur. He died on August 5 after sustaining gunshot injuries under suspicious circumstances at the CRPF headquarters in Motbung. According to the official version, he died by suicide using his personal weapon. However, his wife, Neha Singh, disputed the claim, alleging that her husband could not have shot himself three times in the chest. "How can someone shoot himself three times in the chest? Someone else must have shot him," she said, demanding a fresh post-mortem and a thorough investigation. She also accused CRPF officers of harassing her husband and forcing him to remain on duty despite being unwell. See 3 pictures... 'He had fever but was not granted leave' Neha Singh said her husband had been telling her over the phone for several days that he was suffering from fever and severe leg pain but was still being made to perform duty. She recalled that he called her on the night of August 4 to say he was feeling better and was returning to duty. In the early hours of the next morning, she received a phone call asking whether she had spoken to him recently. When she enquired about what had happened, she was only told that he had been injured before the call was disconnected. She alleged that she would fight for justice, even if it meant travelling to Manipur, and vowed to seek the dismissal of the commanding officer. Family demands post-mortem report The family said the post-mortem report should be made public so the exact cause of death could be established. They maintained that they would continue their fight for justice until their demands were met. CRPF officials handed over an ex gratia amount of ₹1 lakh to the widow. Jawan joined CRPF in 2009 Vineet Singh, a resident of Purwa Bajirao village in Hardoi district, joined the CRPF in 2009. He had recently been transferred from Jammu and Kashmir to Manipur. His body was flown from Manipur to Lucknow on Friday morning before being taken to his ancestral village for cremation. The funeral was attended by CRPF personnel from the 93rd Battalion, led by Assistant Commandant R.K. Tripathi. His elder brother, Anil Singh, performed the last rites. Vineet is survived by his father Deshraj Singh, his wife Neha Singh and their 12-year-old son, Rudra Pratap. Father cuts short pilgrimage The jawan's father, Deshraj Singh, had been undertaking the Kanwar pilgrimage to Baba Baidyanath Dham when he received news of his son's death. He immediately abandoned the pilgrimage and returned home. Meanwhile, Neha Singh has been living in a rented house in Budheshwar, Lucknow, where she is raising and educating their son.

stories.title: ‘My entire family is gone, how do I express this:Aman is sole survivor; says wait for government housing cost six lives in Pratapgarh house collapse
stories.summary: "No one can understand the pain of losing my family. In an instant, my whole world was destroyed... what can I say?" said Aman Srivastava from Pratapgarh, breaking down in tears. The young man, who had dreamed of building a better future with his loved ones, was forced to light the funeral pyres of six members of his own family, one after another, on Thursday. Speaking through tears, Aman said, "For the past five to six years, I had been trying to get a government house. I thought that once we got the house, I would celebrate my younger brother's wedding there. Now, neither the house nor my family is left." The tragedy struck at around 2am on Wednesday in Mahuli village, Pratapgarh. As heavy rain lashed the area, Pramod Srivastava's family was asleep in a room of their old, dilapidated house when two sections of the roof suddenly collapsed. Within moments, the entire family was buried beneath the debris. On Friday, Sadar MLA Rajendra Maurya visited Aman to offer his condolences. Calling the incident deeply tragic, he said the family had been applying for government housing for the past five years, but their application had reportedly been rejected twice. He assured that the matter would be investigated. Family lived in constant fear inside a crumbling house Aman said the family's house had become dangerously dilapidated. Plaster regularly fell from the ceilings and walls, leaving them fearful of a major accident. He said they had applied three times for government housing over the past five years, with two applications being rejected. According to Aman, their latest application under the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (PMAY) 2.0 had finally been approved, and officials had informed them that the funds would be credited within a month. "But before the money arrived, my entire family was taken away," he said. MLA promises probe into rejected housing applications Sadar MLA Rajendra Maurya described the incident as extremely unfortunate and said he would speak to the District Magistrate to investigate why the family's earlier housing applications had been rejected. He also announced that dilapidated buildings across the district would be surveyed to prevent similar tragedies and ensure that deserving families receive timely assistance. Sole survivor performs last rites of six family members After the post-mortem on Thursday at around 4.30pm, all six bodies were taken to the electric crematorium at Phaphamau Ganga Ghat in Prayagraj. Four adults were cremated separately, while the family's two young children were cremated together. Aman, the sole survivor, lit the funeral pyres of all six relatives with trembling hands. Overcome with grief, he fainted several times during the final rites and had to be supported by relatives and family members. Cousin seeks government job and compensation for Aman Aman's cousin, Ankur Srivastava, appealed to the government to provide Aman with a government job and financial compensation to help him rebuild his life. "Our entire family is now focused on helping Aman recover from this unimaginable loss. He has lost everyone. We are now his only support and will do everything possible to help him move forward," he said. See pictures of the accident- Family had returned from Mumbai only 18 months ago Pramod Srivastava had returned to his village around one-and-a-half years ago after leaving Mumbai, where he worked in medical marketing. After his health deteriorated, he moved back to Pratapgarh and began driving an e-rickshaw to support the family. His elder son Aman worked as an accountant at Mahuli Mandi. Pramod also ran a roadside vegetable stall. The family had slowly begun rebuilding their lives and had bought a new e-rickshaw about six weeks ago. They hoped their financial condition would improve and that they would soon be able to build a new home. ₹25 lakh raised by selling land, but new house never built The family owned around 13 biswa of land. About a year ago, Pramod sold three biswa, raising nearly ₹25 lakh to construct a new house. However, due to financial difficulties and other expenses, construction never began. Around 10 biswa of land still remained with the family. The family had also applied under the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana. According to relatives, they submitted applications three times over the past six years. Two were rejected, while the third was still under process. Entire family shared a single room Although the house appeared large from the outside, it had become structurally unsafe over the years. Only one room remained habitable, and the entire family slept there every night on three cots. They had also set up a small prayer area inside the room and installed an air conditioner to cope with the heat and humidity. Aman had planned to ease his father's financial burden once their new house was built and provide a better life for the family. Those dreams ended with the collapse. According to relatives, Pramod had planned to return to Mumbai and had booked a train ticket for 10 August. On the day of the accident, he had asked Aman to cancel the ticket. 6 members of the same family lost their lives, pictures- How the family's world collapsed in the early hours of Wednesday Six members of the same family were killed after their nearly 100-year-old house collapsed in Mahuli Mohalla under Nagar Kotwali police station limits in Pratapgarh during heavy rain on Wednesday night. All seven family members had been sleeping together in an air-conditioned room because of the heat and humidity. At around 2am, the roof suddenly gave way. The collapse was so sudden that no one had time to react or even call for help. Those killed were house owner Pramod Srivastava (60), his wife Rita (55), younger son Nitin (25), daughter-in-law Madhuri (23), and their two sons, Madhav (2) and Advik (10 months). According to preliminary findings, the victims died after being crushed under the debris and suffocating. The only survivor, 28-year-old Aman Srivastava, somehow managed to crawl out from the rubble and raised the alarm. Police and fire brigade teams rushed to the scene. After a rescue operation lasting around two hours, all seven family members were pulled from the debris and taken to the district hospital, where doctors declared six of them dead. The post-mortem found that several victims had suffered fatal internal injuries and multiple fractures. Aman is currently undergoing treatment in hospital. He is now the sole survivor of a family of seven.

stories.title: 'Babua will remain a child all his life':Yogi takes jibe at Akhilesh; says 'Evening gatherings were routine, change requires hitting the ground'
stories.summary: On National Handloom Day, CM Yogi Adityanath said that those who held power in the state before 2017 had no vision for development. When people in power are not interested in work, the state's deterioration is inevitable. Due to this irresponsibility, the state remained engulfed in months of curfews and riots. Innocent children died from diseases like encephalitis and dengue. Without naming the SP chief, Yogi took a jibe, saying: Some people get associated with a word in life that they can never shake off. Some people remain children throughout their lives. Babua was also like that. He would wake up at 12 noon, get ready by 2 pm, go to the gym at 5 pm, and by 7 pm the gathering would be in full swing. Then how could he think about the state's development? Read the key points from CM Yogi's speech Vote bank politics worsened the situation before 2017 The Chief Minister said that before the BJP government was formed in the country in 2014 and in UP in 2017, work for the development of artisans could have been done, but it requires thinking and vision. He listed three shortcomings of the SP government- 1- Deterioration of education: Earlier, basic schools were in bad condition. There was neither arrangement for drinking water nor toilets. Today, schools are providing bags, uniforms, and modern facilities. PM Modi's 'Nipun Bharat Abhiyan' is being implemented on the ground. 2. Security and Infrastructure: Before 2017, the state had neither electricity, nor roads, nor law and order. Daughters and traders were not safe. When markets remain deserted, it affects every artisan, woman, and youth. 3. Plunder and Insecurity: Previous governments had no interest in development works; there was just a race for plunder within the dynasty, and they themselves posed a threat to women's safety. Handloom and Handicrafts received a new identity CM Yogi stated that the handloom and powerloom industry is UP's great heritage. About 30 lakh people's livelihoods are connected to it, of which 70% are women workers. Last year, the government provided electricity facilities worth ₹109 crores to 40 thousand artisans. Before 2017, Bhadohi's carpet cluster had become almost inactive. Today, exports worth crores of rupees are happening from there to world markets. Prime Minister Narendra Modi himself took the initiative and had Bhadohi carpets laid in the country's new Parliament building. When we appreciate the sweat of our artisans and encourage them, the country's money will remain in the country and prosperity will reach directly to the homes of craftspeople. 'Chief Minister and Ministers have to descend into the field' CM Yogi said in the end that the transformation of the state is possible when the Chief Minister himself takes out time to visit every district and ministers go to ground zero. In our government, every scheme is reaching directly to the public without any discrimination and vote bank politics.

stories.title: Car gutted in Lucknow, youth burnt alive:Only skeleton left by the time fire brigade arrived; one hand found stuck in seat
stories.summary: A young man was burnt to death in a Maruti Zen car that caught fire around 11:30 PM on Thursday night in Lucknow. He could not get out of the car after it caught fire. By the time the fire brigade brought the fire under control, only his skeleton remained inside the car. The accident occurred near Saraiya Mod in the Bakshi Ka Talab (BKT) area. According to the police, the cause of the car fire is not yet clear. It is also not known whether the car caught fire while moving or if it was stationary at the time. The body has been sent for post-mortem. Young man's body found burnt on the driving seat ACP Vikas Pandey said that at around 11:30 PM, information was received about a car catching fire on the highway. When the police and fire brigade reached the spot, the car was completely engulfed in flames. After extinguishing the fire, when the car door was opened, a completely burnt body of a person was found on the driving seat. Only a skeleton remained on the seat. The forensic team was called upon receiving the information, and they collected evidence from the scene. In the initial investigation, the body could not be identified. Police identified based on car number Based on the car's number, the police traced its owner. Investigation revealed that the car was registered in the name of Almash, son of Hamidul, a resident of Khurramnagar. Upon contacting the family, it was confirmed that the body found inside the car was that of 32-year-old Almash. The ACP stated that the family is being interrogated. The cause of the car fire has not yet been clarified. The matter is being investigated keeping all aspects in mind. Another body found inside a car in Ashiana Meanwhile, the body of a person was recovered from an abandoned Swift Dzire car at Salenagar intersection in Ashiana police station area around 11:57 PM on Thursday night. According to local residents, the car had been parked on the roadside for the past three days. When a strong foul smell emanated from it on Thursday night, people informed the police. Upon receiving the information, Ashiana police reached the spot, took possession of the car, and started an investigation. During the search, the body was found inside the car. According to the police, the car's registration number is UP 33 BB 8989. The body was identified as Gyanendra Singh, son of Uday Bhan Singh, a resident of Niralanagar, Raebareli.

stories.title: VIDEO | 2 groups of schoolgirls clash outside Gorakhpur school:Argument escalates to physical altercation, hair-pulling
stories.summary: On Wednesday evening, after school hours, a fierce fight broke out between two groups of girl students at the gate of an inter college located in Chargaon, Shahpur area of Gorakhpur. First, there was an argument, which quickly escalated into a physical altercation. Someone viralized a video of this street fight on social media. It is being reported that on Wednesday evening around 4 PM, after school hours, the girl students came out of the school. During this, an argument started between two students over some issue. According to eyewitnesses, as the dispute escalated, students from one side started verbally abusing and physically assaulting the other student. During the incident, a crowd of passersby and other students gathered outside the school gate. Attempts were made to intervene, but both sides continued to clash with each other. Principal said - Investigation underway The school principal stated that as soon as information about the incident was received, the matter was taken seriously. On Thursday, the students involved in the dispute did not come to school. The entire matter is being investigated. Action will be taken as per rules if found guilty. The police say that no complaint has been received from either side so far. An investigation is also being conducted based on the video. The school administration has appealed to students and parents to maintain discipline.

stories.title: Auto-rickshaw driver's body found in Varuna river:Son says, 'Cop had been following him for three days'; police probe underway
stories.summary: A commotion erupted after the body of an auto driver was found in the Varuna River near Varuna Bridge in the Cantt police station area of Varanasi. The Kachahri outpost in-charge had reached the spot with police force upon receiving information about an abandoned auto standing on Varuna Bridge. A bottle of acid was found inside the auto. Following this, when police started searching, a body was found floating in the Varuna River. The police then informed the family members using the auto's number, retrieved the body, and sent it to the mortuary. The deceased's son, who reached the spot, alleged that his father had said that some policeman had been following him for three days. Meanwhile, police have started investigating the case. The causes of the incident are being ascertained through CCTV footage. Police arrived upon receiving information about an abandoned auto People had informed the Cantt police station that an abandoned auto bearing number UP 65 ET 8037 was standing on Varuna Bridge, with a bottle of acid kept in the front. The Kachahri outpost in-charge immediately reached the spot and gathered information about the auto, which was found to be registered in the name of Rajendra Prasad Gupta. On this, the chowki in-charge called, and they informed that their auto is driven by Gyanchand Sonkar. His number was taken and his family members were called. Boy who reached the spot made allegations After receiving information, Gyanchand Sonkar's son Ashish Sonkar reached the spot. Police got the auto identified. After that, when searched, a body was found floating in the Varuna. His son Ashish identified it as Gyanchand. Ashish said that during Sawan, everyone had gone to Ayodhya but father had not gone. For the past three days, he was saying that some policeman was following him. And today his body has been found. Police engaged in investigation Cantt Thana in-charge Raj Kishore Pandey said - The body has been taken out of the water and sent to the mortuary. The post-mortem of the body will be conducted today. stories.title: Abaan Ahmed suffered ruptured liver and lungs, broken ribs:Died from 23 injuries, post-mortem reveals; brother broke down upon seeing body
stories.summary: 23 injuries were found on the body of Abaan (21), son of mafia Atiq Ahmed, in Jhansi. The post-mortem report revealed that his liver, lungs, and spleen ruptured due to a high-impact collision. His ribs were also broken. He died due to excessive internal bleeding. Meanwhile, Sonu, Abaan's companion who was sitting behind Aban's seat in the car, died due to a fractured skull. Fractures were found in both his arms. Both were post-mortemed by a panel of 3 doctors at Jhansi Medical College on Thursday night at 11:30 PM. Aban's elder brother, Ahjam, reached inside the post-mortem house. Seeing the body of his brother Aban, he burst into tears. Relatives consoled him. After this, he asked the police for the post-mortem report. Officials said they would provide the report later. After the post-mortem, Ahjam, along with relatives, placed both bodies in the same ambulance. They departed for Prayagraj with the bodies at 12 AM. Both will be cremated today. On Thursday, Abaan was going to meet his elder brother Ali Ahmed, who is imprisoned in Abaan Jhansi Jail. Four friends were with him in the Creta car. His car collided with the divider in the Poonch area, 70 km before Jhansi on the Jhansi-Kanpur Highway. Aban and Sonu died in the accident. His 3 friends Umar Ahmed, Mohammad Zaid and Farooq Ahjam were injured. Dr. Rajneesh, who conducted the post-mortem, said- Both died due to injuries sustained in the accident. First, Aban's body was post-mortemed. After this, Sonu's body was post-mortemed. Both were post-mortemed along with Dr. Pankaj Mustaria and Dr. Zia Zafar. See 2 pictures of the accident- So much internal bleeding occurred in Abaan's body that it came out of his mouth. Aban was sitting in the front seat of the car. His friend Zaid was driving the car. Sonu was sitting behind Abaan. The car, travelling at a speed of about 120 km/h, hit the divider on the side where Abaan was sitting. This is why Aban sustained the most injuries in the accident. Shortly after the collision, Abaan and Sonu died on the spot. Eyewitness Deepak Yadav, who was the first to arrive after the accident, said - I heard the noise and was the first to reach. I tried to open the car door, but it wouldn't open. After that, I brought a crowbar (iron rod) from a house and broke the door. Deepak said - After opening the door, I first pulled out a young man. His mouth was full of blood. He said - My name is Aban, save me. After this, he became unconscious. Aban had left Prayagraj for Jhansi at 5 AM on Thursday. The Creta car hit the divider in the Poonch police station area. The impact was so strong that the car was thrown about 7 feet into the air. Its pieces were scattered about 40 feet across the highway. The left side of the car was severely damaged. Brother said - Let the brothers be brought for burial Upon receiving news of Abaan's death in the accident, his elder brother Ahjam reached Jhansi from Prayagraj. First, he reached the accident site and gathered information from the police. After this, he went directly to Jhansi Medical College. Here, he met all three injured. Ahjam said - Let the brothers be brought for burial. After Ahjam arrived, the police completed the inquest for both bodies and conducted post-mortems. Ahjam has also given a written complaint to the police, based on which the police may register a case. Sonu's brother-in-law, who arrived in Jhansi from Satna to collect Sonu's body, said - Sonu used to work with trailers. He had come home from Dubai some time ago. Here too, he was working with trailers. But currently, due to the Kanwariyas, work has stopped. He was a friend of car driver Zaid and other companions. That's why he was coming to Jhansi. Cigarettes, shoes and two books found in the car According to Jhansi police, the forensic team found cigarette packets, shoes, and two books in the car. These include 'The Idiot' and 'The Stationery Shop of Tehran'. According to the police, it is possible that Aban was carrying these items for his brother Ali. Abaan was sitting in the front seat of the car, while his companion Zaid was driving. Zaid is the son-in-law of Atiq's maternal cousin sister. He had received this car as a wedding gift. Now only 3 of Atiq's 5 sons remain Atiq Ahmed had 5 sons. Abaan was the youngest. One son, Asad, was killed in a police encounter in Jhansi in 2023. Now there are three sons. Among them, the elder son, Umar, is imprisoned in Lucknow Jail, and the second, Ali, is in Jhansi Jail. While Ahzam, older than Abaan, is currently pursuing his graduation. He has reached Jhansi. Seeing the body, he said, "Let the brothers be brought to the soil (buried)." Lawyer Umesh Pal was murdered in Prayagraj in February 2023. In this case, Atiq, imprisoned in Gujarat Jail, and his brother Ashraf, from Bareilly Jail, were brought to Prayagraj for a court appearance. There, on April 15, 2023, Atiq and Ashraf were murdered in police custody. Atiq's wife, Shaista, is currently absconding. Abaan's mother Shaista, carrying a reward of 50 thousand, is absconding Atiq's wife Shaista Parveen has been absconding since 2023. There is a reward of 50 thousand on her. There are 6 cases. Shaista did not attend the funerals of both her son Asad, after his encounter, and her husband Atiq, after his murder. Ashraf's wife Zainab is also absconding. Questions are being raised about whether Shaista will attend Aban's funeral. Murder took place in police custody Lawyer Umesh Pal was murdered in Prayagraj in February 2023. In this case, Atiq, who was imprisoned in a Gujarat jail, and his brother Ashraf, from Bareilly jail, were brought to Prayagraj for a hearing. There, on April 15, 2023, Atiq and Ashraf were murdered in police custody. Atiq's wife Shaista is currently absconding.

stories.title: Rain lashes Lucknow, highway flooded in Farrukhabad:River swallows 50 acres in Lakhimpur; rainfall 150% above normal in 24 hours
stories.summary: The spell of monsoon rain continues across Uttar Pradesh. Lucknow received rain early on Friday, while around 40 cities, including Agra and Jaunpur, remained cloudy. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a rain alert for all 75 districts today, with a heavy rainfall warning for 18 districts. According to the IMD, the state has received 19.3 mm of rainfall, which is 150% above the normal 7.8 mm. Heavy rain on Thursday evening inundated homes and schools in Bijnor. Waterlogging was reported on a national highway in Farrukhabad and in several residential areas. In Rae Bareli, a road caved in after the rain, leaving a three-foot-deep crater. Rivers are also in spate due to continuous rainfall. In Lakhimpur Kheri, the Sharda River has eroded around 50 acres of land so far. In Ballia, 27 houses have been washed away by the Saryu River. In Farrukhabad, the Ganga has risen close to the danger mark, with floodwater entering 33 villages and 40 government schools. The Ganga is also flowing above normal levels in Varanasi. Floodwater has entered 40–50 small temples, while the Ratneshwar Mahadev Temple is more than half submerged. A crocodile was spotted roaming on flooded roads in Lakhimpur Kheri. Forest department officials also rescued a Russell's viper that had entered a house and released it into the forest. Meanwhile, more than 20 cities, including Lucknow, Saharanpur and Meerut, received rainfall on Thursday morning. Due to continuous rain and rain-related incidents over the past three days, schools up to Class 8 have been closed. Rain-related accidents have also continued. In Barabanki, a dilapidated wall collapsed on five children on their way to a madrasa. All five were trapped under the debris. A 7-year-old boy and his 14-year-old sister died, while the other three children were rescued by villagers and taken to hospital. In Pratapgarh, a 100-year-old house collapsed amid continuous rain, killing 13 members of the same family. See pictures of floods and rain... Lucknow weather scientist Atul Kumar Singh said- The monsoon system has now become active over UP. It is passing through Delhi, Lucknow and Patna. Due to this, several cyclones have become active. Monsoon winds have reached the plains of the Ganges. Due to its effect, there will be heavy rainfall across the state for the next 4 to 5 days.

stories.title: Senior officials spared, juniors punished over Kanpur Expressway mess:Responsible officers cleared files blindly, without inspecting the site
stories.summary: The dilapidated condition of the country's most expensive Lucknow-Kanpur Expressway has ruined the image of the Union Ministry of Road Transport. The department and NHAI (National Highways Authority of India) are facing disrepute all around. NHAI had to blacklist the construction company of a BJP leader's brother. In a hurry, the Authority tried to show by taking action against some officers that it would not spare those responsible. But the truth is that there are others responsible on whom no action has been taken. Because when the expressway was being built for a long time, what were the officers sitting above doing? Did they check the quality or allow morang and asphalt to be laid based on estimates? Are those responsible for the shoddy construction being protected? In this report by Dainik Bhaskar, we will tell who else is responsible for this. First, let's tell which 3 officers NHAI held responsible and took action against them- Major culprits of the irregularity, against whom no action was taken Responsibility - NHAI's Regional Officer Gautam is based in Lucknow. His job is to monitor NHAI projects in UP and conduct quality checks through periodic site visits. Negligence - Initially, the first defect came to light on July 26. Then he tried to suppress the matter. He said there was a problem with bitumen (coal tar) in a small area. After the matter got out of hand, action was taken against the Project Manager and the Director. Dainik Bhaskar tried to contact Vishal Gautam. The call was answered, but immediately disconnected. When called again, the phone was not picked up. Responsibility - After Saurabh Chaurasia, Sharad became the Project Director of the Lucknow-Kanpur Expressway and remained in this position for about 1 year. He was responsible for managing important technical arrangements during construction. Negligence - During his tenure, instead of inspecting the quality by visiting the site, he blindly trusted files and reports. Due to less visits to ground zero, he kept approving every file with 'OK', overlooking construction deficiencies. Dainik Bhaskar tried to contact him, but it was not possible. Responsibility - He is the head of PNC Infratech, the company building the expressway. The company is named after 3 brothers - Pradeep, Naveen, and Chakresh. Naveen Jain is a Rajya Sabha MP from BJP. Negligence - Secured a two-phase tender by bidding a total of ?2926 crore, but paid no attention to site monitoring and quality control during construction. No concrete information could be found about them either. Could not be contacted despite efforts. Now know about two cases of irregularities, in which the company owner was held responsible- What was the responsibility of the officials against whom action was taken? Responsibility- He was the highest-ranking officer for construction work in the field. It was his responsibility to get every layer of soil and gravel inspected and send the report upwards. Negligence- Ignored quality and committed irregularities in the field. Action- On July 30, NHAI removed him from the project and banned him for 2 years. Responsibility- He remained Project Director from the start of construction until 2024. The maximum construction happened during his tenure. Negligence- Instead of inspecting on-site, he blindly trusted PNC's reports. The foundation of irregularities was laid during his time. Action- NHAI has issued a charge sheet, framing the charges. Responsibility- Posted in the position for the last 1 year. The work was completed and inaugurated during his tenure. Negligence- 95% of the Greenfield area work was completed a year ago. Still, they gave an 'all okay' report without checking the quality. Action- Removed from NHAI and attached to PWD. 3 Crores Spent to Repair Sunken Expressway According to NHAI, 3 crores have been spent so far on the repair of the 63 km long expressway. This cost will be borne by PNC Infratech. The company has also been fined 2% of the performance security. The negligence of Theme Engineering Services Private Limited, which monitors the quality of construction, has come to light. Therefore, this company will be excluded from future projects. NHAI itself is getting the quality checked After the embarrassment, NHAI will now get the expressway inspected with a laser profilometer. This technique uses a laser beam to measure the texture, roughness, and height of an object's surface. It creates an accurate 3D map of the surface without touching it, which will precisely reveal the irregularities. How is a non-performer company building the Bahraich Expressway? NHAI admitted that earthwork, drainage, and quality were overlooked. Still, NHAI officials avoided taking action against the company. PNC has been awarded the work for the expressway from Barabanki to Bahraich. PNC has also been given the work of constructing a flyover inside Lucknow city. PNC Company's 'Tarnished' Record

stories.title: Atiq Ahmed's son writhed in car for 2 minutes:'My name is Abaan, save me'; eyewitness recounts final moments
stories.summary: "My name is Abaan... save me." Only this much could come out of his mouth. People pulled him out of the car, but within two minutes of struggling, his breathing stopped. These were the last words of mafia Atiq Ahmed's youngest son Aban Ahmed (21). Abaan was going to meet his brother Ali, who was imprisoned in Jhansi jail. He had also bought two romantic novels for his brother. When Ali received the news of the accident in jail, he started crying. Abaan was very dear to him. Perhaps this was the reason why Abaan had met Ali 49 times in 10 months. Dainik Bhaskar's team spoke with eyewitnesses, the injured, and police. Read the complete story of the last moments of the accident... First, let's understand how the accident happened? Abaan Ahmed left for Jhansi, 400 kilometers away from Prayagraj, around 5 AM on Thursday with his 2 friends and 2 relatives. But an accident occurred 70 kilometers before reaching there. Near Khilli village in Poonch, while trying to save a calf that suddenly appeared on the highway, the Creta car went out of control. It crashed into a concrete wall built on the roadside. At that time, the car was traveling at a speed of about 120. The collision was so severe that the car flew about 7 feet in the air and its pieces scattered up to 40 feet on the highway. In the accident, Abaan and his friend Sonu died on the spot, while three people were injured. Broke car doors with rods and pulled people out Eyewitness Sakesh said, ''I was working at my shop. Suddenly there was a loud explosion. It felt like something had burst. Several people present around the shop ran to the spot. Saw that there was a severe car collision. Immediately called 112 and got an ambulance. Until the ambulance and police arrived, we ourselves got engaged in rescuing the injured and trapped people. The car doors were jammed. Before the police arrived, we broke the doors with iron rods and pulled out the injured. Later, the police and ambulance took them to the hospital.'' Accident while trying to save a calf, car crashed into wall Eyewitness Deepak Yadav said - I was going from home to the field. Then I saw that a calf was crossing the highway. To save it, the car driver turned the vehicle to the left. Meanwhile, a biker came, and to save him, the car driver turned the car even more to the left. The very next moment, the car crashed into a wall built on the roadside. Some people came running. The injured were pulled out of the car. One injured person's mouth was filled with blood. When we asked his name, he said, "My name is Abaan. Save me." After this, he didn't say anything. His breathing stopped. 10 minutes after calling, the police arrived at the spot. The police took all the injured to the hospital in an ambulance. One part of the car was damaged; Aban-Sonu were sitting on this side According to the police, 5 people were sitting in the car. Mohammad Zaid (35) was driving the vehicle, and Abaan Ahmad (21) was sitting next to him. Sonu (24) was on the seat behind Abaan. Next to Sonu were Umar Ahmad (18) and Farooq Ahjam (28). The car was running close to the middle divider. The car crashed into a concrete wall built on the roadside towards the village. The front part was completely shattered. All airbags deployed. The left side of the car was more damaged. Abaan was sitting in the front on this side, and Sonu was sitting in the back. Both sitting on the left side died on the spot. Aban suffered serious head injuries. His hands and legs were broken. Aban-Sonu kept writhing in pain for 2 to 5 mins Eyewitness Ramakant said - Abaan and Sonu kept struggling for about two to five minutes, then their breathing stopped. Ambulance driver Pravesh said - All the injured were brought to CHC Moth. From there, I brought one injured person, Umar, to Jhansi Medical College. He had a fracture in his hand. The condition of all three injured was normal; they were talking. Village head Brijesh Kumar said - The car hit the divider due to loss of balance. The car's speed was high. After the accident, about 50 villagers and I reached the spot. Injured Mohammad Umar said - Car hit the divider Mohammad Umar, injured in the accident, said - The car was at high speed. Suddenly, after losing control, it crashed into the divider. The collision was so severe that Abaan and his friend Sonu died on the spot. Umar was not informed about brother Abaan's death Lucknow Jail's Jailer Ritwik Priyadarshi said - Atiq's elder son Umar has not been informed about Abaan's death. Information is given only as per the protocol prescribed in the jail. Family members have contacted lawyers of Prayagraj District Court to allow Atiq Ahmed's two sons imprisoned in jail to participate in Abaan's funeral.
