stories.summary: Supriya Sule opposes the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026, in its current form. She urges the government to withdraw the proposed legislation or send it to a Joint Parliamentary Committee. Foreign funding should not be viewed with automatic suspicion, she stated during her remarks. Sule also commented on youth protests and disputes over political party symbols. The NCP (SP) leader awaits a hearing on the party's legal battle.

stories.title: Explainer: What changes as Parliament passes Registration of Births and Deaths Bill
Color-changing packaging flags meat spoilage before it’s visible
JPSC, E20, anti-reservation: The issues India is talking about
A Swedish couple moved into the dream home in Malmö; three years later, they left it behind for a rural home in Japan
stories.summary: After recently selling their newly constructed home in Sweden, a Swedish couple has made the bold decision to embrace a fresh start by purchasing an empty residence in Japan. This significant change stems from their evolving family aspirations and a burgeoning affection for Asia. They are now excited to undertake renovations on their Japanese abode while immersing themselves in the enchanting culture and scenery of Japan.

stories.title: Flesh-eating bacteria kill 5 in Louisiana, health officials warn beachgoers as all cases are linked to seawater
Who is Sunder Katwala? Indian-origin writer appointed to UK community funding body
21 of 57 TN MPs attend CM Vijay’s meet, reject Delimitation Bill; DMK, AIADMK stay away
India to recover 'Green Boots' climber's body from Everest after 30 years: Report
'We stand in solidarity': CJP delegation reaches Ranchi to support students protesting JPSC, JSSC exams
US Democrats eye probes into Trump-linked firms over impeachment if they regain House control: Report
stories.summary: In a significant move, US House Democrats are gearing up for extensive investigations into the business practices of the Trump administration. Their strategy involves utilizing hearings and subpoenas to scrutinize decisions made that may have led to personal gains. Major corporations such as Apple and Alphabet might find themselves under examination for their regulatory and contractual engagements.

stories.title: 'End this war': Senate Democrats turn up heat on Trump, seek end to Iran hostilities
stories.summary: Democrats introduced a resolution to end unauthorized US military involvement against Iran. Senator John Hickenlooper leads the effort, citing constitutional war powers. This move escalates a congressional challenge to President Donald Trump's handling of the conflict. Military leaders privately advise seeking an off-ramp from ongoing air operations. President Trump expresses confidence that the confrontation could end soon.

stories.title: Utah wildfire: Helicopter with 2 onboard crashes while fighting massive blaze
'Which freedom fighter received most severe punishment?' Kerala orders probe into Savarkar quiz
stories.summary: A school quiz question in Kerala has ignited a political controversy. The question asked about the freedom fighter receiving the most severe British punishment. General education minister N Samsudheen ordered an inquiry into the unauthorized quiz. Opposition parties accused the government of promoting a Sangh Parivar agenda. Officials are investigating who prepared and conducted the quiz.

stories.title: American entrepreneur says 'I'm shocked but honestly not surprised' as US plans to remove 60-day grace period for H-1Bs
'Army safeguarding territory': Arunachal CM Pema Khandu rejects Chinese encroachment
Evening newswrap: Mayawati hits Akhilesh over 'Pandit' twist in SP's PDA formula; IT ministry asks Meta to revamp algorithms & more
Syrian spy chief accused of 2015 'Children's Massacre' hiding in Moscow: Report
Korean proverb of the day and its lessons: 'If you don't walk today, you must run tomorrow'
A new Kansas law now bars students from accessing phones, earbuds and smartwatches all school day
stories.summary: Many states are banning smartphones in schools due to growing distractions and health concerns. Some districts now restrict student phone access from morning bell to afternoon dismissal. Parents are increasingly supporting these bans, citing research and developmental appropriateness. Concerns also focus on excessive screen time and inappropriate content accessed on school devices. Schools are now reviewing technology policies and limiting device usage during non-instructional periods.

stories.title: SAD backs women's quota, delimitation bills after Badal-PM Modi meet fuels buzz
stories.summary: Shiromani Akali Dal has expressed strong support for the prompt enactment of the women's reservation bill, emphasizing the need for fair delimitation to ensure equitable state representation. This advocacy follows a meeting between party president Sukhbir Singh Badal and Prime Minister Narendra Modi. Speculation is rife regarding a potential electoral partnership between SAD and BJP, particularly as both parties have faced declining influence in Punjab's political landscape.

stories.title: 56 decomposing bodies found at Chicago funeral home; owner’s licence suspended
Senate confirms Trump’s ex-lawyer Todd Blanche as US Attorney General
Colorado teen Jude Kofie taught himself piano at 10; now his debut album is out after $15,000 gift
stories.summary: Colorado teenager Jude Kofie has released his debut album, showcasing his piano skills. He taught himself to play the piano by ear at age ten. A generous piano tuner gifted him a valuable instrument and professional lessons. His album features diverse musical styles, including jazz and gospel influences. This release marks a significant milestone in his developing musical career.

stories.title: IT ministry asks Meta to revamp algorithms, submit roadmap to tackle deepfakes
'Congress not realising own errors': Rijiju draws parallel with Indira Gandhi post Emergency
stories.summary: Parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju criticized the Congress party for its perceived lack of self-awareness. He contrasted the current leadership with former Prime Minister Indira Gandhi's admission of Emergency actions. Rahul Gandhi questioned the delay in implementing the Women's Reservation Bill. He urged its immediate implementation without linking it to delimitation. The bill's passage and subsequent implementation remain a point of contention.

stories.title: Greenland issues ‘strong warning’ over Arctic drilling by Trump-linked firm
stories.summary: A US oil firm has moved equipment to Greenland without local approval. This action occurs while President Trump seeks greater US influence over the territory. Greenland's government issued a strong warning regarding the unauthorized logistical operation. The company plans to drill for oil, which faces environmental and political questions. The situation highlights Greenland's resource development authority amid US strategic interests.

stories.title: 'A morning I will cherish': Raghav Chadha's first social media post with PM Modi
Congress lost the millennials. Can it win over Gen Z?
stories.summary: Rahul Gandhi is focusing on forging a bond with the youth ahead of the 2029 elections, recognizing that Gen Z will be a key voting bloc.

stories.title: US Senate passes stopgap funding bill to avert shutdown ahead of midterms
stories.summary: In a decisive move, the US Senate has passed a temporary spending bill aimed at funding government operations until December eleventh. This crucial legislation is designed to avert a government shutdown just before the midterm elections. Key components of the bill address border patrol funding as requested by Democrats and extend the deadline for enforcing a federal prohibition on certain hemp products by a month.

stories.title: 10-year-old baker's grand champion cake fetches $15,000 at Maryland county fair auction
stories.summary: At a recent county fair auction, a remarkable cake created by 10-year-old baker Herbie Martin IV fetched an astounding $15,000. Herbie dedicated countless late-night hours to master his delightful lemon blueberry recipe. This impressive sale contributed to an overall fundraising goal, raising more than $100,000 for upcoming fairs and youth initiatives, with Herbie's cake standing out as the highlight of the event.

stories.title: Green Bank Radio Restrictions: Tiny US town lives under radio-silence laws
US officials will not release cool water from Glen Canyon Dam this year, protecting hydropower while threatening humpback chub
stories.summary: This year, federal officials have decided against releasing cool water from the Colorado River reservoirs, emphasizing the need for hydropower production over the conservation of a threatened fish species. The river and its reservoirs are facing severe depletion from overuse and climate change, while states have been unable to reach a long-term agreement on water sharing. Utilities welcomed this choice, citing concerns over the costs of alternative energy sources.

stories.title: 'Changing colours like a chameleon': Mayawati hits Akhilesh over 'Pandit' twist in SP's PDA formula
stories.summary: BSP chief Mayawati criticized the Samajwadi Party's changing political stance. She accused the SP of altering its PDA formula for electoral gains. Mayawati stated the SP now targets Brahmin voters after noticing BSP's growing support. She urged all communities to remain vigilant against SP's casteist politics. Such deceptive strategies offer short-term benefits but not societal welfare.

stories.title: US Fire Service In Antarctica: Frozen desert fuels fire risk
Researchers map 100+ lakes in Brazil, Uruguay that could warn of ecosystem collapse
Zebra mussels are collapsing structures and pipes in Spain's Ebro River since 2001 with a population of 40,000 per square meter
stories.summary: Zebra mussels are proliferating swiftly in Spain's aquatic systems, resulting in considerable harm to infrastructure and creating disturbances in water supply. Experts advocate that modifying infrastructure represents the only effective long-term remedy. The mere removal of adult mussels fails to address the persistent issue of shell buildup. This invasive species has already led to substantial economic repercussions, which are projected to escalate.

stories.title: Kinshasa Growth Deepens Poverty: World Bank data tracks soaring population
'Keep your curiosity alive': PM Modi addresses IIT Delhi graduates; highlights rapid tech shift
stories.summary: During a momentous Saturday at IIT Delhi's 57th Convocation Ceremony, Prime Minister Narendra Modi inspired the graduates to welcome transformation and continually nurture their thirst for knowledge. He emphasized the importance of mentors and the networks that support their journeys. Modi also spotlighted India's commitment to self-reliance and the birth of innovative sectors, marking the occasion by inaugurating a cutting-edge AI-powered supercomputing facility.

stories.title: 'Is India truly independent?' Congress targets Centre over US Bill on Russia sanctions
stories.summary: Congress leader Pawan Khera has raised concerns about India's autonomy when it comes to purchasing Russian oil. He criticized the government's unwillingness to confront Parliament over this pressing issue. Additionally, Khera expressed solidarity with students in Jharkhand protesting recruitment irregularities, emphasizing that it's a collective duty of all political parties to address student grievances. Meanwhile, Rahul Gandhi's forthcoming initiative aims to spotlight youth challenges and the aspirations of job seekers.

stories.title: China’s hanging coffins had no known builders. Ancient DNA points to Bo people
Spain's blood-red Río Tinto may hold clues to life on Mars, Nasa says
stories.summary: The Río Tinto in Spain captivates with its vivid red and orange colors, a result of both its ancient geology and extensive mining activities. In this caustic environment, specialized microorganisms flourish by harnessing energy from iron and sulfur compounds. Over millennia, mining has intensified these natural chemical reactions, further enhancing the river’s striking look. NASA's interest lies in finding similar minerals to explore potential Martian life.

stories.title: ‘Should have been more’: PM Modi disappointed over 'just one or two' girls among IIT Delhi medal winners
‘Honey-trapped’ IAF officer held for allegedly sharing classified defence data
Texas A&M creates 17-ft fire whirl; burns oil faster, cuts soot, uses up to 95% fuel
LA homeless nonprofit paid Hawaii-based CEO $1.6M over two years, including $824K in unused vacatio
Sick teen dies as ambulance gets stuck in mud for hours in J&K's Rajouri
Centre seeks Meta's action on deepfakes, awaits legal opinion on further steps
When ‘healthy’ is just a label
stories.summary: From ‘natural’ and ‘organic’ to ‘zero maida’ and ‘heart healthy’, the regulator is questioning whether front-of-pack promises are supported by what is inside.

stories.title: Rijiju vs Rahul over women's quota Bill: Support 'unconditionally' remark gets 'already passed' retort
stories.summary: Union minister Kiren Rijiju has called upon Rahul Gandhi to lend his 'unconditional' support to the Women's Reservation Bill. This appeal came after Gandhi's comments highlighting the necessity of women's freedom of expression for India's comprehensive development. While the opposition has shown its backing for the bill, they contest its connection to delimitation. The Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam, 2023, is set to be implemented following parliamentary approval.

stories.title: QR code, no queue: 25 crore OPD registrations go digital
Zach Dell co-founded Base Power in 2023; now valued at $13 billion it has installed more than 23,000 home batteries
stories.summary: Base Power, led by Zach Dell, is revolutionizing residential energy with its advanced battery storage solutions. Having secured a staggering one billion dollars in funding, the company now boasts a valuation of thirteen billion dollars. With thousands of batteries quickly being installed, they are expanding their reach into additional states.

stories.title: Pumas are protecting human lives by preventing vehicle collisions accounting for a 76% reduction in accidents
stories.summary: Pumas in Washington's Olympic Peninsula play a crucial role in decreasing deer-related accidents on highways. By changing deer movement patterns to avoid roads and nighttime activities, they enhance safety for people traveling in the area. This study underscores the significant environmental services provided by large carnivores, demonstrating the importance of coexisting with such majestic species for community well-being.

stories.title: Akal Takht panel asks Punjab govt to address objections before anti-sacrilege talks
stories.summary: On Thursday, an expert panel from Akal Takht convened to deliberate on the proposed anti-sacrilege law. They highlighted that the Punjab government’s response failed to address critical concerns and urged it to submit a compliance report prior to any further discussions. Additionally, the panel observed that the government had yet to create its own discussion group, emphasizing that this sensitive topic demands a broader Panthic agreement for effective resolution.

stories.title: 17.4 lakh blood components discarded in 2025 despite record collection
FSSAI pulls up two popular food products over safety, compliance lapses
Pentagon strips ex-Air Force secy of security clearance over Air Force One claim
India digest: Nagpur flat owner booked in minor rape case; CBI charges 11 in Suvendu PA case
Sanchez vs Meloni: Spain imposes Italy border checks as Ceuta migrant row escalates
stories.summary: Spain has implemented temporary border checks on travelers arriving by air and sea from Italy, intensifying tensions between these two European Union nations regarding migration policies. Italy had previously enacted similar measures following a significant influx of migrants into Spain. This ongoing conflict underscores the contrasting perspectives on border regulations and the management of migrants within the European Union.

stories.title: Nod for Ganga eway extensionn to Haridwar
Om Birla seeks proposal for Makar Dwar porch
stories.summary: In a recent request, Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla has called for the construction of a new porch to shield MPs and staff from rain at Makar Dwar. CPWD officials will investigate whether this covered entryway can be constructed, especially as the expenses for the new Parliament House project have surged. The proposed porch will offer a protective haven during vehicle wait times.

stories.title: No government role, don’t endorse Hasina’s remarks at private media event: MEA
stories.summary: In a recent statement, India expressed its disapproval of the comments made by former Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina. The Ministry of External Affairs emphasized that India was uninvolved in the private media event, leading to Bangladesh's fierce reaction. Dhaka labeled the event as an attack on its sovereignty, asserting that it offends the sentiments of its people and threatens already delicate bilateral relations.

stories.title: Ex-HC judge on West Bengal SIR tribunal in Supreme Court seeking protection
stories.summary: A former judge of the Calcutta High Court has approached the Supreme Court for protection, citing numerous death threats issued to her and her family ahead of elections. Reports indicate that they received threatening letters, and CCTV wires were tampered with at their residence. Despite submitting complaints, local police failed to provide adequate safety measures.

stories.title: BJP picks audio clip to target Congress over Karnataka ‘cabinet berths’
stories.summary: The BJP has claimed that funds were involved in securing ministerial roles in Karnataka, referencing a leaked audio exchange among Congress officials. BJP representatives have called for clarification from Congress leaders Kharge and Rahul Gandhi, alleging that cabinet positions were obtained through financial means. One BJP leader also raised concerns about the inclusion of an accused figure in the newly formed cabinet.

stories.title: Prime Minister flags Parliament disruptions with new NDA entrants
stories.summary: Prime Minister Modi highlighted the unwavering stability of his administration since 2014, remarking on the contrasting volatility of leadership in Britain. He embraced new members into the NDA coalition, asserting that their partnership is attuned to regional interests and developmental needs. Additionally, Modi underscored the critical necessity for growth in eastern India, showcasing a dedication to inclusive progress.

stories.title: PM Modi's meet with Badal fuels buzz about BJP-SAD pact
stories.summary: Sukhbir Singh Badal, the president of the Shiromani Akali Dal, recently met with Prime Minister Narendra Modi, igniting discussions about a possible revival of their political alliance in Punjab. While the BJP has declared intentions to run independently in the upcoming elections, support for reconnecting with the Akali Dal exists among some state leaders. This split could inadvertently benefit the Aam Aadmi Party amid multifaceted party dynamics.

stories.title: Opposition wants Amit Shah in House; government says 'not your call'
stories.summary: Opposition protests continue, lampooning Home Minister Amit Shah for his absence from Parliament. Parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju stated the opposition cannot dictate ministerial attendance. He asserted Shah is actively working and his presence deters extremists and terrorists. Opposition MPs disrupted proceedings, demanding Shah address police action against protesters. The Lok Sabha passed a bill amid the din, with further confrontation anticipated.

stories.title: Tribunal reforms bill gets nod, paves way for national body
stories.summary: The Cabinet has approved the Tribunals Reforms Bill, which establishes a National Tribunal Commission. This independent body will oversee appointments and functioning of approximately sixteen tribunals. The Supreme Court had previously directed the government to constitute this commission. Concerns were raised about tribunals becoming a liability for the judiciary. The bill will be introduced in the Lok Sabha soon.

stories.title: Supeme Court to Mahua: Freedom fighters faced bullets, you fear eggs
stories.summary: The Supreme Court denied Mahua Moitra's appeal for a virtual appearance in front of the police, as she expressed concerns over potential mob violence and egg-throwing incidents. In response, the court referenced the sacrifices of freedom fighters, suggesting that her fears may be unfounded. The session was overseen by Justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu, with the MP's legal team advocating for video conferencing.

stories.title: Supreme Court seeks Bihar minister's record of appointment & nomination as MLC
stories.summary: The Supreme Court has requested records from Bihar regarding a minister's appointment. This minister was not an assembly member and faced a six-month deadline. He was later nominated as an MLC, which the government claims resolves the issue. The petitioner cited a 2001 judgment on non-legislator minister re-appointments. The court seeks documents on his initial appointment and subsequent re-induction.

stories.title: Supreme Court dismisses Bofors appeal, 4-decade-old case closed
stories.summary: The Supreme Court has officially dismissed an appeal that sought to challenge a 2005 Delhi High Court ruling, effectively concluding the contentious Bofors pay-off case. Advocate Ajay K Agrawal, who filed the appeal, requested an adjournment, but the court declined to extend the timeline on this matter dating back to 2018, which involved accusations against the Hinduja brothers and AB Bofors.

stories.title: No conflict of interest in RDI Fund, says government
stories.summary: The government has staunchly defended the Research, Development and Innovation Fund's comprehensive framework. Officials have emphasized that the presence of strict conflict-of-interest protocols in public funding decisions is paramount. They asserted that a basic professional relationship does not breach any regulations, and measures such as full disclosure and recusal help maintain equitable assessment of all initiatives. For decades, the Technology Development Board has upheld these essential safeguards.

stories.title: Debate Scope Sparks Clash: Andrew Wilson presses Candace Owens on her claims; X spat intensifies
stories.summary: Candace Owens and Andrew Wilson have clashed publicly over the terms of their planned debate. Owens said the discussion should focus on the Tyler Robinson case and rejected a proposed cross-examination format. Wilson responded that the debate should also examine Owens' own claims about the case and Kirk's assassination. The exchange went viral after critics accused Owens of avoiding scrutiny, fueling widespread online discussion before the debate even begins.

stories.title: Eyeing framework to regulate OTT content: I&B min
stories.summary: The I&B ministry is exploring new legislation targeting OTT platforms. This proposed framework prioritizes the regulation of offensive content while preserving users' rights. Plans include implementing robust age verification mechanisms and parental controls. Additionally, an independent review panel will be tasked with evaluating flagged content following its release and determining appropriate sanctions for any breaches of the established guidelines.

stories.title: Share data on river waters, India tells China
stories.summary: India and China participated in candid discussions regarding border conditions, taking stock of the current landscape along the Line of Actual Control. New Delhi highlighted the necessity of maintaining peace for the advancement of their bilateral relationship. Furthermore, India sought an expedited meeting on the expert committee for trans-border rivers amidst China's unveiling of a significant dam project upstream.

stories.title: Delhi high court stays food regulator's ban on certain Dabur products
stories.summary: The Delhi High Court has temporarily halted an FSSAI directive that questioned Dabur India's product claims. Acknowledging Dabur's established market presence, the court provided initial relief. The order from FSSAI was deemed unjust, as it was issued without company representation. Dabur emphasized that the FSSAI's approach contravened principles of natural justice. The case is set for a further hearing on August 24.

stories.title: ‘Little hope of tracing 2 missing sailors’, Centre informs Supreme Court
stories.summary: Two Indian seafarers remain missing after a drone attack on a merchant ship. Intense search operations have yielded no sign of the missing sailors. The government informed the Supreme Court about the grim situation. The court directed facilitation of maritime insurance payments for the families. This ensures support for the affected families during this difficult time.

stories.title: Air India salary hikes salaries of pilots by up to 15%
stories.summary: Air India has announced a significant pay rise for pilots, ranging from eight to fifteen percent, with commanders seeing the most substantial hikes. In a strategic move to resolve fleet shortages and improve career advancement opportunities, first officers will gain command upgrades at Air India Express first. Moreover, the airline plans to resume its international flight services next month, marking a return to normal operations.

stories.title: NCAER: Bihar booze ban hasn't worked; lift it, fund development work
stories.summary: A recent study advocates for the removal of prohibition in Bihar to foster state growth and enhance capital spending. It posits that banning alcohol hasn't curbed crime rates but instead has spurred illicit activities. By abolishing the prohibition, the state could potentially enjoy a tax revenue boost of 14 to 15 percent.

stories.title: Supreme Court shunts out two coal scam judges on unusual Delhi high court request
stories.summary: Supreme Court has replaced two special judges hearing coal scam cases in Delhi. The Delhi High Court requested their transfer for other judicial responsibilities. Judges Sunena Sharma and Dheeraj Mor were moved after serving for varying durations. Virender Kumar Kharta and Ajay Garg will now preside over these important cases. Both transferred judges have been attached to the principal district and sessions judge office.

stories.title: India’s crude import bill up 26% in ’26-27 Q1 despite 18% volume fall
stories.summary: In the first quarter of the year, India's crude oil import bill surged by twenty-six percent compared to last year, reaching forty-nine billion dollars, up from thirty-nine billion. Despite an eighteen percent drop in import volumes, rising oil prices, fueled by ongoing conflicts, significantly impacted costs. Russia emerged as India's primary crude supplier, contributing over forty percent, and refiners incurred substantial war-risk premiums to ensure a reliable energy supply.

stories.title: Government in Supreme Court: Audio clips linking Biren to Manipur unrest doctored
stories.summary: The Centre informed the Supreme Court about the manipulation of audio recordings, with forensic analyses revealing several modifications. The court has instructed that the most recent forensic report be provided to the Kuki Organisation, which is pursuing an inquiry into audio clips that allegedly implicate Biren Singh. Furthermore, the Supreme Court mandated that copies of the report be distributed to both involved parties.

stories.title: Post Pahalgam, panel proposes security boost at major J&K sites
stories.summary: A parliamentary committee proposed an integrated security framework for Jammu and Kashmir's tourist spots. This includes comprehensive CCTV coverage and centralized monitoring facilities for enhanced safety. Clear inter-agency standard operating procedures are also recommended before peak tourist seasons. These suggestions follow a terror attack and a committee visit to assess security arrangements. The committee noted sustained growth in tourist arrivals due to improved security and infrastructure.

stories.title: Government maps 27 Arunachal border locations with standard names
stories.summary: India has taken a decisive step by officially naming twenty-seven sites in Arunachal Pradesh on its maps, a move designed to clarify territorial boundaries and counter Chinese assertions. These sites represent key historical moments related to border conflicts, featuring important mountains and villages along the McMahon Line, helping to raise awareness of India's rightful claims on these significant lands.

stories.title: YRG Cobblemon Racism Controversy: JayMommy hits back at critics; streamer vows to stay
stories.summary: JayMommy has responded to the criticism surrounding her comments during the YRG Cobblemon event, standing by her position and calling many of her critics “losers.” She also confirmed she will keep playing on the YRG Cobblemon server despite the backlash. Meanwhile, YourRAGE briefly reacted to the situation, saying he hoped everyone involved was okay.

stories.title: WhatsApp clue, Mygate trail help CBI crack NEET paper leak
stories.summary: A WhatsApp conversation triggered the CBI's probe into the NEET-UG examination scam. Subject matter experts colluded by memorizing exam questions and distributing them to students for a fee. Tracking through Mygate app logs and WhatsApp groups led investigators to the involved students and question setters. Additionally, papers were smuggled to Rajasthan, where coaching centers disseminated the leaked materials. The CBI's chargesheet scrutinizes the organized gang's exploitation of NTA's weaknesses.

stories.title: FCRA Bill 'internal matter': India rejects US criticism
stories.summary: The government is set to expedite the Foreign Contributions Regulation Act, which focuses on managing foreign funding for organizations. In contrast to criticism from a US Congressman regarding proposed changes, the administration remains resolute. Home Minister Amit Shah has met with church leaders to resolve their issues. The Bill's discussion and possible approval in Parliament are imminent.

stories.title: Quote by Thomas Aquinas: 'Better to illuminate than merely to shine, to deliver to others...'
stories.summary: Thomas Aquinas championed the notion of disseminating wisdom for the greater good of society. He drew a distinction between individual brilliance and the act of enlightening others. This thirteenth-century principle is still highly relevant in contemporary leadership practices, stressing the importance of making intricate knowledge understandable for all. True expertise is demonstrated through the ability to clarify ideas and enhance collective understanding.

stories.title: Quote of the day by Ernest Hemingway: 'Always do sober what you said you'd do drunk. That will teach you to keep your mouth shut' and a funny lesson on self-discipline
Quote of the day by Warren Buffett: 'The most important thing to do if you find yourself in a hole is to stop digging' and a useful business lesson
'Don't be like Yasmin': US makes an example out of Venezuelan woman arrested by ICE, says you are illegal if...
Quote of the day by Blaise Pascal: 'All of humanity's problems stem from man's inability to...'
stories.summary: In today's fast-paced world, the age-old human inclination to dodge self-reflection has intensified. Individuals often turn to myriad distractions to avoid confronting uncomfortable thoughts and feelings. This constant quest for entertainment can lead to poor decision-making and decreased well-being. Modern psychological approaches emphasize the importance of fostering moments of stillness and reflection, as understanding this behavior is essential in facing both personal and societal hurdles.

stories.title: 'Who introduced them?' US senator says it's odd to see Justin Trudeau frolicking around Katy Perry; 'He used to be in charge of a whole country'
Iltija faces FIR, questioning over 'assault' on cop, accuses police of manhandling; Omar calls it 'fixed match'
stories.summary: Omar Abdullah, J&K chief minister, labeled the Iltija Mufti incident a contrived event, alleging that agencies are working to bolster the PDP's tarnished political standing. Iltija Mufti faced interrogation regarding an alleged attack on a police officer, asserting that she experienced rough treatment by police during a protest. She emphasised that her struggles represent the desires of all Kashmiris, rather than being a personal crusade.

stories.title: Police put up posters of Lashkar commander across J&K, declare Rs 15L reward
stories.summary: Authorities are on the hunt for Lashkar commander Mohammad Lateef Bhat throughout Kashmir and Jammu, offering a significant cash reward for information that can lead to his capture. Bhat has been linked to the targeted murders of a police officer and two migrants. In a separate incident, an SUV attempted to run over officers at a Ramban checkpoint, resulting in one arrest after the vehicle was seized.

stories.title: California lost as many as 1.3 million Joshua trees in the 2020 Dome Fire
stories.summary: California scientists developed digital tools to map fire damage in the Mojave National Preserve. These new software programs help park managers focus restoration work on vulnerable desert plants. The tools assist in assessing post-fire conditions and developing recovery plans for affected areas. Scenario modeling directs limited conservation resources to high-elevation climate refugia for Joshua trees. This technology aims to improve the chances of survival for these iconic desert plants.

stories.title: 'Fake news, AI-generated': MEA dismisses report of India requesting defence pact with Israel after Mecca agreement
India counters China's 'map war', assigns official names to 27 Arunachal sites
stories.summary: India ahs onsistently rejected Beijing's practice of assigning Chinese names to places in Arunachal Pradesh, describing the exercise as "vain and preposterous". India has maintained that such actions do not change the "undeniable" fact that the state "was, is, and will" remain an integral part of the country. Several of the newly marked locations hold strategic importance because of their proximity to the Line of Actual Control (LAC).

stories.title: A Cumberland mother's new farm stand was stolen before she could use it; strangers....
stories.summary: On its inaugural night, a mother’s bakery stand faced an unfortunate theft. However, a compassionate construction duo—a father and son team—came to the rescue, reconstructing the entire stand at no cost. They meticulously followed the original design, delivering a perfect replica within a week. With security enhancements now in place, the bakery has officially reopened, bringing sweet treats back to the community.

stories.title: Indian-origin hiker found alive after 3 nights stranded on Vancouver Island
Billionaire Michael Moritz and Harriet Heyman are offering up to $150 million for ideas that...
stories.summary: Billionaires Michael Moritz and Harriet Heyman have launched an ambitious $150 million initiative aimed at enhancing San Francisco. Through their foundation, Crankstart, they invite innovative solutions to tackle urgent housing and economic challenges. Organizations can compete for funding, with the evaluation process culminating in a decision set for autumn 2027. This competition highlights the city's increasing dependency on private philanthropy in addressing critical public needs.

stories.title: 'Stop buying petrol, diesel vehicles until govt clarifies stand': Arvind Kejriwal over E20 fuel concerns
stories.summary: Addressing a press conference in Goa, Kejriwal said, "Till such a time, the government makes its intention clear, I appeal to the people to stop buying petrol and diesel vehicles. The government did not conduct any testing for E20 fuel."

stories.title: 'More like humiliation than rejection': Indian PSU employee denied US tourist visa in 20 seconds, says never going to apply again
Jharkhand government holds talks with protesting students, promises to consider demands
National Handloom Day: Yogi Adityanath salutes artisans, recalls Swadeshi Movement's legacy
stories.summary: Yogi Adityanath on Thursday paid tribute to the state's weaving community, describing handloom artisans as preservers of India's cultural heritage

stories.title: "Our top priority is pilgrims' safety": Uttarakhand CM Dhami on Char Dham, Kanwar Yatra
stories.summary: Uttarakhand Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami on Friday said that the Char Dham Yatra is being stopped intermittently, keeping in mind the safety of pilgrims as the state continues to face heavy rainfall and landslides.

stories.title: Iran officials 'would not be surprised' if Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei dies soon: Report
Who is Sarah Jukaku? Michigan Democrat Abdul El-Sayed has rental properties in India, Dubai in wife's name
Past tense, eye on future: Air India hikes pilots’ pay by 8% to 15%
US judge compares Meta to 'public nuisance,' orders $567m payout over child harm
India’s first satellite-guided chopper approached launched at HAL airport
Exiled Bangladeshi cricket star Shakib Al Hasan willing to return, face murder trial if safety assured
'Why fear eggs in politics?' SC tells Mauha freedom fighter took bullets to chest
stories.summary: A bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu said it was not inclined to interfere with the high court's direction requiring the Krishnanagar MP to join the investigation. Senior advocate Gopal Sankaranarayanan, appearing for Moitra, argued that she should be allowed to appear before the investigating officer virtually as she was entitled to do so under the law.

stories.title: Harvard rejected Paul Devlin in 1981; he wrote back rejecting the rejection letter
stories.summary: In 1981, high school student Paul Devlin responded to Harvard University's rejection letter by rejecting its rejection instead. Inspired by a grammatical error in Harvard's letter, his witty reply was published byThe New York Times. More than four decades later, the letter has resurfaced online and continues to entertain readers.

stories.title: Astrobase unveils 800kN rocket engine, eyes reusability
Toronto gets its own 'Moo Deng'; pygmy hippo calf born to 20-year-old mother, took first steps within minutes of birth
One man began clearing dumped trash alone; his daily cleanups grew into a 100-volunteer movement
stories.summary: A Houston resident's initiative to clean up neglected areas has blossomed into a vibrant volunteer movement. With one hundred dedicated individuals now on board, their mission is to remove illegally dumped waste. Collaborating with local organizations and harnessing the power of social media, city officials and law enforcement are boosting efforts to tackle this pressing issue, ultimately enhancing the community's aesthetics and the well-being of its residents.

stories.title: 'Govt stealing money, destroying lives': Rahul Gandhi vows campaign against E20
Scientists watched a 1km-wide, 100m-thick section of Greenland’s Sorgenfri glacier break away
stories.summary: In a striking display of nature, a massive section of a Greenland glacier detached and collapsed into the sea, captured by scientists on a research vessel. This occurrence unfolded as part of a study examining the implications of meltwater runoff on major ocean currents. Advanced autonomous robots are being utilized to collect vital data from the hazardous ice face.

stories.title: Evening news wrap: CBI chargesheet alleges NTA's own experts leaked NEET-UG, MEA rejects US criticism of of FCRA Bill & more
stories.summary: CBI chargesheeted thirteen accused, including NTA experts, for allegedly leaking NEET-UG 2026 papers. India rejected US criticism of FCRA amendments, stating Parliament will decide the matter. Saudi Arabia, Pakistan, and Turkey signed a mutual defence pact, which India is closely following. Prime Minister Modi advised NDA MPs to avoid Lutyens' Delhi and house anxiety. A meeting between Sukhbir Badal and PM Modi sparked reunion talks for BJP-SAD.

stories.title: H-1B program is not just fraud: Trump official says it's a criminal enterprise; Americans will be very angry when the investigation is over
'Do not endorse anything said': MEA rejects Bangladesh's charge over Hasina's presser
stories.summary: Ministry of external affairs stated no government role in Sheikh Hasina's media event. The ministry does not endorse statements made at the private forum. Bangladesh expressed outrage over the interaction, calling it an affront to its sovereignty. Dhaka urged India to clarify its policy regarding conspiratorial activities. Both nations seek constructive relations based on mutual respect and equality.

stories.title: MacKenzie Scott gave Native Forward $50 mn; organisation reveals how it will spend it
stories.summary: Native Forward Scholars Fund has revealed how it will use the entire $50 million unrestricted donation from philanthropist MacKenzie Scott. The organisation will spend $10 million over the next five years to expand scholarships for Native students, while placing the remaining $40 million into a permanent endowment to provide long-term support. The gift, the largest in the organisation's 57-year history, comes as demand for financial aid continues to rise, with scholars facing an average unmet need of $26,000. Native Forward says the funding will help both current students and future generations pursue higher education.

stories.title: New Jersey police officer disguised as a roadside tree catch 74 distracted drivers
stories.summary: A New Jersey police department used an officer in a ghillie suit resembling a tree. This unusual tactic aimed to raise awareness about distracted driving dangers. Later, plainclothes officers conducted an operation and cited seventy-four drivers. These citations were for using mobile phones while operating vehicles. The campaign sought to reduce preventable crashes caused by inattentive drivers.

stories.title: Archaeologists uncover ancient Roman structure near the Colosseum
stories.summary: In a remarkable discovery, archaeologists have unearthed a second-century building adjacent to the iconic Colosseum in Rome. This newly found structure boasts intricate mosaics and elaborately painted ceilings, hinting at its significant role in ancient society. While it bears resemblance to known firefighters' barracks from that era, some experts speculate it could also have been a luxurious Roman residence. Ongoing research aims to unveil its true historical purpose.

stories.title: New Zealand’s rare woollyhead rises again with 250 new seedlings
Women taking governance to last mile: How Anganwadi workers & ASHA didis are transforming rural India
Divers find 162-year-old Guinness bottle off UK coast, scientists hope to recreate historic beer
'Hands off Jantar Mantar!' CJP says 'won't tolerate' bid to take away protest site after HC poser
Florida’s nuclear plant became an unlikely home for American crocodiles
Scientists discover Titan's methane rainstorms are more intense than expected
stories.summary: On the distant moon Titan, intense methane rainstorms transform the icy terrain, creating striking alluvial fans that showcase the areas most affected by these rare deluges. Scientists leverage data from the Cassini mission to create models of these phenomena, which happen less frequently than once every Titan year—a period nearly equivalent to 30 Earth years. Understanding Titan's unique weather patterns offers insights into extreme rainfall events here on our planet.

stories.title: Martha Hunt’s Tribeca condo listed at $3.75M, nine years after $3.45M buy
Minnesota retiree saved his new rod and landed a 2.21-pound state-record bluegill on day one
stories.summary: On his inaugural fishing adventure, Dale Hoffman snagged a massive bluegill weighing in at 2.21 pounds, breaking Minnesota's state record. This impressive catch happened on Big Stone Lake, renowned for its oversized bluegills, thanks to ongoing habitat enhancements. Notably, Dale used a new spinning rod, a special retirement gift, emphasizing the story behind this extraordinary moment in fishing history.

stories.title: Phil Pister saved the last Owens pupfish from extinction in 1969
stories.summary: Phil Pister devoted his career to the conservation of vulnerable desert fish, making a significant impact in 1969 when he rescued the final Owens pupfish from a drying pond. This pivotal moment sparked vital conservation initiatives aimed at safeguarding other isolated fish species. Pister's mentorship inspired a new generation of scientists, fostering a deeper appreciation for biodiversity.

stories.title: 'Internal matter for us': MEA dismisses US lawmaker's criticism of FCRA Bill
stories.summary: Ministry of external affairs rejected criticism of its foreign funding law. The ministry stated that legislative matters are internal decisions for Parliament. Several countries, including the United States, also regulate foreign financing. A US Congressman criticized proposed amendments to India's Foreign Contribution Regulation Act. He warned these changes could affect India-US bilateral relations.

stories.title: Inside the Guinness record-holding cashew tree that keeps rooting itself
Quote of the day by Galileo Galilei: "Passion is the genesis of genius."
After losing his dog, Ohio man spent 13 years adopting unwanted senior dogs
stories.summary: Inspired by the passing of his dog Wolfgang in 2012, Steve Greig embarked on a heartfelt mission to rescue senior dogs, offering them a nurturing environment for their remaining days. He now looks after a diverse group of elderly animals and showcases their journeys on Instagram, encouraging others to consider adopting older pets. His unwavering dedication has gained him widespread acclaim for transforming the lives of senior canines.

stories.title: Delhi HC grants Dabur interim relief against food regulator's order over '100%' claims
stories.summary: On August ‌3, the ​Food ​Safety and Standards ⁠Authority of India (FSSAI) said products sold ​on Dabur's website ​claimed some of its products were "100% Natural", "100% Pure" and "100% Organic", which were ambiguous, unverifiable ‌and likely to mislead consumers. The Dabur India Thursday approached the high court challenging the FSSAI's directive to the food companies from using claims such as “100% Pure or natural” on product packaging and labels.

stories.title: How did Twitch star LilyPichu end up voicing Overwatch's new hero D.Mon and showcasing her MEKA Squad voice skills?
stories.summary: Renowned streamer LilyPichu has been announced as the voice of D.Mon in the popular game Overwatch. She expressed her enthusiasm about being part of the Blizzard game’s cast. Fans can appreciate her diverse voice acting skills showcased in the 'Growing Pains' comic reading, where she also voiced several other characters, marking another milestone in her thriving voice acting career.

stories.title: Black pine jewel beetles use heat, smoke and infrared organs to find wildfires
Former Nestle CMD Suresh Narayanan says India Inc needs to shed the ‘elite’ tag
stories.summary: Suresh Narayanan shares leadership lessons from his four-decade boardroom. He places trust, authenticity, and purpose as crucial elements, and challenges India's obsession with pedigree. He also reflects on the Maggi crisis and the importance of clear communication in crisis moments.

stories.title: 'News, Spice Rani, He Ram': Names on police merit list triggers row in Chhattisgarh
stories.summary: According to the CGPSC, the candidates had appeared for document verification, physical tests and the preliminary examination under the same names. Former chief minister Bhupesh Baghel mocked the list after sharing it on X. "The Public Relations Department should spend Rs 1 crore daily on s to display this achievement at public intersections so that, in the coming days, 'Radio' and 'Space Raja' might also succeed in some examination."

stories.title: Japanese quote of the day: 'If you are in a rush, take the longer way'
2,400-year-old shipwreck found off Greece carrying hundreds of ancient amphorae
Two Indian-origin men wanted in Canada over $30,000 apartment rental fraud
Ethan Klein’s reported $1M lawsuit against iDubbbz hit a wall over the H3 snark subreddit
stories.summary: Steven Asarch says Ethan Klein’s reported $1 million lawsuit against iDubbbz involved more than damages. According to his breakdown of court documents, Klein wanted a settlement with conditions, including a condemnation of snark communities. But iDubbbz reportedly refused to go far enough on that point, becoming the reason settlement talks stalled. Klein has not commented on Asarch’s report as of this writing.

stories.title: Why was Asmongold banned on Twitch? Here’s what happened after his controversial livestream remarks
stories.summary: Twitch streamer Asmongold faced a ban after controversial livestream comments. He discussed people crossing borders and made violent statements about shooting individuals. Asmongold doubled down on his remarks when questioned by a viewer during the broadcast. These comments quickly spread across social media platforms online. The incident led to Twitch taking action against the popular content creator.

stories.title: Lake cores show 2012 Rwenzori wildfire was first in 12,000 years, with 100-fold charcoal rise
stories.summary: In 2012, a wildfire swept across Africa's Rwenzori Mountains, marking the first such event in over 12,000 years. Analysis of lake sediments uncovered a significant charcoal marker linked to this fire, indicating that human actions and climate change are altering these delicate mountain ecosystems. The lower slopes reveal early human impact and ongoing forest shifts, highlighting the escalating threats to the fragile Afroalpine environments.

stories.title: Monsoon Session: Congress issues whip to MPs ahead of FCRA Bill discussion in Parliament
Sukhbir Singh Badal meets PM Modi, fuels BJP-SAD alliance buzz ahead of Punjab polls next year
'Avoid Lutyens web': PM Modi's advice to 45 NDA MPs at breakfast meet
stories.summary: In the meeting, which also included the rebel factions from the Uddhav Sena and Mamata Banerjee's TMC, PM Modi said: "No one should say anything trashy on TV. Maintain full dignity at all times. Engage actively in social media through Facebook, Instagram and X; interact with youth, inform government welfare work, encourage youth for sports activities." Modi advised the MPs to follow the party line and calmly present their views on every issue.

stories.title: Amazon faces lawsuit over ‘dolphin-safe’ and ‘sustainable’ seafood labeling claims
Italian woman accidentally throws away her $1.1 million winning lottery ticket
stories.summary: An Italian woman mistakenly discarded a winning lottery ticket worth one million euros. Sanitation workers meticulously searched over six tons of rubbish to find it. The ticket was recovered intact after a day-long, coordinated search operation. The woman had misunderstood a message displayed on a lottery terminal. This remarkable recovery ensured she could claim her life-changing jackpot prize.

stories.title: The ‘vampire woman’ whose 17th-century grave is rewriting burial fears in Poland
Uttarakhand CM Dhami approves Rs 1,967 cr for urban infrastructure, GIS-based drainage projects
stories.summary: The Chief Minister has approved the release of Rs 1,960 crore for 15 GIS-based drainage projects to be implemented in various districts of Uttarakhand.

stories.title: Esports Awards 2026 nominees revealed: Jynxzi, Kai Cenat and top gaming names make the list
stories.summary: The Esports Awards 2026 have revealed nominees across nine categories, covering major games, streamers, personalities, creators, teams, partners and esports services. Names including Jynxzi, Faker, Kai Cenat and iShowSpeed feature among the nominees. Voting is already live, with fans able to support their picks until November 10, 2026. Here’s the complete lineup across every category announced for this year’s awards.

stories.title: Scientists studied South Australia cave bones; light left algae marks, darkness preserved bones
stories.summary: In the captivating underwater caves of South Australia, animal bones exhibit unique characteristics brought about by their aquatic environment. The contrast of light and shadow results in algae development while simultaneously preserving bones in an extraordinary manner. Analyzing these distinct changes allows scientists to piece together ancient ecosystems and geological transformations, establishing an innovative framework for fossil interpretation worldwide.

stories.title: Uttarakhand Forward 2.0 | Manoj Pant maps out development roadmap to 2047
stories.summary: As Uttarakhand looks towards 2047, the focus is on reducing distress migration, creating opportunities closer to home and building infrastructure suited to its fragile Himalayan terrain. The long-term vision is to balance economic growth with sustainability while preparing Uttarakhand for the challenges of the decades ahead.

stories.title: Karnataka legislative council chairman Basavaraj Horatti resigns
From Typhoon Dim-sum to frogs and snakes: Asia’s cyclones feature unusual names
‘No one has seen us together’: Rahul Gandhi’s Batman moment in Gen Z session
Esports Awards 2026 Streamer of the Year nominees revealed as IShowSpeed eyes third win
stories.summary: The Esports Awards 2026 have revealed the 12 creators nominated for Streamer of the Year. IShowSpeed, Kai Cenat, Jynxzi, CaseOh and several other major names made the shortlist. Speed has won the award for the last two years, giving the category an extra storyline. Voting is already open, with fans able to support their pick until November 10, 2026, through the official Esports Awards website.

stories.title: How an island suddenly rose from the Mediterranean in 1831 then vanished
stories.summary: In 1831, fishermen spotted a temporary volcanic island off the coast of Sicily, prompting European powers to hastily claim the new territory, leading to several international disputes. Unfortunately, the island, primarily composed of lightweight rocks, eroded rapidly, disappearing into the Mediterranean within months. Today, its remnants lie submerged, creating a unique habitat for marine life and documented on maritime maps.

stories.title: In 2016, Rutgers scientists identified the globe skimmer as the world's longest-flying insect
stories.summary: Globe skimmer dragonflies have been identified as the longest-distance flying insects, showcasing a remarkable ability to traverse thousands of kilometers. Genetic studies indicate that they form a single global population across continents. Their bodies are well-adapted for long journeys, aided by their reliance on freshwater. Researchers are actively investigating their mysterious migration paths and unique population behaviors.

stories.title: Inside Rob Zombie’s $6.5M Origami House with glass walls and waterfalls
New island has emerged in Alaska after a glacier melted away
In 1925, a man 'sold' the Eiffel Tower and vanished with the money
stories.summary: A con artist named Victor Lustig famously 'sold' the Eiffel Tower for scrap in 1925. He convinced scrap metal dealers the monument was being dismantled due to high maintenance costs. Lustig used forged documents and official appearances to execute his elaborate deception. After his initial success, he attempted the same scam again in Paris. His criminal career eventually ended with his arrest and imprisonment in the United States.

stories.title: 'They don’t need a certificate from you': Priyanka hits back at RSS chief Bhagwat’s Gen Z outreach
Any post against PM Modi to be deleted in three hours: Arvind Kejriwal on new social media law
6,000-km-long ant super colony stretching from Portugal to Italy
Govt bars firms filing fake drug data from seeking fresh approvals
A well in Gujarat's Morbi has been shaking continuously with rippling water with experts having no clue why
stories.summary: In Morbi district of Gujarat, a well has been causing an unusual spectacle with its strange water oscillations since early August. Hundreds of inquisitive locals have flocked to Pranjivan Sadariya's fields to witness this rare occurrence. While local officials have dismissed seismic activity as a potential cause, initial investigations point towards groundwater recharge and trapped air as contributing factors.

stories.title: 14-year-old Millie Pradawong uses AI and CRISPR to make microalgae produce more biofuel
stories.summary: Fourteen-year-old Millie Pradawong has developed an AI-powered computational tool that predicts how CRISPR gene editing could improve microalgae for biofuel production. Her project, MACRO, aims to increase oil production without reducing algae growth. A finalist in the 2026 3M Young Scientist Challenge, Millie hopes her work will support future research in clean energy and biotechnology.

stories.title: BJP MLAs storm well, disrupt Jharkhand assembly over exam irregularities
Meet Arya Satheesh: High school student invents plant-based plastic that removes microplastics
Argentina property bill protest: Police fire tear gas, water cannons at protesters
India, China agree to use diplomatic, military channels to avoid LAC misunderstandings: MEA
Vijay vs Udhayanidhi: CM rejects DMK's all-party meet demand on Mekedatu and Cauvery dispute
stories.summary: Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay rejected an all-party meeting on the Mekedatu Dam. He asserted his government would not compromise on Cauvery water rights. The opposition leader demanded the meeting, citing concerns over water release. Vijay stated the state's position was already conveyed to the Prime Minister. He urged the opposition not to politicize the serious water dispute.

stories.title: Scientists release 42 snakes to bring a giant US species back
stories.summary: In Spring 2026, conservationists released 42 eastern indigo snakes into their historical habitats in Florida and Alabama. After a year of specialized care, these reptiles have adapted well, with monitoring indicating successful survival and breeding in the wild. This significant reintroduction effort seeks to restore self-sustaining populations of this unique snake species to their native regions.

stories.title: The 1900 mystery of three lighthouse keepers who vanished
stories.summary: In 1900, three seasoned lighthouse keepers mysteriously disappeared from Eilean Mor. When a supply vessel arrived, they found the lighthouse abandoned with signs indicating a hurried exit. Investigations uncovered no indications of violence or outside interference. The prevailing theory suggests a rogue wave may have taken the men by surprise. This enigmatic maritime case continues to baffle experts over a century later.

stories.title: In 1974, a German fisherman released thousands of baby catfish into a river; 50 years later they are threatening native wildlife
stories.summary: In 1974, German biologist Roland Lorkowsky introduced the Wels catfish to Spain's Ebro River, where they've since become a top predator, threatening native wildlife. Their large size and aggressive feeding present significant hurdles for conservationists trying to maintain balance. Worsening climate change conditions could facilitate their further invasion into European waters, leading experts to deem eradication efforts nearly impossible.

stories.title: 11-year-old boy took Abbot's kneecap in 1956; 70 yrs later, his widow returns it to the museum
stories.summary: A medieval abbot's kneecap and a floor tile have been returned to Glastonbury Abbey more than 70 years after they were taken by an 11-year-old schoolboy during an archaeological dig. The artefacts were kept in Australia for decades before the boy's widow brought them back following his death in 2025.

stories.title: Trump angry over leak of US weapons shortage as Iran talks enter crucial phase: Report
stories.summary: President Trump expresses frustration over media claims regarding the depletion of US weapons stockpiles, fearing the leaks may undermine America's leverage in negotiations with Iran. While he admits some reports accurately reflect a tighter supply of advanced munitions, he aims to pursue severe penalties for those behind the information leaks. Vice President Vance characterizes negotiating with Iran as exceptionally challenging, referring to their people as radical.

stories.title: China's Taklamakan Desert is now capturing more carbon than it emits
stories.summary: China's shelterbelt initiative has made remarkable strides, turning arid desert borders into thriving carbon sinks. Through strategic vegetation choices, this project now captures more carbon dioxide than it expels. This achievement is anchored in mountain meltwater, vital for its irrigation systems. The initiative showcases the powerful impact of ecological restoration given optimal environmental conditions, though future water supply will be critical for sustaining these achievements.

stories.title: 'Power Banks' for satellites? Bengaluru Company builds tech to keep ageing spacecraft alive
Thailand school shooting: Student opens fire; 7 dead
Jharkhand student protest Day 14: Hunger strike continues as BJP, Rahul Gandhi back students
Trump’s Gaza Board moves ahead with first project - military base for Moroccan troops
Italy, France, Germany battle extreme heat as Europe faces record temperatures
Rahul Gandhi flags Ken-Betwa tribal displacement; Centre forwards complaints to MP govt
Government: Global headwinds pressurising finances
Iran President met a 'voice in the dark', isn't sure it was Mojtaba Khamenei: Report
Australian citizenship for 2 Iranian women soccer players who sought asylum
Patient dies in China biotech company’s gene editing trial
Clarify Dhaka policy: Bangladesh to India after Hasina’s presser
‘Need to elect JD’: Trump ‘backs’ VP as president nominee in ‘meet with donors’
Tell Trump to desist or we hit you hard: Iran warns Gulf countries
Senate panel holds Fauci in contempt for not answering Covid questions
Alternative-fuel passenger vehicles fast catching up with petrol ones
stories.summary: In a significant shift, alternative-fuel passenger vehicles have captured forty percent of the retail market, nearly matching petrol-powered models, which hold a slender one percent lead. July marked the highest sales figures for automobiles ever recorded. Additionally, electric two-wheelers are experiencing unprecedented market penetration, highlighting changing consumer preferences towards cost-effective options.

stories.title: Survey: 81% of study-abroad aspirants plan to return home
stories.summary: Nearly all Indian students heading overseas for education plan to come back home after their studies. What's striking is that about 90% are pioneering this journey as the first in their families to study abroad. This trend highlights a shift towards self-driven decisions among students. Business and management fields are particularly appealing, with many utilizing Google searches and agents to find their perfect educational fit.

stories.title: Temporary disability cert no bar for PwBD quota MBBS seat: NMC
stories.summary: Candidates holding temporary disability certificates can now pursue MBBS admissions, reflecting significant changes in the National Medical Commission's policies. The revised guidelines indicate that admission requests from persons with disabilities will be subject to assessment by medical boards. It is noteworthy that the presence of progressive or non-progressive disabilities will not inherently prevent admission, with a thorough evaluation of functional competency taking place.

stories.title: Settling with a few cases won't stop CBI probe: Supreme Court warns realtors
stories.summary: The Supreme Court will continue CBI investigations into defaulting realtors. Builders cannot escape probes by settling with only a few homebuyers. Many bank officials are found to have colluded with these builders. CBI has completed probes in eighteen of fifty registered cases. Banks must grant prosecution sanctions for accused officials within two weeks.

stories.title: Rahul reaches out to Gen Z, backs student stir in Jharkhand
stories.summary: Rahul Gandhi took to Instagram to voice his support for student protests, labeling the education system as deeply flawed and in need of urgent reform. His remarks were made following a meeting with NEET protesters who detailed their encounters with police brutality. The students bravely shared stories of discrimination they faced while advocating for their rights.

stories.title: Prosecutors Outline Grim Allegations: Filings detail alleged planned killing; body reportedly hidden for months
stories.summary: Prosecutors have outlined new allegations in the murder case against singer d4vd, claiming a heated argument with 14-year-old Celeste Rivas Hernandez preceded her death in April 2025. Court filings allege the singer killed and later dismembered the teenager before concealing her remains in his Tesla. d4vd has pleaded not guilty to all charges, and his legal team maintains he neither killed Celeste nor caused her death.

stories.title: Need to seal alliance deal with SP soon for UP polls, MPs tell Congress leadership
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh Congress MPs are actively pushing for a partnership with the Samajwadi Party, considering it vital to mount a formidable challenge to the BJP in the upcoming elections. With a strong consensus among the MPs for quick action, party leaders are currently assessing viable constituencies and gathering data to facilitate negotiations, striving to strengthen their united front against the BJP's dominance in the state.

stories.title: BJP to Congress: Let House function, Amit Shah will come
stories.summary: The BJP has called out Congress leaders Rahul Gandhi and Mallikarjun Kharge for allegedly spreading misinformation. They assert that Home Minister Shah is present at Parliament House, but is unable to participate due to ongoing protests. Continued disruptions by the opposition hinder legislative work, yet Shah is ready to address their concerns directly. The BJP confirmed Shah is in his office daily, awaiting the resumption of parliamentary activities.

stories.title: Rijiju raises point of order, Kharge hits back at minister
stories.summary: The Rajya Sabha approved the Appropriation Bill, 2026, authorizing fund withdrawals for excess expenditure. Opposition members repeatedly demanded Home Minister Amit Shah's presence in the House. Parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju was asked to convey their sentiments to Shah. Leader of the Opposition Mallikarjun Kharge sought the Home Minister's statement on student police action. The opposition also requested the Prime Minister's apology for the alleged police excesses.

stories.title: Land-grab case: Supeme Court grants interim bail to Abhishek's PA
stories.summary: In a significant move, the Supreme Court has granted interim bail for one week to Sumit Roy, who serves as the personal assistant to TMC general secretary Abhishek Banerjee. Roy is implicated in the Salboni land-grabbing case, which followed the arrest of former TMC MLA Sujoy Hazra. Notably, the court has stayed Roy's arrest until it reconvenes for the next hearing.

stories.title: UPI charges: Lok Sabha passes bill for government to make changes
stories.summary: The Lok Sabha has taken a vital step by passing a Bill aimed at simplifying tax rules to enhance investment attractiveness. The new legislation abolishes a limitation on specific electronic payment options, allowing banks and providers to charge merchants on transactions. Additionally, the government is empowered to revise the zero-MDR scheme for UPI and RuPay. This initiative is poised to drive advancements in the financial sector’s infrastructure and innovative capabilities.

stories.title: Amid cyber threats, IT ministry asked to expedite hirings
stories.summary: The finance ministry has sanctioned more posts for CERT-In, yet the hiring remains underway. With rising cyber threats dominating discussions, a parliamentary committee is pressing for expedited recruitment. The IndiaAI Mission's fellowship program initially struggled to attract candidates. In response, MeitY is implementing outreach sessions and promotional campaigns to encourage more applicants. Additionally, final touches are being made to recruitment guidelines for several scientific roles ahead of future job s.

stories.title: 15 Indian seafarers killed in West Asia and Black Sea conflicts: Regulator
stories.summary: Geopolitical conflicts in West Asia and the Black Sea have endangered Indian seafarers. Fifteen Indian seafarers have died and two remain missing in recent months. Drone and missile attacks have become rampant in the Black Sea region. Piracy off Somalia and Houthi threats have also resurfaced significantly. India's maritime regulator is enhancing safety measures and tracking seafarers' well-being.

stories.title: Rahul ignored plan to end my fast, says Sonam Wangchuk
stories.summary: Sonam Wangchuk voiced disappointment with political leaders after his hunger strike concluded. His wife Gitanjali sought Rahul Gandhi's involvement but received no positive response. Union ministers also reportedly broke a promise regarding the release of photos. Wangchuk felt leaders showed a narrow approach and arrived late to his protest. He praised the apolitical CJP organization for its fair and just advocacy.

stories.title: 3 rebel TMC MPs to meet Prime Minister today
stories.summary: A trio of dissenting Trinamool MPs is set to engage with Prime Minister Narendra Modi following their earlier discussions with Union Minister Amit Shah related to pressing concerns. Notably, these lawmakers have distanced themselves from two NDA meetings. Additionally, other NCPI representatives and Shiv Sena MPs are expected to join them for a breakfast meeting with the Prime Minister on Friday morning.

stories.title: Supreme Court happy with progress in talks in Sunjay Kapur case
stories.summary: In an effort to resolve a high-profile family dispute, members are actively engaging in mediation under the supervision of ex-CJI DY Chandrachud, following a Supreme Court directive. So far, six sessions have taken place, where the parties have agreed to continue discussions. They are pursuing a comprehensive settlement related to trust claims, with mediation scheduled to run until November 2.

stories.title: 5.7 lakh people fined Rs 5.1 cr in 2025-26 for smoking in public
stories.summary: In India, over 570,000 individuals were fined for smoking in public spaces, accumulating penalties exceeding Rs 51 million under the COTPA legislation. Karnataka led the charge, issuing the most fines. Interestingly, several states recorded no violations or fines throughout the year. Enforcement primarily lies with state governments, highlighting the varying levels of adherence to the public smoking ban.

stories.title: Weeding out dead wood aim of compulsory retirement, says Supreme Court
stories.summary: The Supreme Court clarified that compulsory retirement is not a punishment for diminished performance, but rather a necessary step to uphold the standards of efficiency and discipline required. The court dismissed a plea from a CISF officer who disputed his removal after his performance had notably dropped from 'Good' to 'Average'. It emphasized the importance of consistent high performance among personnel in disciplined forces.

stories.title: South Africa recalls envoy for attending Zuma meet with businessman Gupta
stories.summary: South Africa's diplomatic relations may be on shaky ground as the country has recalled its ambassador to India. This step follows the emergence of images depicting a meeting between ex-president Jacob Zuma and Ajay Gupta, a businessman facing serious corruption accusations. The Gupta brothers, known for their controversial ties during Zuma's term, along with Zuma himself, have staunchly rejected all charges against them, raising questions about accountability.

stories.title: Can't exclude SC/ST creamy layer from quotas: Government to Supreme Court
stories.summary: The government is against extending the creamy layer to SC and ST reservation benefits, emphasizing that the challenges these communities face are rooted in more than economic issues. Reservation serves to right historical wrongs and ensure equitable access. The Supreme Court has permitted states to categorize castes within SC groups, but only Parliament holds the power to amend the lists of SC and ST populations eligible for these allocations.

stories.title: Netanyahu calls PM Modi, discusses bilateral ties, West Asia situation
stories.summary: In a significant phone discussion, Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu evaluated the progress made in their strategic partnership and bilateral engagements. They also addressed current developments in West Asia, amidst Israel's increasing international scrutiny due to its military actions. This exchange highlights their continued efforts to bolster cooperation and deepen ties between India and Israel.

stories.title: Foreign funding up despite tightening of FCRA rules
stories.summary: Despite the tightening of regulations, foreign contributions to NGOs have surged. Recently, however, there has been a notable decline in the number of registered NGOs, now totaling merely 14,500 compared to several lakh in the past. The government emphasizes that the amendments focus on specific foreign-funded channels, aiming to enhance oversight without hindering the broader civil society framework.

stories.title: Opposition opposes FCRA bill, says minorities being targeted
stories.summary: Rahul Gandhi briefed opposition parties on discussions regarding the delimitation bill. The opposition maintains its stand on women's reservation within the current Lok Sabha strength. Discussions also covered the FCRA bill, with concerns raised about its impact on minorities. Some members noted potential government removal of retrospective effect clauses. Parliamentary functioning remains contingent on government statements regarding protests and donations.

stories.title: Amit Shah assured proposed FCRA changes will not be retrospective, says Mizoram CM
stories.summary: Chief minister Lalduhoma from Mizoram held a pivotal meeting with Home Minister Amit Shah on Thursday, where Shah confirmed that amendments to the FCRA will not have a retroactive effect. Church representatives were also part of the discussion, emphasizing the need for suggestions to safeguard the FCRA. A vital debate on the proposed bill is set for August 12, promising to clarify future legislative actions.

stories.title: Supreme Court dismisses plea challenging Delhi HC relief to Hinduja brothers in Bofors case
stories.summary: The Supreme Court has officially closed the chapter on the Bofors payoff case by dismissing an appeal that challenged the Delhi High Court's 2005 ruling, which had previously annulled criminal proceedings against the Hinduja brothers. Advocate Ajay K Agrawal filed the appeal, but the court decided against allowing more time for arguments, finalizing the legal dispute once and for all.

stories.title: Quote of the day by Mignon McLaughlin: 'The proud man can learn humility, but he will be proud of it' and why some things never change
Quote by Michel Foucault: 'Maybe the target nowadays is not to discover what we are but...'
stories.summary: Michel Foucault posited that identity is sculpted by societal labels rather than an inherent human essence. He asserted that true freedom lies in critically examining and discarding these imposed identities. Today, power operates subtly through institutions dictating people's identities. Furthermore, technology and algorithms play a role in shaping digital personas, echoing Foucault's warnings. Choosing to resist these labels empowers individuals to transcend predefined identities.

stories.title: Quote of the day by JD Vance on 'Limousine socialists': 'They're not promising you industry, they're not promising you good jobs, what they are promising you is...'
Quote by Martha Nussbaum: 'Knowledge is no guarantee of good behavior, but ignorance is...'
stories.summary: Martha Nussbaum emphasizes that possessing technical skills isn't synonymous with ethical conduct. She points out that ignorance, whether intentional or overlooked, can lead to detrimental choices. Today's educational systems may churn out proficient employees but often lack the essential elements of critical thinking and empathy. The humanities, she argues, play a crucial role in fostering understanding and reducing harm by encouraging a variety of viewpoints.

stories.title: Hawaii congressional candidate Kirill Basin allegedly threatened beachgoers in Maui
stories.summary: At Keawakapu Beach, Democratic congressional hopeful Kirill Basin encountered serious legal issues after reportedly threatening individuals with a knife and a gun. A bystander, trained in martial arts, bravely intervened and rendered Basin unconscious during the altercation. Now charged with terroristic threatening, Basin faces a one million dollar bail, further complicated by a troubling history of previous arrests for assault and property damage.

stories.title: Iltija booked for ‘assaulting’ cop; PDP says she was manhandled
stories.summary: An FIR has been filed by J&K Police against Iltija Mufti, accusing her of assaulting an officer amid protests. Charges against her involve public servant assault and rioting, while her mother, Mehbooba Mufti, is also named for failing to adhere to protest regulations. The PDP refutes these claims, asserting police brutality led to Iltija's injuries and criticizing the questioning of an individual in medical care.

stories.title: 'USCIS makes mistakes': Immigration expert breaks down new H-1B, Green Card rule, calls its another step in dismantling legal immigration
Landmine blast injures Army duo in Poonch’s Mendhar, 2 rusty shells destroyed in Mankote sector
stories.summary: In the Mendhar sector, two personnel from the Army Bomb Disposal Squad sustained injuries while trying to defuse a dangerous landmine. A nearby team later located and safely destroyed rusty mortar shells in the Mankote sector. The initial discovery of the landmine was made by an Army patrol, which promptly notified the bomb disposal unit.

stories.title: Quote of the day by Michael Fassbender: "I've always been more inclined to go out to work than…"
Andy Burnham 'personally intervenes' as UK reviews early release of grooming gang offenders
'12 years in the US, leaving with empty hands': Indian woman says her H-1B was revoked because employer didn't run payroll
'He deserves to be remembered': British man who wrongly spent 11 years in jail raises funds to restore murder victim’s grave
Chicago homeowner sues US govt over alleged warrantless immigration raid that damaged property
stories.summary: A Chicago homeowner has sued the US government, alleging Customs and Border Protection officers entered his property without a warrant during an immigration operation in 2025. The lawsuit claims officers damaged his home, ignored requests to leave and violated his constitutional rights. The Department of Homeland Security says its officers acted within legal authority.

stories.title: Saudi Prince's $450 million superyacht hides a secret cabin deep inside the hull, designed to...
stories.summary: The superyacht Serene, owned by Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman Al Saud, features a unique hidden sea cabin. Strategically positioned for stability, this Balinese-inspired retreat offers serenity during turbulent waters. Additionally, the yacht showcases an extraordinary custom snow room, perfect for cooling off from the intense Middle Eastern heat, merging ingenious engineering with unrivaled luxury for ultimate comfort at sea.

stories.title: 'Islamification of the country has to stop': McKinney council meeting extends for 5 hours over debate on mosque project, plan gets nod after massive fight
Europe’s forests losing biomass fast; carbon sink weakened by drought, beetles
Canada deported 3,323 Indians in first half of 2026: Report
UK officials issued a legal warning after protected seahorses were disturbed; divers should...
stories.summary: UK marine authorities are sounding an alarm for water users and film crews alike, as the rise in coastal tourism increases the chances of encountering protected seahorses. Disturbing these delicate creatures without the necessary permits can lead to legal repercussions. It’s advised to maintain a respectful distance and refrain from touching seahorses, while reporting any sightings contributes significantly to conservation efforts for these vulnerable populations.

stories.title: Study discovers that primates take care of animals outside their own family
Indian-origin landlord sued in Pennsylvania for harassing tenant: Only wore khaki pants, showed photo of naked man and woman
Vance over Rubio for 2028? What Trump reportedly told donors at private meeting
Los Angeles singer taught her rescue horse to play the guitar and harp
stories.summary: In a fascinating blend of music and animal companionship, a California singer-songwriter is working on a groundbreaking album alongside her rescue horse, Yupia. Using his nose and teeth, Yupia has mastered playing the guitar and harp, creating a partnership that has captivated millions online. The album promises a heartwarming fusion of Yupia's unique sounds and Khramov's vocal artistry, showcasing the profound trust and bond formed between humans and animals.

stories.title: Meet Bartlomiej Kubkowski: The first man to swim 100 miles across the Baltic Sea from Sweden to Poland
stories.summary: In a remarkable display of endurance, Bartlomiej Kubkowski swam an astonishing 160 kilometers continuously across the Baltic Sea, achieving this incredible milestone in 55 hours and 10 minutes. After four previous attempts without success, his persistence finally bore fruit, helping to raise nearly $190,000 for children battling cancer. This achievement signifies a noteworthy moment in the annals of marathon swimming history.
